# Changelog

All notable changes to Tessellate (formerly MemoryMap AI) are recorded here. The format is loosely
based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and the
project follows a "waves and phases" development history (see the milestones
below). Versioning is `0.x` while the app stabilises.

## [Unreleased]
- A summary request ("recap", "summarise") no longer reads in polynomial time on a long run of spaces or tabs (CodeQL alert 1862). The trailing marks are cut after the match instead of by a lazy span before `\W*$`, and a request over 200 characters is not read as one (the question reader refused those already); 40,000 characters now take under a millisecond, about 2.3 s before (`ai/activity.py`, tests in `tests/test_composer_leftovers_1029c.py`).
- The note picker's preview and a board's note card no longer ask the web for a picture at another address (review of the audit 1029 round, row 45 follow-up). `notePickThumb` took any https address and the board card took the Library's `thumb_url`, which the route returns as written; the page refuses both, so each logged a CSP error. Both use `isRemoteImage` now and fall through to an attachment or no picture: the preview of a remote-picture note returns no `<img>` (was one with the https address), a same-address picture still draws (`note-pick-preview.js`, `whiteboard.js`, test `tests/test_remote_image_note_1029.py`).
- Settings no longer draws Help's 191 topics every time it opens (audit 1029 row 38, X15 and H12, part). They were about 2,040 nodes built into a pane nobody was looking at, and the page kept them after Settings closed. They are drawn when Help is shown or when Settings is first searched (the topics are findable settings: a search for "undo" still lists the same 8 results). Measured on 300 notes: the Settings window 5,293 to 3,249 nodes (the page after one open 15,708 to 13,660); opening Settings at 4x CPU, three runs each, 1,579 / 1,786 / 1,688 ms of main-thread task time to 1,204 / 1,266 / 1,371, script 205 to 143 ms and style recalculation 287 to 203 ms (means). The space menu (22 to 32 ms, 70 to 81 at 4x, no more than the idle page) and the dashboard's own 848 nodes were not slow here, so nothing was changed there: the rest of the page's 13,000 nodes is the markup of the other tabs, and the board bundle is loaded at boot by the note editor, so a template for it would not have saved any (`settings.js`, test `tests/test_settings_help_lazy_1029.py`).
- A 2,000-note graph comes to rest sooner and draws less while it moves (audit 1029 row 35, partly fixed). Cold open on 2,000 notes and 3,796 links, machine load 4 to 7: 27.9 to 29.7 s to rest before, 16.0 to 21.6 s after; click round trip p50 57 to 80 ms before, 42 to 48 ms after; 500 notes 8.5 to 10.4 s before, 6.2 to 9.2 s after. The line-clearance force scans each chord's corridor, not its box (289,939 nearest-point checks a tick to 18,202, same pushes; 11.0 to 7.5 s of worker time); a category-turn call that took 7.2 s now keeps to its 0.6 s pass budget; the worker yields 8 ms after a costly tick instead of as long as the tick (a drag and performance mode keep the duty cycle); a map whose draw costs over 8 ms is drawn once a tick, not glided (472 full draws for 141 ticks to about one a tick), and names skip the line grid while it moves. Still open: per-tick draws of 140 to 230 ms and click maxima of 240 to 310 ms under load (`tests/test_graph_clearance_corridor_1029.py`, `tests/test_graph_tick_rate_1029.py`).
- Data coming back is never rewritten by the new input rules (review of the audit 1029 round). A legacy tag holding a comma ("work, home") was split into two by any background write (the janitor, a tag suggestion, undo) and by restore and import; only what a person types is split now. Undo of a deleted blank reminder and of a space whose name held an invisible character brings them back as they were. A note-to-self ("Remember to call mum", "Try to sleep earlier") reads as a task in a digest again, not as "you remember to call mum". The composer imports without the database layer again (0.69 s to 0.11 s).
- The lead note is the one the subject names, not the one a doing word matches (composer leftovers, audit 1029 row 54 follow-up). "What should I buy for my sister" answered "Buy a capo, from your Guitar note" because "buy" is in the Guitar checklist. A note must now hold a word that names something when the question has one, and the doing words ("buy", "get", "spend") count with the rest (`composer_digest._members`); a question of doing words alone reads as before. `tests/test_composer_leftovers_1029c.py`.
- "Summarise my week" is the week's recap (composer leftovers, audit 1029 row 54 follow-up). It was read as a note to summarise and answered with one note's short version. A request to summarise, recap or sum up a bare period (week, month, year, today, yesterday, with "my", "this" or "last") is now asked as "what did I do ..." (`activity.as_recap`), in Ask and in Chat, and the study reader leaves it alone (`chat_extra.events`). A summary of a subject is unchanged. `tests/test_composer_leftovers_1029c.py`.
- A note that is only a checklist is shown as the checklist when it is asked for by name (composer leftovers, audit 1029 row 54 follow-up). "What is the checklist note" and "what is in my gear list" answered "One, from your Checklist note. Also: two; three." The digest now writes how many are ticked and every item with its box (`composer_digest._show_checklist`), and the composer's ranker counts "list" and "checklist" a quarter beside a word that names the note, so a note that only says "list" no longer leads (`composer._term_weights`). `tests/test_composer_leftovers_1029c.py`.
- A properties block with CRLF line ends is a block (composer leftovers, audit 1029 row 54 follow-up). The fence rule in `entry/properties.block_end` and the reader in `core/docmeta` both stopped at the carriage return, so a note saved with Windows line ends had no properties and was named "---"; the fence rule now takes a CR, and a blank line after the closing fence no longer leaves the note without a name (`composer.read_note`). `tests/test_composer_leftovers_1029c.py`.
- A greeting's invitation never takes a function word as the topic (composer leftovers, audit 1029 row 54 follow-up). A note titled "Note 3 about cats" made the hello end "The last thing you wrote touched on about." The class: a word offered as what something is about was filtered against the search stop words, which keep "about" so search still matches it. `query.is_topic_word` (stop words plus `FUNCTION_WORDS`) now gates both topic pickers, the hello's `_newest_word` and the chat's `_chat_topic`. `tests/test_composer_leftovers_1029c.py`.
- A plain drag of a note only moves it (audit 1029 G15, G14, rank 43). Dropping one note on another opened "How are these connected?" on every drag that ended over a neighbour (measured on 36 notes: a plain drag lit the target and opened the dialog). Linking by drop now needs Alt held when the drag starts (Shift still pins); the graph Help panel, the Guide topic and the site say so. G14 (the first selection refitting the camera) did not reproduce: the selection dock is already a menu for the refit, measured 0 px of camera motion and no refit call at three window sizes, and a test now pins that.
- Heading order in Settings, Models, and the chat title (audit 1029 H13, rank 62). The Installed models list is an `h3` whose cards named themselves with `h5`, a skipped level; an installed card is now `h4` (a suggested card stays `h5` under its group's `h4`). The chat's title was `<h2 role="button">`, a role axe does not allow on a heading; it is a focusable heading again and Enter or Space still rename the chat.
- Copy names the real place and cause (audit 1029 X16, H11, G18, G17, rank 52). The first steps said the name is changed in "Settings, General"; it is Settings, Profile, which the button opens. A tool turned off in Settings, Tools it can use was refused on Confirm with "the note or item may have changed"; it now answers 409 "That tool is turned off in Settings, Tools it can use.", for a single call and for a batch undo. The graph's hover hint said "Click to open" for a card that shows details; it says "Click for details, double-click to pin". The topic chip in the graph card is no longer styled as a tag. A test reads the Settings nav labels off the page and checks the first steps and every Guide topic path against them.
- Accessible names start with what is drawn (audit 1029 N10, X22, rank 47). axe's label-content-name-mismatch named the timeline's day buttons ("Fri" and "23" ran together), the Manage categories and tags rows (name and count), the Reminders tab and the phone More button with a badge, the Tidy button past 99, the Statistics range select (its opener took the label's options as its name) and the welcome's Skip button (a tooltip as its label). A trailing or leading space in a flex item is read but not drawn, so each is told apart for free; Tidy says "99+" when it draws it; the select's name is the label's own words; Skip is named by its word. Axe on the timeline, notes, reminders and statistics: 7 findings in the timeline and 22 on the two overlays to 0.
- Targets reach the floor (audit 1029 N11, X8, G13, G20, X22, rank 46). A link pill's menu button was 21 by 21 with a mouse, its chip clipped to 19 high, "Show more" 14 high, every search well's input 20 high, the movable-dialog grip 16 by 16 and the space menu's rows 20 high. One `::after` overhang now serves chips, "Show more" and the card menus; a connection chip is clipped across only; the input stretches to its well; the grip and the space rows take `--target-min`; wrapped pills keep a finger's room apart; the graph's hit slop is 20px under a coarse pointer (a 44px target on the smallest dot) and its legend is one Tab stop with arrow keys. Measured by `elementFromPoint` probes at 390 (touch) and 1440, and axe target-size: 0 on the dialogs.
- Focus and feedback after a cancel or a failure (audit 1029 N14, N22, N19, G19, X21, X23, rank 56). Esc in link mode takes the instruction notice down with it. A `[[link]]` to a note that does not exist has a Create chip in the card. The `[[` picker inserts the whole title, up to 120 characters, not 60. Esc from the map's popup leaves the keyboard on the map. The OCR workspace opens with focus inside it and says in words why Read is off. A wrong password in the unlock prompt and every failed field of the recovery card is marked invalid, linked to its message and focused; Esc in the space menu returns to its button. The dashboard rows and the Library cards no longer request a note's first remote picture.
- A toast is no longer faded over the sketch (audit 1029 X9 and X10, rank 50). Focus sits on the drawing area, which covers the window, so every toast there was drawn at opacity 0.12 and let clicks through to the canvas; a focus target over half the window in both directions no longer makes a toast step aside. The panel reset (the head button, a double-click on the head, Home on the grip) already existed; the button's tooltip now names the double-click.
- A picture at another address in a note is never requested (audit 1029 N7, rank 45). It read "tracker deleted" with a Dismiss control and logged four CSP errors per render: the page's `img-src 'self' data: blob:` refuses it, so the picture was not deleted, only blocked. `isRemoteImage` now decides before either `<img>` branch, so the browser is never asked, and the card shows "Remote image not loaded. Open link" (a link that opens the address in a new tab; the tooltip says the notebook works offline). CSP errors over three renders of the seeded note: 4 per render before, 0 after. The box's class is `entry-image-note` for both states (a gone file keeps its closable "deleted"). Test: `tests/test_remote_image_note_1029.py`.
- A note's card draws a table and a code block the way a document does (audit 1029 N8, rank 44). The card showed `| a | b |` rows and the fence's backticks as text, where a document, Chat and the Read view draw them. One rule, recorded in the row: a card renders the same safe markdown subset as everywhere else, so `mdBlockEnd` (markdown.js) finds a fence or a pipe table and `renderNoteText` hands it whole to `renderMarkdown`, with its Copy button; search terms are not marked inside those two blocks, and the card's heading-hash and list-dash tidying now runs on the prose only, so a fence keeps its own `#` and `-`. `pickMediaDialog` moved to the lazy library-pick.js to pay for it in the gzip budget. Test: `tests/test_note_card_blocks_1029.py`.
- The service worker's cache is named `tessellate-assets-<version>` (audit 1029 X28, rank 63). The legacy `memorymap-assets-*` caches, like the older `memorymap-shell-*` ones, are deleted when the new worker activates, whatever their version, so a browser that installed the old name does not keep a stale set; other sites' caches are left alone. Test: `tests/test_pwa_shell.py` (the activate test now holds both old names and both versions).
- The "search by meaning" notice no longer ends a sentence twice (audit 1029 X18, rank 61). The bell's detail and the Settings line were built as `${error}. Settings, Models ...`, so an error that ended in a period read "..". One `withoutEndStop` takes the closing full stops off an error before our own sentence is joined to it; a question mark or an ellipsis character stays. Test: `tests/test_notification_detail_period_1029.py`, run in node on the real functions.
- Statistics says what it leaves out, and About health counts the whole database (audit 1029 X13, X17, rank 51). The notebook figures read 7 of 8 notes because the words, tags, links and growth skip private notes (a figure that moves when a note is made private would leak it) and archived ones; `GET /statistics` now returns `notebook.left_out` and the page shows one line under the tiles, "Words, tags, links and growth leave out 1 private note and 1 archived note.", only when something is left out. `GET /debug/health` sums the database file with its write-ahead log and shared-memory file (`db.size_bytes`, with `main_bytes` and `wal_bytes` beside it), where the main file alone read 4 KB beside a 2.9 MB log. Tests: `tests/test_statistics_left_out_1029.py`.
- One normaliser per thing, at the model (audit 1029 N6, N15, X6, C29, rank 10). `entry/cleantext.py` holds what blank and "the same name" mean: a note or a reminder of only spaces, line breaks and zero-width characters is refused (422, "That note is blank. Write something first."); a comma splits a tag ("work, home" is two tags, full-width commas too), a tag rename to a name with a comma is refused with the reason, and removing a tag still finds a stored one that holds a comma; space names drop invisible characters, fold runs of spacing to one space, and are compared without case, spacing or zero-width characters, so "Work" with a zero-width character in it is the existing "Work" (409), and a name of only invisible characters is refused ("All" stays a usable name; its id is deduped, tests/test_spaces.py). Reminder times that are not dates ("31 February", "next tuesday") were already refused by the create and update models; the snooze step the composer runs now answers an error sentence for one instead of failing. Nothing stored is rewritten. Tests: `tests/test_input_normalise_1029.py`.
- Request caps finished (audit 1029 H10, X26, N18, G27, rank 9). The history, media-name, attachment-name, graph-pin and unknown-graph-id caps were already in; what was left is bounded now: the chat persona and mode names, skill inputs, the confirmed-tool body (name, arguments, batch steps), the edited text of an attached file and the generated-file save body each have a limit at the model (a 422 before any work), and `tests/test_input_bounds_1029.py` carries a lint that fails when a text, list or dict field on a request body in the chat, files or graph routes has no bound.
- A note's popup on the Graph follows its dragged node in y as well as x (audit 1029 G25, rank 58): a long note took the map's whole height less 16, so at 1280x640 the node moved 280px and the popup 0; an undragged popup is now held to 60% of the room (never under 280px, its body scrolls and its dock stays pinned), and tracks the node down to the map's edge (78px of travel where it had 0, always beside the node). A popup the head has moved keeps the whole room.
- Graph furniture (audit 1029 G9, G22, G23, G24, rank 57): the legend wraps to two rows and scrolls past them instead of hiding five of seventeen entries off to the side (scrollWidth 2088 in 1308 at 1440, now 1308 in 1308); the Filter fold no longer shows a lone "No kind 64" chip when no link has a kind (it says so in a line, and keeps the chip if that kind was turned off); the map's Help is a lead line and seven short items (1,296 characters scrolling 568 in 510, now 780 characters that fit); and the minimap's top corners drop below Trace and its result while they are open (8,861 px² of overlap, now 0). The slow-reload progress line (G30) is left.
- Light theme: a graph dot's rim is half a shade deeper on a light ground (it was a quarter), so the palest automatic colours clear 3:1 against the map (worst of the 22 went from 1.87 to 3.46 sampled off the painted dot), and every placeholder takes the muted colour whole (the graph search's was 3.68:1, now 4.86:1) (audit 1029 G12, G21, rank 48). The toast action measured 7.72:1 on its opaque toast; the 1.2 axe reading came from a toast behind another card, not from its colour.
- The Graph search says how many notes match ("12 matches", "No matches") in a polite live region beside the box, Enter goes to the next match and pans to it, Shift+Enter to the one before (both wrap), and Esc clears the search and the similar-notes highlight (audit 1029 G11, rank 42). The matched note is ringed and named while the rest stay dimmed; the Guide's Graph topic says the keys.
- Summaries and the digest read a note without its settings (audit 1029 C35, X19, rank 55): a note that opens with a properties block (`---`, `tags: [meeting]`) is read from after the block, so its title, summary and digest quote never carry the fence or the tags (`properties.block_end` in `composer.read_note`, `properties.strip` in `study.title_of` and `study.sections`); a summary never repeats the note's title or a section's title and drops a bare label ("Actions:") left where its text was cut; label lines end with a stop so "Attendees: Sara, Tom, Priya" is not glued to "Decisions: ..."; and a note that is only a list is summarised by its items and counts ("is a checklist of 3 items, none ticked: ...", `study.list_gist`) instead of "too little in it". Tests: `tests/test_composer_summaries_1029b.py`. The extract preview's Save (`commitExtractPreview`) moved to the lazy gesture-kit.js to win back the gzip budget rows 49 and 53 went over.
- Frame grammar is mended at the source (audit 1029 C6, C7, C11, C12, C13, C14, rank 54): a checklist with nothing ticked reads "none of its three" (never "no of three"); a gap is said with its hedge once (`_bare_gap` for "every", so no "about one every about three months" and no "about it about a month ago"); a day list that is cut says "And four more." and leaves boards and mind maps out of the count of notes, and a busy day's line in the activity recap counts what it drops; a question that is only a day ("what did I write today") answers with the newest note ("Your newest note is from yesterday.") and no "other items that mention it"; one `realise.mend_stops` removes the stop after a question or exclamation ("theme?.", "next?, from your note"); a need ("need to cut eating out") is said as one, not as what was "written down"; and a greeting is answered in the part of the day it named ("good afternoon" is never "good morning", and "good morning" at night is not "good night"). Tests: `tests/test_composer_grammar_1029b.py`.
- Offers, kinds and clips are one rule each (audit 1029 C4, C5, C9, C10, rank 53): an offer is taken only from a note the answer cites ("Remind you to buy a capo?" no longer follows an answer about a sister); a review names what the notes say it is (a book is "your only book review" and "a list of books to read next", never a film, and a review that names nothing says "note"); every name, label and title is cut by one `realise.cut_title` at a word, with an ellipsis, never ending on "the" or "of" (note names, activity titles, the chat list and the citation mark's label); and a time phrase carries its own preposition from one reader, `recognise.adverbial` ("on 20 October", "in October", "from 15 to 20 October", "in the last 7 days"), with a leading "Tomorrow" lowered inside a frame. Tests: `tests/test_composer_offers_1029b.py`.
- Citation numbers run in the order the answer first cites its notes, in Ask and in Chat, with a model on or off (audit 1029 C49, rank 49): the numbers read 1, 2, 3 down the answer instead of 3, 2, 1, 1, 4, 5, so a screen reader no longer hears 3 before 1. The Sources panel is renumbered the same way: `chatSourcesFrom` puts the cited notes first in first-mention order (a web page or a file keeps its place, uncited notes follow), and every surface that marks or lists sources (Chat live and final, Ask live and answer object, a reopened chat and Ask turn, the popup agent) passes the same grounded sentences. The live list is rebuilt on every sentence, so a digit shown mid-answer is the one it keeps. Tests: `tests/test_citation_order_1029.py`.
- Typing in the Graph search no longer repaints the whole map on every key (audit 1029 G10, rank 39). The matches are found once per change into a set (each node keeps its lowercase name, the label index) instead of lowercasing every preview several times a note per frame; the canvas draws a search over the dimmed scene layer the hover already uses, so only the matches are painted per key; the dimmed layer is painted in an idle moment when the box is focused; and the 150 ms pause in front of the first letters is gone (only the phrase filter's server read keeps one). Measured on a seeded 2,000-note notebook, 13 characters, a key every 250 ms: at 1x 19 long tasks, 1.9 s, longest 159 ms before, 3 tasks, 0.36 s after (the longest, 179 ms, is the one-off layer paint on focus) with a key's own frame 3 to 45 ms; at 4x CPU 24 long tasks, 7.3 s, longest 567 ms before, 28 tasks, 2.6 s after (one 564 ms on focus, most keys 50 to 70 ms). The matching was never the cost (0.6 ms for 2,000 notes): the canvas commit of a whole repaint was, 80 ms a key at 1x.
- Sixteen long functions split into named steps (own activity, typed commands, composer plan, slots, study, missing words, intent, note recency, chat prepare, the search route, engine filter, retrieve, note references), none over complexity 15 now; behaviour unchanged.
- "What is new", "what changed", "what have I added lately", "what did I edit this week", "my longest streak" and "how many days in a row" are answered from the notebook's own counts, in Ask and in Chat, with a model on or off (audit 1029 C32, rank 31): the notes made and edited in the window you name (else the last seven days), and the longest run of consecutive days with a note beside the run you are on now. A word that is not part of such a question is a subject ("what changed in the harbor plan"), which stays a search; dates are said only when the question asks about time.
- The Library puts a section's scroll offset back after reading every section (INBOX 1446, the same read-after-write class as the timeline calendar): a `scrollTop` written between two reads made the next read recalculate again. The lag lint now counts a `scrollTop` write. A never-called `deleteCategory` left over from the sidebar menu is gone.
- Jumping to a note (a search result, a link, the graph, the palette) fits the new count chips once instead of once per card (INBOX 1446, the owner's lag log: `capture-ask.js LI.onclick` 153ms). Each chip was inserted and its line then fitted, which reads widths and lays the list out again: 64 to 210 forced layouts across six jumps at 4x CPU, now 8 to 16 (one per count batch). The first layout of the new list is still paid, so the saving in milliseconds is within run-to-run noise here.
- A tab pressed with the pointer hands the reading keys to its page again (INBOX 1446, the owner's lag log: the tab click at 216ms). `switchTab` awaits before it reveals the page, so the lookup inside the click found the page still hidden and never moved the focus (measured: the focus stayed on the tab button on every tab); it now runs two frames on, on a clean layout, and tests a box's size before its style. The forced layout in the click itself is the arriving page's own first layout, which any reader would pay.
- The Timeline tab no longer lays the page out for its year and month labels (INBOX 1446, the owner's lag log: `timelineTicks` 248ms of forced layout): the strip's height comes from its resize observer, which hands it over after the browser's own layout, instead of a `clientHeight` read in the same task as the draw. Four visits to the tab: 513ms of forced layout at that line before (29 layouts, 4x CPU), 0 after.
- The reminder chime's audio context is no longer built after the first key or click of every session (INBOX 1446, the owner's lag log: `status.js build 557ms` and a 536ms keydown on the lock screen, the audio device opening on the main thread). It is built when a reminder is due within five minutes, or when a chime is wanted and there is none (the chime plays once it exists). A session with no reminder near builds none: 1 context at the first keystroke before, 0 after.
- The companion no longer flushes style once per part it eases (INBOX 1446, the owner's lag log): `nameMarkBuddyBlend` read a part, eased it, then read the next, so each `animate` made the next read re-style; it reads every part first and eases them after, in the same order. A lint (`tests/test_lag_layout_reads.py`) names the loops that measure after writing.
- The Timeline calendar draws without a layout per cell (INBOX 1446, the owner's lag log): the fit of chips to cells measured one cell at a time and the scroll and fade read a second and third layout; one measure now serves all three. A month of 900 notes at 4x CPU: frame 954 to 1177ms (forced layout 822 to 951ms) down to 261 to 454ms (106 to 250ms).
- The Appearance panel has its own Help entry under Look and feel, and its current section reads in the accent text colour; "tell me about golf" answers with what you confirmed about golf, not as a person.
- Quick sketch swatches (INBOX 1447): removing a recent colour offers Undo, a plus beside the picker saves the current colour as a swatch again, and the remove x is a small control beside the swatch (16 px, nothing over the disc; the 24 px target floor met by spacing); the picker's icon is an eyedropper.
- Find anything and the palette rank the row that opens a feature above a Guide topic about it, for every feature (INBOX 1449): Help-pane rows are a "Guide" group listed after the rows that name the thing; "ocr workspace" had the Guide topic first.
- Movable panels move the whole panel (INBOX 1448): the OCR workspace's head sat in a wrapper, so a drag moved the head bar alone; the moved box is now the dialog or its direct-child card for every panel.
- Mind map left-drag pan (INBOX 1445): a left-button drag on empty map canvas pans, Shift-drag draws the selection box, a drag from a topic still moves it; boards keep the box select.
- Dates and names, after 1441 (CI regressions from it): a dropped date takes its whole clause in every phrase and voice ("You use HCI in two notes.", never "..., the last."); a one-line sentence ("Intro to Cloud Computing starts Monday.") is quoted, not worn as a title; a note's own label names it again ("your trip planning note", "your gym note") while "Pros:" and "Attendees:" never do; "do I like golf?" hears the notes' age (gold 9 back to 81, floor 80); the time-word reader moves into `ai/recognise.py`; the digest's `_fragment`, `_clause`, `_section_line` and `_gist_tail` split under complexity 15.
- Dates in answers (INBOX 1441, the owner: "I dont like how it refers to dates"): a date is said only when the question is about time (`composer.asks_time`); otherwise the sentence carries the fact and the record card the date. No "On 4 September, you saved", no "your note of 27 July" (a note is named by its title, or "written on 31 August" when time was asked), no "A week on, by 3 August", no span in the count opener ("You have six notes about hobbies."), no "- 17 July:" bullets in the topic overview, and the staleness footer only for a question about now. Three notebooks, ten phrasings, Ask and Chat: 18 of 24 checks failed before, 0 after (`tests/test_composer_dates_1441.py`).
- Sentence frames (audit 1029 C1, C2, C3, C8, C38, C39, rank 22): one naming and fragment rule in `ai/composer_digest.py`. A name or a title keeps its capital ("Project Atlas", "The Overstory", "Sara, Tom and Priya"), a title is named and never spoken ("you started your Atlas retro meeting note", "your Sourdough starter note says ..."), "you still need to", "Remind you to" and "you planned to" go only before an item that starts with a verb (a list of things reads "your Lisbon packing list note still has passport, charger and walking shoes"), a section of one note is that note's part ("Your Project Atlas kickoff meeting note has attendees: ...", "It also has decisions: ...") and never "your attendees note", a title-less note is named by its clipped first clause ("the note that starts “Idea: a bike route along the river…”"), `[[Reading list]]` is said as its title, and no reporting verb the note did not make ("you heard that"). Three notebooks, 22 phrasings, Ask and Chat: 30 of 42 class checks failed before, 0 after (`tests/test_composer_frames_1029.py`).
- Connections column and its forgotten notes name a note in plain words (INBOX 1442): "**Gym Routine Overview**" showed its stars; both now use the chip label.
- The Connections column is resizable (INBOX 1443): drag its left edge, or focus the edge and press the arrow keys (16px) and Home to reset; 240 to 560px, kept on this device, on a fine pointer at 600px or wider, the list beside it reflowing.
- Update bar instead of the update dialog (INBOX 1440): a found version shows a closable bar under the top bar, once per version, with an Update button that is the only thing that installs (`/update/apply` no longer needs the install switch; elsewhere the button opens the release page); Settings, About has Show the update bar (on by default), and the old install switch is now Pull the latest code when start.sh or start.bat runs, which saying yes to checking no longer turns on.
- Update dialogs (audit 1029 X12): the apply poll gives up after ten missed answers instead of spinning, Escape or the backdrop on any confirm answers "decide later" (the update choice is then not stored), and the copy names Tessellate.
- Bidi control characters (U+202E and kin) are dropped from note titles and previews, so a label reads as the note does (audit 1029 N20).
- One date-window reader (audit 1029 C24 to C28, C30, rank 21): `composer_plan.window` reads a question into one window for every date shape. A day gone is a lookback ("what is on 14 August", "what was I doing on 2 August" go to the activity recap, no wrong-year weekday), "the next two weeks" or "next 2 months" are unit windows, "before December" or "by 15 November" end on the day, "what is overdue" lists the overdue reminders alone (or says nothing is), and the day plan counts and shows every open item, including ones dated outside the day.
- Subject extraction (audit 1029 C15, C16, C17, C18, C37 in part, rank 20): the verb a command opens with (read, draft, move, merge, split, compare, rename ...) and its filler (me, the, two, "to the bin", "a message to") come off the subject before it is chosen, so "draft a message to Sara" is Sara; the study note lookup matches whole stems, so Tom never matches tomatoes; "tell me about Tom" and "what do I know about Tom" take the "who is Tom" shape for a name; "define X" and "the meaning of X" read as "what is X"; the "none of these notes mention" footer skips instruction words (main, two, sentences, tags, related ...). `atlas` and `canvas` are no longer cut to `atla`. Tests: `tests/test_composer_subject_1029.py`, linearity in `tests/test_composer_regex_linear_1029.py`.
- Windowed Notes list (audit 1029 rank 37, N9): every note is a hidden row holding its height and only the rows near the window are built, in runs of six, emptied past thirty rows once the scroll settles. 300 notes at 4x CPU, scrolled to the end: 2,074 list elements against 12,126 (page 13,515 against 24,363), downward scroll p50 frame 17 ms against 67 to 83 ms, and opening the oldest long note from the end of the list 1.2 to 1.4 s with the editor on screen, where HEAD had not opened it after 8 s. Home, End and the arrows build the row they move to; Shift-click range select runs over ids, so unbuilt rows in the range are selected; a long jump to a note is instant then re-centred (the phone landed off screen before, on HEAD too). The rail spy observes only changed rows. `renderIncrementally` moved to library.js (its one caller), and the row chevron and the bell's untagged and review nudges to the lazy notes-lazy.js, so the boot scripts stay under their gzip ratchet.
- One note count (INBOX 1439; audit 1029 rank 7, N13): `manager.count_notes` holds the one definition, every entry not in the bin, archived and private included, boards, drafts and blank entries not, and `/entries/count`, the list total, `/diagnostics`, `/statistics`, `/categories` and `/graph` all build on it, so they no longer say 282, 279 and 277 in the same minute; the Statistics page now counts a private note (its words stay unread).
- Slot-first answers (audit 1029 C22, C23, C33, C36 in part, rank 19): `ai/composer_slots.py` answers "did I pay X" from the ticked or unticked task (yes, not yet, or that no note says so), "what is left on the Lisbon packing list" from the open items of the list the question names (a list nobody made is said, not replaced by another), "how long since I called mum" from a dated line that says it (an open to-do does not count), and "compare the two lentil soup notes" with both sides or which is missing; "how long until the dentist" uses the note titled Dentist, not a to-do that names it. Value slots, how often and kind questions remain, see `composer-ranker-1029.md`.
- One ranker for Ask and Chat (audit 1029 C19, C20, C31, rank 18): `ai/note_rank.py` orders notes exact title, then a note that defines the subject, then a title that holds it, then the rest (newest first inside a tier), and `routes_chat`, the search tool and `topic_notes` all call it, so "show me notes about X" lists the same in both; "open X" names the note in Chat as in Ask; "latest notes about X" filters by X then sorts by date; "last three notes" is a count. Compare (C36) and slot-first answers (rank 19) remain, see `composer-ranker-1029.md`.
- Search and mentions (audit 1029 N1 to N5, N16): a note is mentioned as a whole word of at least three characters, one matcher (`entry/mentions.py`) for the Referenced-by rows, Connections, counts and backlinks, so a title like "t" no longer has 58 incoming notes; `is:` and `has:` filters, `tag:` and the bin narrow the search in SQL before the limit (pinned notes no longer vanish, binned notes are left out unless `is:deleted`, and marked "in the bin" when shown), `title:` searches titles only, a number is matched as typed (no prefix or typo guess), and a filter the search does not know is named under the box with a suggestion (`has:attachment` and `is:favourite` work as aliases).
- Locked private notes (INBOX 1437; audit 1029 rank 8, H15, N21, N12): every read surface now passes the one vault gate (`manager.note_is_sealed`). Export and History of a private note while locked answer 409 "Unlock first" and the app asks for the password; the Graph node stays, titled "Private note", with no preview, tags or word count; `/tags`, the note list, exports, Library and Timeline drop its tags; one test walks every GET route with a locked private note and fails on any leak (`tests/test_vault_read_surfaces.py`)
- Graph lag and reopen drift (audit 1029 G5, G6, G8): a restored map opens where it was left (500 notes after a reload: 99.1 px RMS drift before, 0.4 px after), and a frame that only the camera or the hover changed is composed from two cached layers of the map with the hover painted on top. At 500 notes and 4x CPU, measured under load: zoom p50 133 to 183 ms before, 16.7 to 33.3 ms after; hover p50 100 to 116.7 ms before, 50 ms after; pan p95 116 to 150 ms before, 33 to 50 ms after. The hover card no longer forces a layout every frame.
- Quick sketch: a colour added to the recent row can be taken off again, by the x beside it (shown on hover, focus and a finger) or Delete on the focused swatch; the help and the Quick sketch Guide topic say so (INBOX 1438).

- Appearance quick panel (INBOX 1435): Settings, Appearance can be popped out into a non-modal panel on `panelMovable` (drag, resize, dock) so each change is seen on the app without closing Settings; opened from the command palette (Appearance panel), a right-click on the top bar's light and dark button, and Pop out in the Appearance page's title bar. The page's own controls are moved into it, not copied (`LOOK_ROWS` and the appearance sync rule hold), with a section strip (Theme, Colour, Text, Layout, Background art, Motion) that remembers the last one, a Peek toggle (token mix, never opacity) and the page's per-control reset. Its row styles are generated from the Settings rules (`scripts/appearance_panel_css.py`, tested fresh). - Hung model and unbounded input (audit 1029 H3 to H6, H9, H10, X11, X26, N18, G27): Stop and a closed tab now cut the connection to a model that has not yet answered (the socket, not the response, which does not exist yet), and one table of deadlines in `core/deadline.py` bounds the utility AI routes and cancels them with the request (a hung fake now ends `/drafts/title` at its deadline instead of the 600 s read limit; a route with no fallback answers 504); `/models/hardware`, `/activity`, the greeting, tensions, the support bundle and `/websearch/searxng/status` read a bounded last answer instead of probing a hung backend (second call under 300 ms); the MCP server answers shape errors with -32602 and survives any one message; `/auth/reset-code/open-logs` never names the path; history, media and attachment names, pin coordinates and unknown graph ids are bounded in `api/bounds.py`. - Agent harness (audit 1029 H1, H2, H7, H8): a card that waits on the person (Confirm, a question, a memory proposal, a plan) is drawn outside the collapsible step group by one helper, `placeWaitingCard`, so prose after a parked `delete_note` no longer folds the Confirm away (button 79 by 32 at x 406, y 409, not inside a `details`, after prose followed); writes that change or remove existing text (`edit_note`, `rename_tag`, `rename_category`, `unlink_notes`, `save_skill`, `audit_link_reasons`, `tag_note` with a removal) now park for a Confirm card on the server like destructive ones, while a plan or skill the person started still runs its listed changes, and adds keep their Undo; Stop on a regenerate puts the earlier answer back; a model silent for 8 seconds gets a waiting line. The Agent tip, chat help and tour say what is true now. Tests: `tests/test_waiting_cards.py`, `tests/test_write_gate_h2.py`.
- Graph and links (audit 1029 G1, G2, G4, G16): the layout worker no longer throws at 2,000 notes and more than 4,000 links (a skipped untangle stage keeps empty buffers; positions now save, settle 28 s then 2.5 s on reload); the node popup saves an unsaved edit on Escape, the X, a map click or another note (one guard, Ctrl+Z undoes); a Size or Colour change keeps a settled layout instead of laying out again; startup removes link rows whose note is gone, a purge clears links across spaces, and diagnostics counts only links between live notes.
- Space menu (audit 1029 X4): a menu of rows, each the space (a radio item) with hide, rename and delete as real buttons beside it instead of inside it; axe on the open switcher goes from 1 critical and 6 serious findings to none.
- Timers (audit 1029 X14): a second timer no longer replaces the first; several run at once and the status bar shows the one ending first with a count; each keeps only its end time (kept in this browser), so a reload brings them back and one that ran out meanwhile is announced.
- Recording (audit 1029 X2, X3, X1, X7): closing or reloading the tab mid-recording asks first; pause and stop send the audio held since the last slice, slices are 2 s not 10; the status line shows the saved size from the server ("Nothing saved yet" at zero) instead of a fixed claim; the voice dialog opens on its first field, not Record, and single-key chords stay quiet under any open dialog; "Start and record" and the Library Record button now say "Start and open recorder" and "Open recorder", which is what they do.
- Deleting a space (audit 1029 X5): the dialog selects "move everything to Default" first and counts what the other option would take ("N notes, M documents", `GET /spaces/{id}/counts`); deleting with the contents stays final, as decided.
- Panels dock (INBOX 1434): drag a panel's head to a screen edge and a faint outline shows the zone (left or right half, bottom half, a quarter at a corner, the whole window at the top middle), kept off the top bar and status bar; letting go fills it. A dock is remembered and re-fitted on open and on window resize; dragging it off, or using the grip, brings back its old size. A reset button in the head (Put back in the middle) shows once a panel is moved, resized or docked, and Settings, Appearance has Panels open where you left them (off: every panel opens in the middle). Help and Guide updated.
- Background art (INBOX 1436): two new styles, Wander (pen strokes that walk and fade, 0.12 ms a frame) and Drift (slow value noise, 0.41 ms a frame), both under the dearest existing style (microbes, 2.15 ms); a pause of 20 seconds or more swaps the live canvas for a picture of it and puts it back on resume (a hidden tab included: canvases in the page 1 to 0, art frame callbacks 0); constellation, waves, bubbles and fireflies draw at 15 frames a second at unchanged speed and dusk at 5, each within 2 percent of the old frame by pixel diff (paint per second down 14 to 45 percent). Measured by scratchpad/ui-sweeps/bgartcost.js and bgartdiff.js.
- Companion on a board (INBOX 1432): while the companion is held, nothing pans the board (the zoom filter and the edge pan refuse), and any pan that tries is written to the lag log once a press with its source, so the next log names the path.
- Tab switching (INBOX 1433): the toast rules no longer ask the whole page whether a tab is hidden (`body[data-tab]`, set by `revealTab`), and the graph dock and map observers read the size they are handed instead of forcing a style pass. At 4x CPU on 42 notes a tab switch spends 25 to 39 percent less time in style (notes 258 to 166 ms). The lag log now names the path and caller behind `Response.json.then` (`[apiJson /entries from notes-list.js loadNotes]`).
- Security (INBOX 1424 review): asking for a reset code is limited to one every 30 seconds (429 with Retry-After), and a new code no longer kills the one being typed: up to two codes stay live, each with its own expiry and wrong-try count, and a correct one consumes both; guesses still go through the login throttle. The lock card now says where the code went: the terminal, or the log file by name when there is no terminal (desktop launch), with an Open the logs folder button for this computer only. Help and Guide updated.
- Diagnostics (INBOX 1430): Settings, Logs, the three dots, has Copy diagnostics and Save diagnostics as file (and the palette has Copy diagnostics): one plain-text report under 20 KB with the version, device, notebook size, grouped and counted lag lines (script, function, forced layout, the control pressed, viewport), the last errors with their frames, a slow-routes table, slow database statements, failed jobs and a complexity snapshot (elements, widest lists, worst stalls, the ten costliest animation loops, heap). Lag lines now carry the control pressed, viewport, pixel ratio, cores, memory, notebook size, version and build; stalls no script owns are merged into one counted line; a sampler of animation loops by script reports a loop over 120 ms a second for 3 seconds (about 0.01 ms a frame, measured; it can be switched off in the same menu). No note text, titles, query strings or home-folder paths are in the report.
- Security (INBOX 1424, audit 1028 K1): "I don't have it" on the lock screen no longer resets on a typed word alone. Print a code asks the server to write a six-digit code in its own terminal (this computer only, ten minutes, one use, five wrong tries, kept only as a hash, never in a response or the Settings logs), and the reset needs that code as well as RESET; wrong codes earn the same waits as wrong passwords, and asking again buys no extra guesses. The card now says plainly that private notes are lost for good. Help, Guide and docs updated.
- Movable panels (INBOX 1427): every dialog, popover and floating panel that wears the dialog head can be dragged by it and resized from a bottom-right grip on a fine pointer at 600px or wider; the grip is also the keyboard route (arrows move 16px, Shift and arrows resize, Home resets), a double-click on the head resets, and size and place are kept per panel on this computer and clamped to the window. One lazy script (`panel-movable.js`) hooked by delegated listeners, `translate` while dragging, no observer or frame loop; recipe `panelMovable` in DESIGN.md with a lint listing the panels that cannot be moved.
- Speed (INBOX 1426 L5, L6): opening the whiteboard no longer forces the board's first layout inside its set-up (panel sizes come from the ResizeObserver, listeners told before the write), the notes list measures rows only down to the fold, and the chat timer and clock detail paint nothing while the tab is hidden.
- Speed (INBOX 1426 L1): the model status poll no longer waits 2.5s on a slow model server (a quarter second, then the last answer; the first poll after a start says Checking and the page asks again in 1.5s), the suggested-models list asks what is loaded once at a time, the Health page's folder size is cached and measured off the request (a first count that runs long says "or more"), and start-up no longer re-folds the whole edit history on every launch (1.3s to 0.07s on 30,000 events) or holds one write transaction over it.
- Companion: far moves are calmer and varied (a portal, a puff of smoke, off one edge and in at another, ducking under a bar, a short walk), never the same twice and never the old leap; it wanders less and has four new quiet acts; Reduce motion gives a fade; per-frame layout reads are gone from the follow loop, pacer and drag release (INBOX 1429).
- Lock screen: the password field keeps focus when the splash goes, a wrong password marks and describes it; mind map names lose trailing blank lines; the browser log tag clears contrast (sweep 1028b W9, W16, W25)
- Spaces: the seeded name is Default space (migration for stored ones), a duplicate name answers 409 inline, and the space dialogs submit on Enter with a named icon group (sweep 1028b W11, W12, W30)
- A failed load of chats, backups, logs, the tag cloud and the notes shuffle says so with Try again instead of an empty state (sweep 1028b W4)
- Reminders take typed dates and a past date answers inline; one plural helper; failed-load titles read whole (sweep 1028b W2 to W5, W13 to W15, W28, W29)
- Reminders: the "Remind me to…" box reads its words like the magic box ("Pay rent next tuesday at 9am" is due then, chips show the time first); an empty add or a refused date is one line under the form with the field marked and focused, never an unhandled rejection; the date picker starts at today; the "Remind you when?" question shows once; the snooze label says Tomorrow (sweep 1028b W2, W3, W13, W28, W29).
- Plurals: one helper, nounCount(n, one, many), in place of 270 hand-made ternaries and templates that always pluralised ("1 more tags", "1 more notifications", "1 words"); a lint holds the rest down; the heatmap summary names the busiest day by date (sweep 1028b W14, W15).
- Composer: an act that names its own note ("delete the note about lentil soup") never takes the chat's last subject as its own; tested over delete, pin, open, rename, move, tag (sweep 1028b W1).
- Boards: a board opened from the timeline, a link or the Library fits its content unless its own last view shows half of it; the last board's camera is never kept (INBOX 1428).
- Boards and maps: the presentation bar shows the page name centred between the arrows as a button; it opens a list of every page (current one marked) that opens upward, so you can jump to any page, and the presentation keys wait while it is open.
- Composer: tasks as acts (audit 1028 E10) finished: "cancel the dentist task" bins a reminder or removes a checklist line, "snooze the dentist task until Friday" moves a reminder, both asked about when the name fits more than one and both with Undo; a Guide topic, Tasks in Chat, says add, complete, cancel, snooze and undo.
- Complexity: eight functions the 1028 merges grew past 15 are split by step, and commands.py plan/run shrink (seed lowered).
- Help and Guide match today's UI: Run again, the 20,000-character limit, Stop, Move under, the eraser on touch and pen, Insert, Sticky note, the Links and media menu, kept unsaved words, New code file, the lock screen focus and the import toast counts.
- Composer: "add X to my to-do list" still adds the line to a note called that, when there is one; the composer asks act_registry.READER whether a sentence is an act, instead of importing commands (the cycle test_no_import_cycles caught).
- Chat does tasks with no model (audit 1028 E10): "add a task to read chapter 5 tomorrow" or "add chapter 5 reading to my to-do list" sets a reminder (the time asked once if not said), and "tick off buy milk" or "mark read chapter 5 as done" completes the open reminder or unticked checklist line it names, with Undo; a name that fits more than one thing asks which, never guesses.
- The answer engine reads dates a note mentions for "what is on" questions, acts without the word "note" ("tag my gym log with fitness"), says when nothing matched instead of quoting the newest notes, and stops repeating the search-by-meaning loading line (audit 1028 E6, E7, E12, E30).
- Unsaved document words are kept per document, so a second document's failed save no longer replaces the first's, and kept copies go after two weeks (audit 1028 D4, D5).
- Documents fixes (audit 1028 U7, U8, U10, U11, U43, D7): a code file draws in a monospace face; a new empty document opens in Edit on a phone; Image in the links menu opens a file picker and inserts the uploaded picture (the bare stub is the fallback if the upload fails); the second Insert menu is now "Links and media" and Numbered list moved to Insert; the find panel uses the input radius and its close button is at least 24px (44px on touch); a document over 30,000 characters checks spelling and style in a window around the view, so a 100,000-character pause fell from about 75 ms to 11 ms.
- The code editor is under New (audit 1028 U6): the Library's Create picker and the command palette have New code file, which opens the template dialog on its Code group.
- Mind maps: Move under… (key M, the topic menu, the palette and the keys sheet) puts a branch under another topic without a drag, as one Undo step; and Undo or Redo pressed while a whiteboard delete is still in flight now waits for it to settle instead of restoring a row the server then deletes (audit 1028 U4, B9).
- Whiteboard fixes (audit 1028 B5, B8, B16, B21, U1 to U3, U5): a failed delete now says so and keeps the redo history; dragging an item to the edge no longer replays a fake mouse move to every listener; the eraser tests every sample of a fast touch or pen stroke; link hover paints once a frame; black or white default ink and text re-pick to read at 4.5:1 on the board or sticky behind them; Insert, Sticky note from the keyboard adds a note; a mind map's fold chevron, count and add buttons stay at least 24px (44px on touch) at any zoom.
- Importing a calendar file no longer freezes the app while it runs (audit 1028 K17): the import ran on the server's event loop.
- The browser error log route takes at most 30 lines a minute from one device, so a flood cannot push real warnings out of Settings, Logs (audit 1028 K10).
- Spelling and autocorrect leave accented words alone (audit 1028 D8): "café" and "naïve" were split at the accent and the pieces flagged or rewritten.
- Links read their scheme as a browser does (audit 1028 D14 to D16): "java<tab>script:" and leading control characters no longer pass the link allowlist, opening a document link uses the same allowlist instead of a blocklist, and a pasted address with ")" or spaces is encoded rather than breaking out of its Markdown link.
- The composer quotes short facts (audit 1028 E5): "Rent 650." or "Wifi: hunter2" was dropped as a two-word fragment, so "how much is my rent" had nothing to answer from.
- Commands keep the person's own words (audit 1028 E9): "delete notes about uni" finds the Uni notes rather than notes about "university", and "move all my uni notes" names the uni notes; a word in the notebook is never spelled out as slang.
- The command palette field is a combobox over its list and announces the result count (audit 1028 S5); the active row was already tracked with aria-activedescendant.
- The import toast says what happened (audit 1028 S9): imported, skipped as already here, and failed, and it appears even when nothing new was made (it used to say nothing then).
- The dashboard line under the greeting counts today's and yesterday's notes in SQL (audit 1028 S8): an import of 130 notes read as 120, the size of the sample the line names notes from.
- Changing the theme keeps a page background scheme (audit 1028 S10): the light and dark pair stay and the one for the showing mode applies; only a single hand-picked colour, which would override the new theme, is still cleared.
- The timeline header line is one helper for the feed, grid and table (audit 1028 S7): "1 day" not "1 days", and while more pages follow the count reads "100+ items" instead of passing the loaded page off as the total.
- The Ask button stays on screen on a phone (audit 1028 S6): the five controls beside the question wrap inside the card, where they ran 38px past a 390px screen.
- The lock screen is a labelled modal dialog and takes focus when it shows, even over an open dialog, and focus goes back to where it was on unlock (audit 1028 S4).
- Jumping to a note (palette, graph, links, chat) renders the list through the target before flashing it (audit 1028 S1): a note past the first 60 rows did nothing; one that cannot be found now says so.
- Typing in a long document no longer serialises its whole undo history on every keystroke (audit 1028 D6): the snapshot is taken once per pause, when the store writes.
- A chat message over 20,000 characters keeps its draft and says so (audit 1028 E8): a longer message names the limit instead of blaming the model, and "Save as a note and ask about it" turns the paste into a note and asks for a summary of it.
- Text from outside is marked as outside (audit 1028 E4): a Library file attached to a chat, an imported document, and a note carrying picture or file text the app read now start the turn tainted, so write tools ask for a confirm as they do for a clipped web page.
- Browser Stop now stops the model (audit 1028 E3): a closed tab or an aborted fetch sets the turn's stop flag, which cuts the stream to the model between chunks and while it waits for the first token, so the next question no longer queues behind a turn nobody is waiting for.
- Regenerate from an earlier answer cuts the saved chat the way the screen is cut (audit 1028 E1): turn 3 of 3 is no longer overwritten by a copy of turn 1. An answer that made a change (a note to self, a reminder, an agent write) asks "Run again" before Regenerate or Edit asks the question a second time (E2).
- API answers carry `Cache-Control: no-store` (audit 1028 K12): note JSON no longer outlives a lock in a shared phone's back/forward cache or a proxy.
- Restoring a backup zip keeps this computer's model address, "keep the AI on this machine", web search, update and background-task switches (audit 1028 K9): a zip from someone else could point every chat at their server.
- Security (audit 1028 K2, K3, K7, K8): an attachment's stored name from a restored database can no longer serve, read, stash or delete a file outside the uploads folder (a sibling such as `uploads2` included); unlock guesses sent in parallel count against the throttle while in flight (40 at once passed a five-try check); the session table is read by snapshot so a sweep during an unlock cannot raise.
- Document autosave sends one save at a time (audit 1028 D1 to D3): a second save sent mid-request carried the old hash and raised a false edit-conflict prompt; words typed during a save were marked saved and lost on close; a refused first save of a new document now says "Not saved".
- The composer answers lists due for a subject, kind or window, "what is left to read" over several checklists, and a summary of every note on a subject (audit 1028 E11).
- The Guide places realistic questions (audit 1028 E31): "how do I export to PDF", "stop the AI", "edit my question", "delete all my data", "which model for my laptop", "why is the AI slow" reach their topic, and a miss offers "Did you mean" with the nearest topics.

## [0.6.2] - 2026-10-27
- No-model answers read as English on untitled and title-only notes (INBOX 1420): a note is named by what it says, never a cut opening, a doubled "the" or a kept colon; bold marks and bold-only headings no longer show; questions, advice and sentences join as sentences; the note that defines a subject leads; the open-note closing appears only when the answer is about it; a citation goes after an emoticon. Ten graded questions: 26 defects to 0.
- The graph popup's Save row no longer covers the action footer (INBOX 1421): both are pinned at the panel's foot and Save, one layer higher, was drawn 36px over Open, Focus, Pin and Link after a picture was resized; Save now stands above the footer by its measured height (Save bottom 567 against a footer top of 531, now 526). Pictures already resize in every Live note editor (Capture, the Notes edit form, the graph's two boxes, Write with the AI, concept cards), one shared grip that writes the width into the picture's alt text.
- The Ask answer's head shows what was pressed (INBOX 1423): a press, an open menu and Read aloud while it speaks take the accent ground (pressed bg 0.09 white to 0.16 accent), Copy swaps to a tick for 1.2 s, Read aloud shows a stop icon with `aria-pressed` and a second press stops it, Regenerate stays and shows the ring while the answer runs. A lone Alt press is no longer handed to the window (INBOX 1422), so it cannot leave the window's own menu open until an Alt-Tab.
- The companion's landing after a throw no longer hands over idle motion that is not moving: the land act's call fell from a median 8.2ms (max 18.8) to 1.6ms (max 9.4).
- A model server that accepts the connection and never answers no longer holds every turn (INBOX 1420): each liveness check of a turn waited its own 2 s, five or more per turn, 4 to 9 s before the first step on a silent runner; one silence is now remembered for 10 s (Ollama and OpenAI-compatible), the probe waits 1 s, and a second question answers in 0.04 s.
- A hard, steep upward throw now leaves the top of the window from anywhere on screen (its climb is lighter on the way up) and falls back in; a moderate one still hangs from the top bar or bounces off it.
- The default board keeps its picture (INBOX 1418): a board thumbnail was fingerprinted on the newest write to any note on its cards, so a pin, a body edit or the janitor re-filing a note retired the stored picture and the Library card went back to the drawn preview until the board was opened again; it is now fingerprinted on the card titles it shows, and boards of drawings were never affected.
- A thrown companion goes where the throw sends it: a soft toss lands near; a hard one sideways goes far, into a corner, or off one side and in at the other; a hard one upwards can leave the top of the window and fall back in. A panel catches it only when it comes down slowly (otherwise it passes or glances off an end), and it comes down caught, sliding off or tumbling and getting up, never the same way twice running. All planned at the release; the drawn step stays under 40px a frame.
- Faster launch and fewer forced layouts (INBOX 1419): the model list is asked at launch, so the first status poll and Settings > Help find it known; the suggested-models list answers within 2.5s even on a runner busy loading; the summary words of the digest are stemmed on first use (about 0.3s off every launch); a tab strip's sliding indicator is placed a frame after the click, not inside it (library, whiteboard and Settings > Help: 100 to 250ms of forced layout at 4x CPU to about 12ms); the brand emblem waits for the page to load, the dashboard outline reads after a paint, and the Notes strip token has no read of its own.
- Lighter Python, same behaviour: the CI complexity and perf scan fell from 86 findings to 27 (every PERF finding fixed; fourteen long functions split into named steps or lookup tables), and `tests/test_complexity_ratchet.py` keeps the count from rising.
- Motion and failed reads (INBOX 1415): ten floating panels (Spaces, the bell, the clock, the history lists, the model, skills, More and Attach panels, Find on this page, the graph's note card) open and close on the menu's fade and grow instead of between two frames; Boards, Images, Contents, Bookmarks, Documents and Recordings now say they could not load, with Try again, instead of claiming nothing is there or printing the server's line; the dashboard's loading outline follows the grid by `translate` and the "Add your name" offer is not drawn under the Get started card, which took layout shift at boot from 0.105 to 0.011.
- A thrown companion lands without the hitch: the landing spot is worked out after the first frame (not in the release), its landing act waits one frame after the move, the splat face a few frames after the splat, the whiteboard box is not measured off its tab, and letting go no longer forces the selection popup's layout read (landing call 26 to 83ms before, 0 to 7ms after at 1x CPU).
- Settings' suggested model list no longer waits on a busy model runner or the graphics card probe (INBOX 1415).
- Interface: forced layouts the owner's lag log named are out of the key, frame and tab paths: a zoom keypress writes one property and no longer re-runs the font probe, Settings no longer lays out every skipped button on each focus (Help section 2.1 s to 0.3 s at 4x CPU), the OCR pinch zooms once per frame and fits words in one read pass, the dashboard map card is sized from its observer entry, and boot draws the brand emblems after asking all six slots, and idle was measured per tab (INBOX 1415).
- Companion: a throw is smooth again. Its whole flight and where it comes down are worked out the moment it is let go, on one measure of the page, so no frame of the flight reads the page (the landing's search had run in the last frame, 11 to 40ms, and 217ms on a slowed machine), and the check for popups waits until it is down.
- Whiteboard: a text box or sticky linked to a note saves again (it was refused as not a web address), and a pasted item that carried stray link ends is no longer dropped. Answers from facts: a date in a tool's time stamp (2026-10-30T17:00) counts as named, so a correct reply giving that day is kept.
- Digest: a linked title in the weekly digest draws bold inside the link instead of showing its asterisks (a link label now reads bold, italic and code, in every surface that renders markdown), and an overdue reminder reads "Do my tax return when I get home (due 20 October)" with no stray space before a comma, dangling "around" or bracketed date.
- Chat: the Confirm, Not right and Done row under an answer that cites a plan is shown (it sat in a hidden holder on a digest answer), and a plan confirmed in place keeps its Done in Chat, the Ask box and Tidy without a reload.
- Reminders: "remind me this weekend" said on a Sunday is due that day at 9:00 (it was the Saturday already gone, which Chat then asked about again); from Monday to Saturday it is the coming Saturday and "next weekend" the one after, at 9:00.
- Guide: "how do I pin a note" is answered with pinning a note (it had the Graph's node pin), a PIN for the lock screen no longer matches pinning, and with a model running a greeting, thanks, "who are you" or "that didn't help" is answered in the first person instead of "not sure".
- Guide: open and social questions are answered in the first person (what can you help me with, who are you, thanks, that didn't help, a vague organise, a request outside the app); a composed answer adds a Where line only when a place is asked for and no longer repeats "From the app's help" (the byline says it); a finished action such as a pin is no longer offered as work to resume, and the next-question suggestion follows the question.
- Graph: a note's popup follows its note as the map pans, zooms and settles (beside it, flipping side at the edge, hidden while the note is out of view), and its title row drags it to wherever you put it, by mouse or finger, until it is closed.
- Dates: "last weekend", "this weekend" and "next weekend" are held to the right Saturday and Sunday on every day of the week, and "what did I do last weekend" is held through Chat.
- Patterns: a plan line that says it is still open has a third verdict, Done. It removes your Confirm on that plan and the plan, with its variants, is never said again (shown once as Marked done). A later note that shares the plan's words also retires a plan you had confirmed, so Atlas stops saying it is open once you wrote it was done.
- Quick sketch: a thick arrow ends at its point (the line no longer pokes out past the head), and the paper colour picker opens by the More button, not the window's top left corner. The Ask box's AI switch has room inside its pill.
- Companion: a drop or throw that comes down at the bottom bar stands above it instead of sitting with its box 20px into the bar and over its buttons, and over the bar's buttons it floats just above them instead of being sent across the screen; Escape no longer throws when the onboarding overlay is gone.
- Answers from facts: a model reply is refused when "a reminder" or "both reminders" miscounts the facts, or when it states a calendar date (28 Oct, 2026-12-01, Thursday 29) the facts, the question and the clock do not name; clock times stay unchecked.
- Documents: in focus mode the sidebar and the suggestions panel can be resized by dragging their edge (or the arrow keys), and the sidebar width is the one it has outside focus mode.
- Grammar: fewer wrong suggestions; a file name (start.bat), an interface word (draggable, scrollbars), a dotfile and "back to normal" are no longer marked, and real errors still are.
- Settings, Appearance: Glass controls (off by default) puts icon buttons in the image chip's frosted glass, only while the glass blur is on; its styles are fetched only when it is on.
- Atlas guide: a long help sentence no longer leads whole (over 40 words, its best clause leads), the Dashboard help is split into short sentences, and the slash commands list is one command a sentence.
- Dates: "next fortnight", "the coming fortnight" and "in the next fortnight" are read as the fourteen days after today ("last weekend" and "this weekend" already were).
- Atlas: standing on the status bar, its tail no longer counts as touching the bar's buttons (it is tested down to the soles); 19 of 31 stands along the bar read as blocked, now none.
- Whiteboard: select words in a text box or sticky and the bar's Text style button sets a size, font, text colour and highlight for just those words (kept in the text as a run, drawn by the board, the export and Undo), with the whole box's text settings one press away; a bolded or styled edit now shows rendered as soon as you leave the box
- Whiteboard: the top of a context bar's ... menu is one labelled grid (Shape, Start, End, Dash, Order and the rest), aligned in two columns, with no wrapped pills, stray rule or indented orphan, at 1280, 700 and 390 wide.
- Whiteboard: a connector label drags by its words (a press that does not move still selects, a double-click edits), the small grip is gone; a shape you draw is selected and the tool returns to Select, while the pen and highlighter keep theirs.
- Diagrams: every ```mermaid fence now draws (flowchart, sequence, class, state, entity relationship, Gantt, pie, mind map, timeline, journey and the rest) in Read, Live, a print, the HTML export, chat and Ask replies, using the vendored Mermaid 12.2.0 loaded on first use inside a hidden same-origin frame with its own policy (the app's policy is unchanged); pictures take the app's colours, redraw on a theme or contrast switch, and a fence Mermaid cannot read stays code with one line of reason under it.
- Pictures: deleting a picture while a model is captioning or reading it no longer raises an error; the read is skipped, and a slow read no longer holds the database open.
- Library: the image ⋯ chip is glass only while the glass look is on; with it off the chip is solid.
- Library: the image ⋯ chip no longer vanishes when hovered, focused or open over a white or black picture: those states are an opaque panel with an ink glyph and an ink and panel edge, in both themes, glass on or off (open over a white picture was 1.05:1 glyph to fill in dark, now 9.3:1); the other Library cards' ⋯ already read at 7.9:1 or more.
- Atlas guide: a suggestion chip pressed inside the open guide no longer closes it, and a how-to question leads with the sentence that says how (not one that only mentions what "changed").
- Library: board and map thumbnails no longer fade to grey on the light theme, and the image tiles' ⋯ is a glass chip with a full-strength glyph in both themes (it had stayed transparent).
- Whiteboard: dragging a connector between two cards no longer leaves "Drop here to delete" on screen.
- A thrown or dropped companion settles where it lands: come down over a button it moves only to the nearest clear place (8px at 1280 by 720, where it went 256px along the bottom bar), and never along the bar across the window. Over 84 seeded throws at three window sizes the furthest landing move (a deliberate climb aside) went from 256 to 65px, and the total from 3,875 to 1,487px.
- Atlas looks friendly at rest: its brows no longer slope down to the nose, focus and a long answer wear a steady look instead of a scowl, its arms rest a little out instead of folding across the chest, and a sulk after too many pokes lasts 8 seconds, not 30. The other companions only drift between friendly faces. Measured over a scripted 3.5 minute session: a grumpy face or pose 92% of the time before, 1% after (his look); 100% to 1% (hers).
- A question toast kept up until answered steps aside for the buttons of the form or section in use (it covered Save at 1280 by 720).
- Command palette: words typed while it was still opening now list their matching notes too.
- Get started: the first answer ticks step three even if you left for the dashboard before it finished.
- Search by meaning runs on fastembed (ONNX Runtime) instead of sentence-transformers and PyTorch, with the same BAAI models. The one-time download is about 130 MB where it was about 2 GB (57 MB of packages, a 66 MB model), the engine holds about 300 MB of memory where it held 650, and one note embeds in 14 ms where it took 257 (measured here). Vectors are unchanged for the two models compared (cosine 0.9999987 or better between the two engines: bge-small on 8 texts, multilingual-e5-small on 20), so notes embedded with those are renamed to the new engine by migration f1b3c5d7e9a2 and not embedded again; notes embedded with any other model are embedded again in the background; a saved "sentence-transformers" setting reads as the new engine. A model chosen from this computer or typed by name needs an ONNX export now; one with PyTorch weights only says so.
- The search-vector backfill (at start, after a warm-up and in the periodic pass) now fills a note whose vector was made by another model, not only a note with none: search ignores such a vector, so the note was unfindable by meaning until a full re-index.
- Settings, Search and index, Old search files: once the new search model is ready, the previous engine's model folders (`models--BAAI--...`, `models--intfloat--...`: only the PyTorch weights where the new build shares the folder) are listed with their sizes and removed with Remove; in the packaged app it also removes PyTorch and sentence-transformers from the extras folder (restart to free them). Nothing is listed or removable before the new model is in place. A pip removal also leaves the installer free again; it used to stay marked running until a restart, so the next install was refused. New Guide topic: search-engine-moved.
- The launchers no longer have the torch-sharing opt-in: `TESSELLATE_SYSTEM_SITE_PACKAGES=1` and `scripts/system_site_packages.py` (which refused a system torch outside a `torch>=X,<Y` line that requirements.txt no longer has, falling back to a made-up range) are gone from start.sh, start.bat and the install guide. Search by meaning adds ONNX Runtime at about 24 MB, so there is nothing worth sharing, and a shared system package can only shadow the one the app was tested with.
- Upgrading from the PyTorch engine: the old model files do not work with the new engine, so search by meaning needs one download (about 130 MB, replacing the old engine). The notice and the welcome card now say the engine moved, that nothing downloads until you say yes, whether your notes keep their search data (BGE Small and Multilingual E5 Small) or are read again in the background, and that keyword search works meanwhile. The server sends this as `semantic_engine_moved` on the model status and the preferences, set only while the old PyTorch copy of the chosen model is on disk and the new one is not. The troubleshooting page no longer says nothing needs downloading.
- The yes to downloading search by meaning now embeds the notes saved while the question was open as soon as the model is loaded; they waited for the next launch or the next periodic pass.
- Fixes: "how do I make a reminder" leads with Magic add again; every hello invite says what to ask; the packaged builds install certifi; the reminder offer leaves past times to the date reader; a failed new-tab link says why, with Try again.
- Security: certifi is held at 2026.10.23 or newer, the first CA bundle without the eight compromised eMudhra CAs (distrusted by Chrome and Mozilla, 19 to 20 October 2026). Web search, model downloads and extras installs verify HTTPS against it.
- Tables and code blocks in a reply (and a note's Read view) have a Wrap lines button in the card's top bar, beside Copy: pressed, long lines break and nothing scrolls sideways (a wide reply table 679 over 656 becomes 656 over 656, a code line 1245 over 656 becomes 656). Tables and code each remember their choice. The table's old Fit to panel row left the ⋯ menu for the button.
- Reminders: a row's ⋯ is always drawn and takes a plain click, and the date stops a gap short of it (they shared 28px at 1280; now a 6px gap), while the snoozes and Edit still come in on hover.
- Reminders: the reminder phrase reader moved beside the parser, so the chat suggestion no longer forms an import cycle with the routes.
- Graph: the map opens settled and flows to rest in one motion (the owner, 2026-10-27: "a bunch of nodes started individually rearranging themselves sliding instantly into position one after the other", and asked for it "smooth and flowy"). Each untangle pass and the clean-up used to wait for rest, then slide its notes in a burst whose first frame closed a quarter of the way, then freeze. The worker now settles, untangles and cleans the map out of sight before the first paint and plays one eased motion into it; a map too big for that is shown at rest and glides once, every note together. With Reduce motion on, the settled map is the one frame, and the camera no longer hops after the cut-in. Cold open at 1440 by 900, median of 3, before and after: 36 notes, largest move in one frame 113 to 8 px, frames over 20 px 35 to 0, at rest 3.2 to 1.1 s after the first paint, first paint 1.3 to 1.7 s; 300 notes, 257 to 10 px, 24 to 0 frames, at rest 7.5 to 2.8 s after paint (8.9 to 4.9 s after opening), first paint 1.5 to 2.2 s; frame time over the first 3 s 16.8 ms both at 36 notes, 24.4 to 21.4 ms at 300. The clean-up no longer leaves two notes touching (3 in 12 test maps before, 0 now).
- The popup agent has a Send button beside the box (Enter still sends), and the graph Options section chevrons sit a gap short of their "?" instead of touching it.
- Chat and the popup agent: with a model running, the model writes every answer. A count, a worked sum, what is due or a read list ("What is due?", "how many notes do I have", "list my tags") is handed to it as the app's exact facts; it says them in its own words and the list, chart or panel rides under its reply. A reply whose count differs from the app's (a number tied to what it counts, said in figures or words, never a date, a time, a year or an id), a span or a conversion that differs from the app's, or that drops it, is replaced by the app's own answer, with no model named under it and none of its thinking shown. A counted list keeps its rows under the reply, and a list within a window is checked against the window's count; a request to change something (a verb with something the app can change) is never answered this way. A reminder made on a private note reaches the model, and Chat, as "A reminder on a private note", in the list and in the day's activity; that holds with no model too, so the activity reply now masks such a reminder (on purpose, not a side effect). A reminders question is cut to the window it names, read forwards ("tomorrow", "next week", "on Friday", "the next 3 days"), and the model's count is checked against that window's. Spans are checked with the rounding a person uses ("8 weeks and 3 days", "roughly 60 days") and, with none in the facts, against the dates they carry; a figure after "by", a range and a year are verified, not skipped. With no model nothing else changes.
- Picture viewer: Open in a new tab works from the desktop window. The system browser has no session there, so it gets a two-minute link to that one file. The lag log no longer counts the other-devices long-poll as a slow request every 25 seconds.
