- The composer's utility reading (`utilities.kind_of`, cached since the long-question fix) follows the web search setting: it is part of the cache key, so flipping the setting changes how "search the web for ..." routes without a restart. `web_on` reads the loaded config without building app state, and `conftest`'s `app_state` waits for background threads (`background.join_all`) so an embedding warm-up cannot recreate the repo's `data/` folder after teardown (the last `test_typo_routing` leak).
- INBOX triage: eight placed items (735, 742, 771, 772, 804, 807, 808, 903) moved to HISTORY's "INBOX resolved"; the tray holds eleven.
- Boot JS back under its cap after the companion and popup-citation merges (588,399 of 588,400 gzipped): the dead `logTerminalLineText`, same-file `typeof fn === "function"` guards in `avatars.js` and `atlas.js`, and a folded release and landing path in the companion; ten one-off probe scripts left `scratchpad/` for the file cap.
- The owner's "a ghose cursor" reads as "a ghost cursor" and "shorter and shortyer" as "shorter and shorter" (INBOX 904 fixtures). A five-letter word keeping its first three letters is now a reading (`spelling._prefix_kept`), so "ghost" competes and the word frequency still gives "ghose" to "those" where nothing else says otherwise; no plural or relative determiner follows an article ("a those cursor"); the word after "a" or "the" is not an asking word ("a whose cursor"); and a long consonant-y stem with a comparative or past ending put straight on ("shortyer", "happyer") is no longer accepted as a word.
- `test_the_running_model_manager_is_never_its_module` no longer fails only under `gate.sh`: its child interpreter got no `PYTHONPATH` (pytest.ini's `pythonpath = src` does not reach a child), so it could not import `tessellate`; the test now passes the repo's `src` in the child's environment.
- The speller loads the app's own words itself: they came from the help topics, registered only when the Guide (`help_chat`) was imported, so a process that had not met it (the first question after launch, `test_composer_725` run alone) left "dayz" as typed; `spelling._app_counts` now imports the topics on first use.
- Intent routing no longer depends on what ran before: `intent.classify` brings in `commands` (which registers the typed reader) itself, so "pin the dentist noe" and "unlnk the gym note ..." route as acts on a cold process and when `test_owner_typos.py` runs alone; before, they read as notes questions until something else imported `commands`.
- A chat named from a question no longer keeps a trailing backslash ("what is there about a gaming mouse?\\", INBOX 808): the first-turn name, the rename fallback and a model's title all drop it, and a name is one line (`routes_conversations._question_title`, `tests/test_conversations_api.py`).
- CI: the Performance workflow's frame spec no longer waits out its 180 s timeout on a tab that does not exist. It opened `#tab-btn-documents` (Documents became Library), so the click hung and every later scenario was skipped; the spec opens Library, `openTab` fails in 15 s, an idle screen that redraws names the loop (`tests/test_e2e_tab_ids.py` checks every tab the e2e specs open). The dashboard's 62 rAF/s idle on the CI runner did not reproduce locally (0 rAF/s on a seeded notebook).
- Tests: six `test_mcp_server` tests and one `test_conversations_api` test built the app config without `app_state` and wrote an untracked `data/` folder into the repo; they take the fixture, and an autouse guard in `conftest.py` clears the folder and, in a serial run, fails the test that made it.
- The owner's newest misspellings are composer fixtures (INBOX 904: alo, comoposer, comoser, coumns, idication, lisence, luve, modesl, prefileld, probablu, somehwere, whwere, bototom, timelone, underlinedd, arent, hasnt, orsmth). Two were misread and are fixed: "alo" read as "all" now reads "also" (a prior in `spelling.FUNCTION_PRIOR`), and a small word run into a slang word ("orsmth") splits into "or something" (`question_noise._repair_by_speller`); `tests/test_owner_typos.py` 135 to 153 fixtures.
- Autocorrect reaches the reminder boxes. The Magic add box and the Reminder text box carry `data-autocorrect`, so a clear typo (teh) is corrected as the word ends, underlined, with the same Keep, Put back and Edit the word menu; Harper's grammar suggestions are not applied here (`frontend/index.html`, `scratchpad/ui-sweeps/autocorrectreminder.js`, `tests/test_autocorrect.py`).
- The popup agent numbers its answers in the text. It listed Sources and drew no marks; it now takes the `grounding` events and places Chat's own numbered marks (`addInlineCitations`) after every paint, over the same list its Sources rows draw, and each row shows its number (`palette.js`, `scratchpad/ui-sweeps/popupcite.js`, `tests/test_inline_citations.py`).
- The companion's "Stay here on every page" answers the press. It was the one menu row that moved nothing (an instant pinned move to where it already was), so nothing showed it had worked; it now nods, where a nod fits its pose (`companion-menu.js`, `tests/test_companion_mind.py`; the popup-actions audit of the BACKLOG row, every other row already walks, pokes, eases, rebuilds or leaves).
- Letting go of the companion stalls less. The release read the page (obstacles, ledges) after it had written the companion, so each read restyled the whole drawing again: Atlas at 4x spent 253 ms in three restyles of 400 to 625 elements on a drop (release handler 319 ms), and a throw's landing frame did the same. The reads now come before the writes, in the restyle the box read already pays for: a drop is 2 restyles and 180 ms (release 259 ms; at 1x 87 to 56 ms), a throw's release 199 to 68 ms, its landing frame one big restyle instead of two (`release` and `nameMarkBuddyThrow` in `avatars.js`, `nameMarkBuddyThrowSpot`; `scratchpad/ui-sweeps/releasetrace.js`, `tests/test_companion_physics_cost.py`).
- Showing the Library restyles 209 elements before its first frame, down from 1,335. The 60 cards the Library keeps between visits were all restyled on every reveal (155 to 225 ms at 4x CPU on 500 notes, 18 of them on screen); cards off screen now take the Notes rows' `content-visibility: auto` with the measured median height, in the lazy sheet. The reveal's recalc is 86 to 108 ms; the first card positions are identical to 0.01 px, the settled scroll height is 56 px taller (2,587 against 2,531, until each card has been seen once) and text in cards at fractional offsets can snap 1 px differently (`tests/test_tab_entry_cost.py`, `ui-sweeps/tabtrace.js` with ULT_MS and ULT_TS).
- "in 2 weeks at 3pm" keeps its clock. `when.resolve` read a day-sized offset (days, weeks, months) as `now` plus the offset and dropped the "at 3pm"; the offset's day now takes the clock or part of day beside it, and hours offsets are unchanged (`recognise._with_clock`, `tests/test_when.py`).
- A 20,000-character question answers in 0.7 s of route time, down from 4.1 s. `utilities.kind_of` ran seven times a turn and each run read all 364 words of the first 2,000 characters against the utility vocabulary; it is now cached and skips the per-word slip search past 40 words, since a utility is a short ask (`tests/test_composer_long_question.py`).
- A quoted line starts and ends at a word. Search results, source cards and the agent's source rows cut a window out of a note at a character offset, so a card could begin "uding servers"; both cuts now move to the nearest space and carry an ellipsis (`search/snippet.py`, `tests/test_snippet_word_boundaries.py`).
- Settings: the last two Autos say what they resolved to (INBOX 904 B56). The Timeline's Bucket by reads "Auto (week now)" for the bucket it chose, and the Context window box reads "Auto (131,072)" once the model reports its window (measured at 1440: a 216 px select shell for a 109 px label, a 207 px box for a 91 px one).
- The folder import is a durable pool job (Brief 9, the last kind of B2): `POST /import/directory` queues kind `import` on the `batch` lane instead of a request task, so a quit part-way is finished at the next launch (the runner skips a file already imported by path and text hash) and the panel lists it as "Importing a folder of notes" (`tests/test_import_job.py`).
- "Remind me at midnight to see the new year" is 00:00 on 1 January, not 2 January, and keeps "see the new year" as its words (it read "To see the"). Decided: midnight alone is tonight's, the next one; a date keeps the rule that midnight belongs to the night of that day ("midnight on 5 october" is the turn into the 6th, "new year's eve" the turn into the year); "new year" on its own is the midnight that opens the year. A holiday after "the" is the thing to do, not the time. Also fixed on the way: "remind me at midnight to lock up" came out "To lock up"; the stranded "to" is dropped after the "at" goes (`tests/test_when.py`).
- A weekday named after a week offset is read: "in two weeks on wednesday" read 5 October 15:55 (the weekday dropped); it is now Wednesday 7 October, 9:00 (or the clock said: "... at 3pm"). The rule, decided to match "next friday" (the Friday of next week): weeks run Monday to Sunday, "in N weeks" is the week N weeks on and the weekday its day there, so "in a week on friday" is "next friday", and said on a Friday, "in two weeks on wednesday" is the Wednesday before the two-week mark rather than the one after it. "In a fortnight on friday" and "in 3 weeks wednesday" read the same way, and "in two weeks" alone is unchanged (`tests/test_when.py`).
- The time reader reads an hours-and-minutes offset whole and reads "eod". "In 1h30", "in 2h", "in 1.5h", "in 1h30m" and "in 1 hour and 30 minutes" were unread or, for the last, read as one hour with the half hour left in the reminder's words; they now land 90 minutes on (and "in an hour and a half" is unchanged). "eod" and "by eod tomorrow" are 17:00 on the day named, like "end of day"; said after five, both are the next day's 17:00 instead of an instant already past (`tests/test_when.py`).
- The time reader now reads a clock said or written without a colon: "3 o'clock" and "three oclock", "at three", "at ten thirty", "at three thirty pm", and the 24-hour figures "at 1530", "at 0330", "at 15h30". The word and o'clock forms keep the bare-hour rule (3 is afternoon, 9 the next nine); the figure forms are 24-hour notation, so their hour is stated and never guessed. "At one point", "at three people", "the 1530 train" and "at 2461" stay unread. Before, each answered "Remind you when?"; now `resolve("tomorrow at ten thirty")` is 10:30, `"2/11 at 1530"` is 15:30 on the locale's reading of the date, and "every monday at 1530" keeps its repeat. "thrity", "thirtey" and "fiften" are put right first (`tests/test_when.py`).
- Tag suggestions with no model can now be new tags (B80, `tagging.new_topics`): with room left after the notebook's own tags, a subject the note names in at least two different words and the notebook has never tagged is offered ("gym" and "squats" give #fitness, the chip says why); one passing word, a subject already in use or on the note, and a sensitive subject (an illness, a debt) are not. Before, "Did squats and deadlifts at the gym this morning" in an empty notebook offered no tags; now #fitness, and a trip-and-code note beside an existing #holiday gets #holiday then #software (`tests/test_tag_new_topics.py`). The suggested-tags Guide topic says so.
- Closing the "+ Tag" popover after the list re-rendered under it (Escape or the close button) no longer drops focus to the page: it goes to the chip the new card drew, else that card's tag area, else the Notes heading (`noteTagFocusTarget`). In Chromium, `document.activeElement` after closing went from `body` (both ways) to the new `+ Tag` chip (both ways), and to `#entries-heading` with its card gone (`tests/test_a11y_wcag22.py`).
- A slash command that raises an unforeseen error no longer ends the chat stream in a 500: the turn falls through to the ordinary one and the log names only the failure's class (`_guarded_slash_lines`, `tests/test_slash_falls_through.py`).
- Improve with no model proofreads the first 4,000 characters of a note (cut at a line) and returns the rest exactly as typed, saying "Only the first N of M characters were proofread" and `truncated: true`; no 4xx for a long note. Proofreading a 40,000-character misspelled note took 21.1 s on the way in (13.8 s earlier) and 2.2 s now (`tests/test_proofread_bounded.py`).
- A long question no longer stalls the composer: the app plans, routes and searches over the first 2,000 characters (`composer.PLAN_CHARS`) and still gives the model, and the saved turn, the whole of it. Planning a 20,000-character paste (`the cat or` x 1,800) went from 34 s to 0.3 s, and the same question through `/chat/stream` with no model from over 100 s to about 5 s (`tests/test_composer_long_question.py`).
- Time reader: "the last day of this month", "next month on the 3rd", "a week from friday" and "30 minutes from now" are read as what they say, not as the month, the weekday or nothing.
- A weekday's place in a month is that day: "the first monday of november", "third friday of october", "the last friday of next month" read as the day they name (they read as the next Monday or Friday), for a reminder and for a note about the past
- A day offset keeps the time said beside it: "call bob in 2 days at 3pm" fires at 15:00 in two days, not at the hour it was typed (Magic Add and the typed reminder command)
- A time said aloud is read: "half past 4", "a quarter to five", "ten past 6pm" in a reminder, a note date and a repeat ("every day at half past 7" kept its repeat rule rather than becoming one 19:30 reminder); "from ten to five" and "the 5 to 7 train" stay unread
- A typed reminder command ("remind me 3/4 at 9am") reads a numeric date in the person's date order: 4 March for en-US, 3 April for en-GB; the command path took no locale and read day first for everyone
- Notes close to this one no longer answer 500 when the notebook holds vectors of two sizes (a model switch mid-rebuild): a vector that cannot be compared counts as none, and the note is kept only when it is joined by a link, tag or category
- Every tab entry: four `:has()` anchors with a universal child restyled a whole card on every insert, so the Timeline's feed (appended in chunks of 60 rows) restyled 897 elements per chunk instead of 59: the collapsed sidebars' keyboard peek (07 and 08; the aside, hovered or focused, now sets `--sb-peek`, `--sb-peek-events` and `--sb-peek-transform` and its children read them), an opened row's `::first-line` (a sibling selector in place of `:not(:has(> .entry-title))`) and Atlas's blink (`.atl-blink.nm-blinks > *` named). Timeline entry at 4x CPU, 2,000 notes, companion off: style 654 to 246 ms, 10,375 to 2,823 restyled elements, layout 197 to 130 ms, worst task 246 to 178 ms; at 1x style 84 to 39 ms. Computed styles of every collapsed sidebar (rest, hover, keyboard focus; 1440, 1024 and 390 light, 1440 dark), 138 Atlas animation records and 60 opened rows are equal old to new. `--measure` and `--outline-step` (read once each) are inlined to keep the token budget. `tests/test_tab_entry_cost.py` holds it.
- Every tab entry: the reduced-motion blankets (the OS hint's, Reduce motion, Interface animations off) are a sheet, `motion-still.css`, that matches nothing until the OS asks for calm or one of those two switches is on (theme-boot.js before first paint, `applyAppearance`). Their subject is `*:where(:not(...))`, so every element restyled on a tab entry walked its ancestors against them in the default state, where they never apply: deleting the four rules of the manual pair took the Library's reveal from 22.6 to 13.3 ms of style at 1x. On a 2,000-note notebook at 4x CPU, the forced style of a tab being shown went (median of 15 shows, two runs each) Library 111 to 66 to 80 ms, Dashboard 57 to 36 to 40, Notes 52 to 40 to 43, Timeline 68 to 51 to 54, and `revealTab` over two entries 527 to 310 ms (Library), 266 to 185 (Chat), 243 to 164 (Notes). The computed animation and transition values of 61,000 elements and their pseudo-elements are identical before and after in the default, Reduce motion, Interface animations off and both states, at 1440, 1024 and 390, light and dark, and under the OS hint at 1440 (`tests/test_tab_entry_cost.py`).
- Two regexes that were quadratic in long input are linear (CodeQL py/polynomial-redos): `/todo`'s open-checkbox line read on through every blank line under it (a note of 20,000 blank lines: 5.1 s to under 0.1 s), and Improve's proofread, looking for the word before a slipped modal, tried an open-ended `\w+` at every letter of a long unbroken run (30,000 letters then a slip: about 7 s to under 0.1 s) (`slash_more._OPEN_BOX`, `proofread._modal`).
- Slash commands: `/recent ²`, `/oldest` with thousands of digits, `/find` with over a thousand words and `/made last 99999999999999999999 days` (also asked in words) were server errors (`str.isdigit` is true for "²"; SQLite's expression depth is 1,000; a span past `timedelta`'s range). The count is read as ASCII digits and clamped, `/find` reads its first eight words, a span too large is no span, and `/find` and `/count` match `%` and `_` as themselves, not as wildcards (`slash_more.count_arg`, `recognise._measure_cands`).
- Graph pins: a pin id such as `²` or a 30-digit number is a 404 instead of a 500, and a pin of Infinity is refused (422) instead of being stored, which made `GET /graph` fail until the pin was cleared (`routes_graph.py` `_pin_target`, `PinBody`, `PinRow`).
- Dashboard, the constellation: the scene draws on the canvas context (one gradient for the wash, a colour string per line and star) instead of calling p5's `fill`/`stroke` for each of 55 wash strips, each connecting line and each star, every frame; p5's colour parser was 426 ms of the 540 ms the idle page was busy in 5 s at 4x CPU. Busy time in 5 s at 4x: 540 ms to 309-414 ms (scene 473 to about 256 ms); the still frame differs from the old one by at most 2 of 255 on any channel (`dashboard.js` `scene`).
- Chat, first visit: arriving no longer fetches and runs the Library bundle (17 scripts, d3, documents.js and the whiteboard files, about 2 MB) in the press that focuses the composer. - Graph, leaving the tab: the map's canvas is no longer redrawn after its tab is hidden. The worker's last ticks used to each ask for a frame of a map nobody could see, inside the next tab's entry window (2,000-note notebook: 37 draws and 60 ms at 1x after the press, about 240 ms at 4x CPU, now 1 draw and 0 ms); the next visit draws in full (`gcTabHidden`, graph-canvas.js; `scratchpad/ui-sweeps/tabenter.js`).

- Accessibility, calendar add sheet: its Reminder and Event tabs now each control a tab panel (`aria-controls`, `role="tabpanel"`, `aria-labelledby`). Before: 2 tabs, 0 panels, `aria-controls` empty, so a screen reader said "tab 1 of 2" and nothing for the form beneath.

The Appearance sliders were 144 by 16; they are 144 by 28, and 205 by 44 at 390. - Accessibility, from the 2026-10-17 sweep (`scratchpad/ui-sweeps/a11ysurfaces.js`): the "/" menu in the chat box and the note boxes now names its listbox on the box that keeps the focus (`aria-controls`, `aria-haspopup`, and `aria-activedescendant` following the highlighted row), so a screen reader hears the menu open and each row. Before: the active descendant sat on the list, which is never focused.
- New chat page, from the owner's 2026-10-12 report ("appears a second or two late and all at once"): the card is no longer hidden while its starters load. The mark and the heading paint on the first frame and the starters' own box holds skeleton pieces (`showSkeletons` / `clearSkeletons`, settling in staggered), so nothing moves when they arrive. Measured in Chromium with the starters held 1.2 s (`scratchpad/ui-sweeps/chatemptypaint.js`): heading visible at 854 ms before, 15 ms after; heading moved 39px before, 0 after. Boot CSS paid for by moving sixteen OCR workspace rules to library-lazy.css (computed styles identical at 1440, 1024 and 390).
- Autocorrect, from the owner's 2026-10-17 report (B04, "hover over it and confirm it, edit it, or rewind the change"): resting the pointer on a corrected word's underline now opens the same Keep, Put back, Edit menu a click does (after 350 ms, and not while keys are going down, since the menu takes focus), and the document editor draws the underline too (`autocorrectShow`), where it had only a toast. Measured in Chromium (`scratchpad/ui-sweeps/autocorrectmenu.js`): the mark sits exactly on the CodeMirror word in the note box and the document (22x18 at the word's own rect), the menu opens from hover and click in both, and Put back restores the typed word.
- A note that says how long it holds ("until June", "through March", "by the end of September") and has no newer note on the same thing now gets one line in the answer saying that time has passed and the note may be out of date.
- The toolbox is ranked tool by tool, not group by group: every tool gets a chance from the words of the question (name, description and argument words, the fired group, the core, a question about a capability halving its writes), a small window keeps the likeliest, and Settings, Logs says what a turn offered and held back with each score. Of 15 fixture questions the wanted tool survived an 8,000-character window 14 times, up from 11.
- The composer runs nine built-in skills with no model (Summarise my week, Daily review, Catch up on a topic, Find loose ends, Auto-tag my notes, Link related notes, Tidy suggestions, Notebook health check, Find notes worth combining), read straight off the notes and labelled as composed; the others are marked (needs a model) in the Skills menu. A window such as "the last seven days" is now read and worded "in the last seven days".
- Chat, 13 more slash commands (`ai/slash_more.py`): `/today`, `/yesterday`, `/find <words>`, `/pinned`, `/oldest [n]`, `/random`, `/tags`, `/categories`, `/todo`, `/due [week]`, `/calc <sum>`, `/stats`, `/orphans`, all exact with no model; the "/" menu has a row for each, built from `GET /chat/commands` (a command that takes words fills the box), the Guide topic and `/help` are written from the same registry, and plain words read as the command ("what are my pinned notes", "show my 3 oldest notes", "do I have any open todos", "give me a random note", slips such as "wich notes are pined" included; 1 false read in 7,945 fixture strings, the existing untagged one).
- Composer, hello, thanks and goodbye are composed from a head and a tail (`ai/composer_parts.py`), not a stored line said whole: with no model, 300 seeds of "hi", "thanks" and "bye" gave 19, 18 and 18 distinct replies (13, 8, 8 professional), now 104, 121, 124 (104, 70, 71), and a reply never ends on a sentence one of the last three ended on.
- The enlarged profile picture reacts (B62, the owner: "doesn't have any life to it"): its face drawn from your name kept one mood, and under reduced motion it only blinked. Now its face changes as the companion's does, a crossfade so also under reduced motion: brighter as the view opens, glad, excited, then laughing as you poke it in a row, a neighbouring look with each line it says, and back; it waves as the view opens. Measured in Chromium (`profileviewer.js`): five face changes in 12 s plus five over three pokes, one figure left after, eyes on the pointer at -1 and 1; reduced motion, the same faces and no movement. The companion's perch, re-verified (B88a, `perchloss.js`): 26 of 26 scenarios on a perch at 6 s on the chat and notes tabs.
- The companion decides from what you are doing (B87c, B88c, the owner: "lifelike ncp decision making"; "more movement, more transition and actions"). Typing, it keeps you quiet company (reads along, stops to think) and saves the big gestures; scrolling, it looks about; sitting idle, it plays; gone a while, it winds down; the pointer close by, it notices you; each tab leans it to its own thing (a map on the graph, a book in notes, a think in chat). The wait between picks stays in the decided 20 to 60 seconds and is placed by its energy, your typing, a big act just done and you idling. A big gesture comes on a beat (a dip at the knees, a glance your way before a wave), a breath out follows it, and sometimes the act that comes of it (a pleased nod after juggling, a think after its map, a stretch after meditating). Three new acts: it stops to think, it sighs, and Atlas tosses one star from its hand; a new switch, Stop to think, or sigh. All in the lazy companion-menu.js, fetched at the first tick; nothing new runs between acts.
- Atlas throws its stars (B88b, the owner: "the throwing stars action for atlas isnt animated"): the juggle was three stars turned on CSS circles through the face while both arms held still. The arm rig now throws them in its own frame (no new frame loop): a shower from the right hand high over the head to the left and back low, three a third of a cycle apart, each hand dipping as it catches and flicking up as it throws. Thrown across the screen, Atlas loses its stars: they fly out, fall and fade, once a flight. Reduced motion keeps the drawn stars. Measured in Chromium (`atlasstars.js`): each star runs x 10 to 52 and y 3 to 18.5 in drawing units, at 57 fps; thrown, the stars show, fall and are at 0.18 opacity by 0.9 s and cleared by 1.3 s. The spill is drawn at 30 a second: a throw's style invalidations (`atlasinval.js`) are 2,277 without it, 3,348 with it drawn every frame, about 3,030 at 30.
- Companion physics, Atlas (B87a, the frame cost left from the physics run): a carried or thrown Atlas no longer forces a restyle each frame. Its rig, its breath and its props read the page's style only after a wake (a class, a pose, a mood, a gesture) and work from what they read until the next, and its rings', planets' and idle layers' loops hold while it is carried or flies (atlas-lazy.css). Traced at 1x (`atlasinval.js`, the same carry and the same throw before and after): the carry 7,671 style invalidations to 3,218 and 7,571 elements restyled to 3,280; the flight 6,745 to 2,277 and 7,933 to 2,610; forced restyles over a carry and a throw at 4x (`atlasrecalc.js`) 221 to 75.
- Settings, Models: saving or resetting the memory correction offers Undo (and Redo), like every other write (`saveModelHardware`).
- Note offers, from the owner's 2026-10-17 list ("recognise future date and time mentions and suggest ... to add it to the timeline, calendar and as a reminder"): a future day or time in a note is still offered as Remind me, and now says the reminder goes on the timeline and the calendar; taking it ends on a notice with Show on calendar, which opens the calendar (or, below 768px, its agenda) on that day with the new reminder in it.
- Timeline feed, from the owner's 2026-10-17 list ("scroll above today's date to see future dates"): the feed opens on today with the week ahead above it, each empty day ahead a head with an Add (the calendar's add sheet). An empty today no longer sits above later days that have rows. A row's detail moved to its own lazy file (boot JS 588,462 to 587,787 bytes), and a Ctrl+wheel zoom after a pause no longer throws.
- Timeline calendar, from the owner's 2026-10-17 list ("double click on a date and be able to add an event and set a reminder"): a double click on a day or an hour, the calendar head's Add, or N opens one sheet with that day filled: a reminder, or an event (a meeting note at its time, with a reminder at its start). The words are read as quick add's chips, and a time alone keeps the day pressed. Undo takes either back.
- Workflow: sessions on this repo auto-compact at 400k tokens (`.claude/settings.json`) with compact instructions in CLAUDE.md section 8, so long sessions stay cheap per turn and keep their state.
- Companion physics, from the owner's 2026-10-17 report ("throwing companions ... insanely framey and laggy"): a carried or thrown companion no longer restyles the whole page tree each frame. At 4x CPU slowdown the flight ran at 19 fps (median frame 50 ms) and now runs at 55 to 58 fps; the carry went from 34 to 38 fps to 56 to 59. The cause was a document-wide `:has()` rule matched on every restyle of the companion and an inherited sway property written on it each frame; both are replaced. A throw let go on a busy page is also read from the input's own timestamps, so it flies instead of dropping. Atlas's arm rig now reads style once before it writes any (a thrown Atlas: 29 fps to 58 at normal speed, 5 fps to 24 at 4x CPU slowdown).
- Companion perch, from the owner's 2026-10-17 report ("loses its perch and is left stuck floating"): a drop or a throw that comes down in open air over a control it cannot step clear of (measured on chat: a throw to the window's foot at the right floated over the composer's mode switch and stayed, 3 of 117 drops there) now comes down on the nearest good perch; open air with nothing under it still floats where you put it.
- Boot budget: the Saved companions pane (`mountBuddyPresets` and its four helpers, Settings > Appearance only) moved out of avatars.js into companion-menu.js (lazy, behind a stand-in), taking the boot from 588,462 to 587,474 bytes gzipped against the 588,400 cap, which is unchanged.
- Companion physics, re-measured at 4x CPU slowdown (`throwframes.js`, 1440x900, 3 runs each, against the code before the 2026-10-17 fixes): carrying and throwing your face 38 fps to 57 (style recalculation per frame 13 ms to 2.7); Atlas carry 8 fps to 28 and its flight 10 fps to 25 (style 93 ms to 18 per frame). Atlas is still under 30 fps at 4x: its breath, tail and arm-rig loops (atlas-life.js, atlas-motion.js) each dirty style every frame. Without the slowdown both run at 56 to 60 fps.
- CI: the companion's data-cover check reuses the file's own body observer and the perch check's frame (no new MutationObserver or requestAnimationFrame), and the bar watch reuses the follow loop's resize observer, so the wake-source ratchet needs no raise.
- Companion perch, second cause (B88a): sitting on the status bar with its legs peeking over it, the bar going (a phone's emptied status bar is `visibility: hidden`) left it in the air for good, because a peeking or leaning companion counted as supported whatever was under it and nothing watched a bar. Measured in Chromium (1280x800, reminders): in the air for the whole 14 s window before, 0 ms after (it is on a card within 250 ms). A bar it sits on is now watched by a resize observer, a peek or lean is supported only while its edge is shown, and a perch lost inside the three-second rate limit is looked at again when it ends instead of waiting for the next idle look.
- Settings, from the owner's 2026-10-17 list: every Auto names what it chose, Default accent restores the palette, the dashboard mark follows the accent, Expand all / Collapse all on panes with folds, Use/Stop model follow what exists, dictation sizes show what is installed and can be removed, the gemma4:26b card says a4b, Settings hints share one size, a stale "running" job keeps its own start time, and the web menu offers SearXNG with the DuckDuckGo provider.
- Documents and forms, from the owner's 2026-10-17 list: an md document opened after a code file starts in live view, the edit form's tag input sits under the chips, unticking a quick access row no longer scrolls the manager, Full view holds in a short window, a document's date row uses the app's own picker, new documents and boards open with their name selected, a redraw no longer sends the shape library to the top, the empty-board card is one row, a packaged build refuses to remove the desktop window, and clicking an autocorrected word opens Keep, Put back or Edit instead of reverting.
- Writing room: Save as note now files a note (it saved a draft); the caret half offers Save as draft. The Tag with Atlas panel moved out of the boot scripts into the tag-suggest bundle.
- Tag with Atlas: the panel offers the other categories the note could go in (one tap moves it), says plainly when it has no tags to suggest, and always has a field for a tag of your own.
- Canvas fixes from the owner's 2026-10-17 list: the whiteboard's Group and Ungroup follow the selection, W and H scale a multi-selection and x/y/w/h update live; the companion rides a scroll area that became scrollable after it perched; a middle-mouse drag pans the graph from its first pixel; file, bookmark and document nodes open from the mind map and graph (F2 sets a caption on a reference node); a document node can be pinned in the graph; a leash force keeps linked bridge notes nearer their category.
- Emoji search reads everyday names as well as Unicode ones: the folded hands now answer to pray, thanks and high five (`ICON_EMOJI_ALIASES`).
- The plain Ask and Chat prompts now carry the user's date and time like the agent's (`librarian.clock_hint`); Tessellate is a taxonomy topic, so Tidy no longer offers to rename "About Tessellate"; a failed agent step names what failed instead of "Failed due to error".
- UI, from the owner's 2026-10-17 list (INBOX 904): a Get started menu on the dashboard and in the bell until the three steps are done (B01); Connect a model is a split button whose caret hides the no-AI popups (B05); the writing room's working spinner sits in the Atlas column head (B76); a Japanese emoticons group in the icon picker (B81); the Logs button of a finished job stays top right; the OCR workspace explains a missing PDF renderer and links to Packages.
- Composer, from the owner's 2026-10-17 list (INBOX 904): "What have I saved recently?" lists the newest notes again; key mashes ("asdkjhfgs") and test messages ("test", "testing 123") get their own replies instead of being taken for a nickname or searched; the assistant says it is Atlas's assistant and how to reach Atlas; the capability rundown is composed and sized to the request; "what do my notes cover?" is answered about the whole notebook. Plan mode keeps `make_plan` on a small model's toolbox.
- Workflow: the `lean-workflow` plugin (1.1.0) moves to its own MIT repository, `Braydenh563/lean-workflow`; `tools/lean-workflow`, its marketplace file and its template test leave this repository, and the install line in CLAUDE.md section 8 changes.
- Workflow: `lean-workflow` 1.1.0 adds a generic `scripts/codemap.py` (Python, JS/TS, Go definitions and test files, `--check` freshness), `orient.sh` and `gate.sh` (`--changed`, `--staged`, filled from the repo's CI) that `lean-setup` installs, an Inbox and a Decisions list in `now.md`, line-limit warnings for CLAUDE.md and `now.md`, and rules for remaining-work files, fixed test clocks and measured UI claims; `lean upgrade` adds them to a 1.0 repo.
- CodeQL notes on main: timewords' deferred weekday rule is a named function, logbuffer's sequence is an `itertools.count`, composer no longer builds an unused synonym table at import.
- Workflow: `usage-guard` becomes the portable `lean-workflow` plugin (agents, `retro` and `lean-setup` skills, autopilot prompt, `/prune`, session history, large-output and auto wrap-up notes); `test_acts` reminder time bomb fixed.
- Workflow: usage tiers, model rungs and the Fable opt-in rule (CLAUDE.md section 8), four project subagents, `scripts/usage_report.py`, the `retro` skill and ledger, and the `usage-guard` plugin.
- Docs: the owner's 2026-10-13 composer batch placed in BACKLOG (magic add-on wording, Harper hover-confirm, variation, unusual input, Atlas's Assistant naming, note-type switch, the packaged desktop window, recent-notes composing, taxonomy options and uni filing, the composer's Improve writing and Generate title).
- Tests: the 32 date-suffixed test files are folded into their feature's test file, five same-feature groups (undo bin, routes batch, LAN, OCR page, graph layout) are one file each, and the reminder, time-words, stats and reading tests run on a fixed clock; the test count is unchanged.
- Tests: the 32 repo-scanning tests share one cached tree walk (`tests/_repo_files.py`) and one decoded copy of each `src/`, `docs/` and `tests/` file (`tests/conftest.py`), instead of an `rglob` each; every test keeps its own file set and exclusions.
- Tests: stabilized the model-path validator test by freezing its clock (a wall-clock minute that matched the answer's number was read as backed and the "Heads up" warning was lost); production validation behaviour is unchanged.

## [0.5.0] - 2026-10-12

- Tessellate: the product renamed from MemoryMap AI ("Your notes, pieced together"); the no-model composer answers personal, task, Guide and date questions from your notes; PIN quick unlock; LAN device trust; launch splash and logo animation; whiteboard mind map placement; timeline pill glide; jobs logs per run.
- 0.5.0 finish: the packaged Windows exe shows the launch splash; new installs keep notes in a `Tessellate` folder (an existing `MemoryMap AI` folder is kept); the notebook file is `tessellate.db` (an old `memorymap.db` is renamed once at start, older backups still restore); backups and exports download as `tessellate-*`; board previews no longer draw captions across sketched shapes; the README's Timeline shot shows the month calendar. The manual prints every page; the logo's resting motion is visible; the first accent swatch is the palette's own default; Atlas searches the web first when asked to, and no longer calls a past form or a typo of a quoted word missing; the launcher splash's name and links are centred; note link chips no longer clip "g" and "y"; Ask no longer writes "every a week" or "Your the ... note"; a wrapped line in the terminal log view lines up under its message; the Timeline calendar shows a loading placeholder while it reads a period; the shortcuts dialog keeps its header while it scrolls; the About logo is larger; the launcher splash shows its links at once and its step list after a second; the log list view wraps a long message inside its own column; Draft with Atlas is disabled while the AI is off; each backup's Restore and bin buttons sit at the row's right end; the calendar's loading placeholder matches the Timeline list's; the dashboard greeting says days since your last note, not days away; the dashboard's loading placeholder follows the grid down instead of covering Quick access; the Add tags panel opens at once and always closes on an outside click and has a close button; the graph, whiteboards and mind maps fade in on their first draw; the table block's ⋯ button is a full-height pill, so its hover matches the Copy button; Atlas no longer reads ":D" as a name, answers the time in am/pm and "what about the time in Japan", and treats "search up" as a web search; app links such as "[Open your notes](#/notes)" render as links and no longer trigger a "could not find Open" warning; the note type dropdown in Properties is the full width of the fields below it; Settings, Models has a switch to hide the "No model connected" banners (under Model backend, so it shows with no model connected; the Guide and Help name it); Settings, Models hides Model per feature (unless one has its own model) and Advanced response settings while no model is running; a dropdown and its reset button in Settings have a gap between them; the Arc layout fits low on the screen with its arcs in view; the focus timer's time and ring are filled in when the widget is first drawn; Quick access no longer shows an empty dark square beside the check on hover; a fresh dashboard opens with the digest and the notebook constellation (wide) first; the README says plainly that Tessellate is in beta (and its "Formerly" line sits tight under the tagline); the installer, the program folder, the exe and every download are now named Tessellate (uninstall the old version and reinstall; notes are kept); the CI test job has a 40 minute limit, as the Python 3.13 run was cancelled at 25; a refused connection to the model server is one plain log line, not a page of traceback; only one formatting-toolbar dropdown is open at a time; the launcher splash's log sits under the step list instead of the screen's bottom edge.

- Fixed: chat with no model answered "how do i pin a note", "how can I rename a note", "how do I tag a note", "how do I make a mind map" and "how do I use the whiteboard" with "nothing in your notes about ..."; they now reach the Guide (the Guide gold test also runs on its own).
- Fixed: chat with no model, "summarise my work notes" when the only note is titled Work answered "Your notes don't seem to cover that"; it now says the note is only a title so far.
- The Guide with no model: typed questions reach the right topic and its first line answers them, "why is the chat so slow" is Performance mode, "where did my deleted notes go" is the bin, "can i export everything to markdown" is Import & export, "is my data sent anywhere" opens with "No."; a switch's topic says how it is set now ("Web search is off now. Turn it on in Settings, Web search"); help sentences no longer break at "e.g." or "0.5x" (25 of 25 gold questions, from 19).
- Fixed: a real server answered every chat and the model status with an error since the import-cycle change (the model manager module took the running manager's name). Chat with no model: "how do i export everything to markdown", "how do I back up my notes" and "why is the chat so slow" are answered by the Guide, not searched for in the notes.
- Chat with no model: a reminder time says which half of the day ("12:39am", "12:39pm", "midnight"); "remind me tonight" said after eight is the next whole hour, not eight o'clock gone by, and a time already past ("tonight at 8", said at ten) is asked again rather than refused; "file the golf note under sport" moves it (a word after "under" is never a nickname).
- Chat with no model: "remind me to call the dentist" with no time said is asked once ("When should I remind you to call the dentist?") rather than set for tomorrow at 9, and a reply of just a time ("friday at 3", "tmrw") sets it. "On my birthday" reads the birthday a note gives ("my birthday is 3 December") when no other is known. "who is Sam" looks in your notes again, not treated as general knowledge.
- Ask and Chat with no model: questions about you are answered from what your notes say of you, from every note: "where do i live" is "You live in Perth, going by your note of 11 October.", "whats my sisters name" is "Your sister is Jess", "how old am i" says it needs the year, "what's my favourite food", "what do i do for work", "what am i learning", "do i have any pets"; "what do you know about me" lists every fact with its note (30 of 30 gold questions, from 9). Questions about Atlas ("do you have feelings", "who made you", "whats ur fav colour", "can you keep a secret") get a short true answer, "am i a good person" is not judged, and a general-knowledge question with nothing in your notes says so and where to turn on web search. Typed tasks reach their act through the speller: "remnd me to pay rent on friday", "delte my old wifi note", "dont let me forget to water the plants tomorrow", "tag the dentist note health", "get rid of the note about golf" (30 of 30, from 18). An act's Confirm line and its "which note do you mean?" are said eight ways a voice and never like the last three.

"Nothing matched" now says how many newest notes it shows instead, and counts are words ("of six in all").

"when did I buy that gaming mouse??" over "You just bought a new gaming mouse discounted from $150 to $68 haha" is "On 17 July you bought a gaming mouse, discounted from $150 to $68.", the source mark right after the day; a note's day words ("yesterday") give the day, and its asides (haha, lol, emoji, "just" before a done thing) are left out when its words are said back.

The OS protected store keeps it (Windows DPAPI, macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service), never the notebook or a backup; the lock screen says "PIN or password" only where one is set; five wrong PINs, a password change or Forget PIN remove it.
