- Notes, Questions and Library, Recordings show the empty state block with an icon, the sentence and the action; a Settings section fades in; Background jobs has a Report button for the last import.
- Settings, Themes: resting the pointer or focus on a theme shows it on the whole app, and Surprise me applies a random one.
- Long menu labels are cut with an ellipsis inside the row and shown whole on hover, in every font; the no-model notice steps its button down in a narrow card; Settings, Help, Credits has a Guide topic.
- Toasts stack neatly: the same notice inside 4 s is one card with a count, three show and the rest fold into a "+N more" card that opens the bell; no two cards cross while they move.
- First run: an empty notebook is offered a way to bring in notes kept in another app.
- Settings and menus: a worded button is announced by its words, Most used follows a write at once, a found setting lands on its control, the palette learns from what you ran for longer searches, help popovers fade out, and the background jobs poll stops when you lock.
- Settings, Help: a Credits section lists every library and data set the app is built on, with its licence and a link to its source.
- First run: the welcome, the tour, the recovery offer, the console question and the updates question take turns in a fixed order, one at a time, after any toasts have gone.
- Recordings: an empty Recordings page shows an icon, a title, a line and a Record button.
- Recordings: the waveform track has visibly rounded corners and its own tint, with the bars kept inside them.
- Recordings: the playback speed menu is the same height as the menu button beside it.
- Agent mode: a new Move notes tool (71 tools) files chosen notes under a category or sends them to another space. The app asks first and shows what will move, and Undo puts every note back in its old category or space. The Move to a category and Move to space buttons use the same code.
- Agent mode: Stop now also cancels the write a step was about to make. A step whose model call came back after you pressed Stop used to write anyway; it is refused, and reads still run.
- Agent mode, whiteboards: reading a board also returns it as a flat outline (frames with their cards, text boxes, shapes, links); searching boards matches every word in any order; a diagram can grow from a card already on the board (parent_ref card:<id>) instead of starting a new one.
- Debug (JavaScript): classes (methods, static methods, extends, super), `**`, `??`, simple default parameters and `for...of` over an array or string now step; what is left (getters and setters, class fields, destructuring, `?.`, async, generators) is still named with its line.
- Backups: a backup is one file. Reading a copy back no longer leaves `-wal` and `-shm` files beside it, in the backups folder or in the second-copy folder.
- Settings, General: the Bin row reads "Auto-clear the bin after" with the list of what it covers on a line below, so changing the value no longer makes the row taller.
- Backups: in the desktop app, "Also copy each backup to" sends a second copy of every backup to a folder you choose (an external drive, a synced folder), keeps the same number there, and notes on the backup when the drive was not connected. Each backup row says where it was also copied.
- Settings, About: Files on disk is a bar with a legend (the notebook, attached files, pictures, backups, optional features) and a total, so you can see what is taking the space and what an optional feature costs.
- Backups: a line above the list gives the automatic schedule, when it last ran and whether that worked (or why it failed), and when the next is due.
- Import: an imported note that was in the bin longer than the bin keeps notes now gets a full period from the import, so the next start no longer clears what you just brought in; a big import commits in batches and reads each note for dates once (about 12 to 25% less processing per note).
- Settings: a second browser that has never agreed with your notebook now takes the notebook's look instead of pushing its old one over it.
- Documents: a code file spell-checks only its comments and the words inside strings (a string's f, r, b, u prefix and an f-string's `{expr}` are skipped), the browser's own squiggles are off there, and an underline opens the prose suggestion popover on hover, click or right-click.
- Selections: right-click a selection to bring its popup back (the editor's format bar or the ⋯ menu) after it was dismissed; the browser's menu stays when nothing is selected there.
- Documents: the "/" menu has a Flowchart starter the Live view draws at once; the toolbars' inline marks and the renderer share one table (`MD_INLINE_MARKS`); the Dashboard's open-question line shows the question without its markdown; the code editor's completions have their own Guide topic.
- Settings: Evidence checks now turns an answer's evidence view off and on (it was stored and shown and switched nothing).
- Documents: a Python document offers the standard library's names after an imported module's dot (math., os.path.), with signatures, and pointing at one shows its signature and first doc line.
- Documents: a .docx with tracked changes imports with them kept as suggestions, a code block's language survives a round trip through Word, a single word typed in suggestion mode is spell-checked, and a code file's finding card stays closed while a menu is open.
- Documents: with no model, the code Assistant's and the document assistant's model-only controls stay visible but disabled with the reason and a Settings link; the model-free tools stay live, and a code question the tools can answer (format, run the tests, where is a name used) runs that tool. The inline Ask bar in a code document speaks of lines and code. All of it comes back live when a model connects.
- Documents: the split view's second half has completions, lint and snippets; Ctrl+K in a code file waits for its second chord, so Ctrl+K Ctrl+S opens the keys sheet without the palette flashing first.
- Documents: a SQL document's query can read a CSV document as a table by its name (Sales 2026.csv is sales_2026). Library: Live Text is on every page of a PDF in the scroll layout, not only the single-page view.
- Documents: the debugger's Variables open a list, a dict or an object into its first fifty items, and a document's breakpoints are kept on this device after a reload. Ctrl+Shift+D (the Debug tab) is listed in the keys sheet and the palette.
- Documents: a Python console line still running after ten seconds is interrupted (KeyboardInterrupt) rather than its runtime ended, so the names the last run left are kept.
- Notes: a card no longer shows a topic chip that repeats one of its own tags (a topic the graph named after the tag).
- Chat: the time somewhere answers for a place typed one letter off ("westen australia" is read as Western Australia), and the answer names the place as read.
- Documents: Replace in every document reads every document's text in one request (it read one page of the list and then each document by itself, so documents past the first page were missed), and it has a row in the document's ⋯ menu.
- Statistics and Ask charts: the axis ticks at round numbers (0, 500, 1000, 1500 rather than 310, 620, 930), and ten thousand and up reads 10k so a five-digit label is not cut off.
- Find anything: Sort has Group by category (a note under the category it is filed in, with a count, the rest under their kind), and GET /search now names each note hit's category.
- Accessibility: the status bar's notes and reminders counts are named by what they show ("29 notes: Your notebook..."), and a finished first step by its own words, so an assistive tool hears the visible text (WCAG 2.5.3); axe on the dashboard (light, 1440) goes from 1 finding on 3 controls to none.
- Dashboard: the no-model notice in the digest card (306px wide) puts its Connect a model button under the words, as on a phone, instead of leaving them a 52px column nine lines tall; it is 82px tall, was 157px. Wide notices (Chat, Ask, Writing room) are unchanged, one row of 47px.
- Filing and tags: with no model, notes are filed by a larger everyday vocabulary (boiler, payslip, parents evening, brake fluid, hand luggage and about 600 more, in memorymap_everyday.json beside the taxonomy pack). On the 120-note test notebook the share filed right went from 42% to 62% (79% when sensitive notes are suggested, not filed); on 48 notes written beforehand and never used to choose a word, 46% to 67%, and wrongly filed notes fell from 6 to 3. The pack file is untouched.
- Notes, Capture: while you type, a "File under" chip beside the suggested tags offers the category your notebook's own words point to (the reason on hover); pressing it sets the Filing menu. It appears only while Filing is on Atlas's choice, needs no model and writes nothing.
- Filing: a model that misses the wait is not asked again for a minute (notes are filed by meaning at once, ending the 15-second wait for each of a burst), and a note made through the API (scripts, importers, the agent) waits for the model no longer than the filing wait in Settings (15 seconds by default, was three minutes), with at most four waiting together, so a burst against a silent model no longer fills the database connections.
- Background tasks: an autonomous pass with no model running says "Skipped: no model is running" instead of "Finished analysing and linking notes."
- Notes: Similar notes no longer lists a note that is already linked (a press on it answered "already linked"), nor a draft against a committed note.
- Search by meaning: a model whose files would not load, or one not downloaded yet, is fetched as a visible task ("Fixing search by meaning") while search uses keywords, twice at most before you are asked to reinstall it. The embeddings backfill in Background jobs can be stopped between batches.
- Settings, Search and index: each built-in embedding model says its real state, Downloaded with its size on disk, Not downloaded, or Files missing with a Reinstall beside it. A folder holding the weights without their config no longer counts as downloaded. Settings, Packages points there instead of keeping a second list of the same models.
- Dashboard: the Quick access tiles no longer overflow their group by 4px (1440, 1024 and 600 wide); the ring room is kept only for the strip that scrolls on a phone.
- Statistics: the links and unlinked-notes counts no longer count a link to a binned or private note, so a hidden note cannot show as joined to anything.
- Settings, Data: "Clear dismissed suggestions" now also forgets the tags turned down on notes ("Not suggested" in a note's edit form). The line above the button counts them, and Undo (the toast or Recent changes) puts each back on its own note.
- Graph: a dragged note settles near where you let it go and is never pinned by the drag; double-click pins it (and again lets it go), and Unpin all clears only those pins. Opening or closing the gear panel or the ⋯ menu no longer moves the map or a single note. A note's popup and New note stay between the top bar and the status bar at any window height, their body scrolling and their buttons pinned in view.
- Graph: a topic's card has File as a category, which files its notes under one category named for the topic, with Undo. A topic no strong shared term names is named by a term two of its notes share, then by its most linked note's title ("Around …"), rather than "Topic 2". A deduced link reason says how sure it is in a word (a strong, fair or loose guess) instead of a percentage, and dragging a topic by its name saves its pins in one write.
- Graph: picking a saved view puts every note back where the view stored it and holds it there; a note added since is placed beside its links while the saved ones stay still. Before, the view's layout change warmed the map before the hold arrived and moved every note. Atlas: under the system's reduce-motion hint the figure's float, glide and trailing lower body stop rather than slowing to 6s; a gesture still plays.
- Menus: opening a '?' help popover closes any other open menu, everywhere, so they no longer stack. Dashboard: the constellation's yellow and cyan stars are drawn darker in light so each reads at 3:1 on its well.
- Companion: asleep, it keeps its Zs in its large view. It no longer wakes because the view opened under a still pointer, an act under way ends as it falls asleep (a wave no longer plays on under the Zs), and an act caught by the window being hidden ends when you come back rather than holding its pose. Its keyboard focus is a soft glow behind the figure instead of a box, and a click shows none.
- Docks: past seven items a dock's sort and view controls fold into its ⋯ at every width, and Notes' Select and the graph's Refresh go there below 600.
- Mind maps and boards: the View menu is two columns with its groups parted by hairlines, no printed headings (a map's measured 785px tall, now under 450), and Full screen is a row there only on a phone, where the top bar's own button is hidden.
- Phone: eight dialogs (extract, history, connections, binned, run a skill, board keys, meeting notes, features) open as bottom sheets below 600px instead of floating centred cards.
- Notes: a note's ⋮ menu has Make a mind map, which builds a map from the note (its title in the centre, its headings and lists as branches) with no model; the agent does the same in one call with its new map_from_note tool.
- Chat with no model: "delete the other one" after an answer that named two notes acts on the note it did not name; each answer now carries its notes' titles back on the conversation.
- Code documents: Debug on a Python file of tests runs its tests, so a breakpoint inside a test stops there and the Tests tab lists each result with the totals; Stop ends the run without the tests after it.
- Chat with no model: the other tabs' starters now do what they say (suggest tags for the open note, save the last answer as a note, what links to the open note, what is on the open board, summarise or list the key points of the open document) rather than quoting notes.
- Settings: importing a settings file adds its skills, personas and templates to yours by name (the file's wins a clash) instead of replacing each list; Undo still puts the old lists back exactly.
- Activity: the Guide, drafting and document review now write their steps into the running list (thinking, writing the answer, each suggested change), as Chat already did.
- Library: each list's search box (documents, boards, bookmarks, recordings, skills, files) now suggests that list's own titles as you type, under "In this list", not only your recent searches.
- Skills: a skill held back from small models (its measured rate is below the bar) can no longer be started by the agent's run_skill either; the agent is told why and does the job step by step.
- Chat: a stray key typed against the last word ("dentist\\") no longer shows in your own bubble; an emoticon such as ":\\" stays.
- Chat with no model: "what's the time in Australia" (or the USA, Canada, Russia, Brazil, Indonesia, Mexico) names each of its time zones, west to east, rather than the capital's alone; a named state or city still gets its one zone.
- iPhone: the app keeps out of the notch and off the home indicator (the page now asks iOS for the safe areas), a dialog's head and foot stay inside them, a note opened full screen starts below the notch, field text is 16px under a finger so Safari no longer zooms into a field, and a dialog's fields, a note's icon facts and the Categories counts are 44px targets. Measured at 390x844 with an iPhone's user agent and touch: 40 findings to 2 (the chat title, and one sheet that would not open under load).
- Other devices: QR code beside the address in Settings, Account & security and on the privacy receipt shows a code the phone's camera opens, so the address need not be typed. It is drawn on this computer (no service, no download) and only for an address the notebook itself shows.
- Phone: a note changed on one device shows on the other within seconds. The notes list asks every 15 seconds while it is on screen, and at once when you come back to it, which notes changed and redraws only those; a note open as a page on the phone takes the new text, and a note you are editing keeps yours (Save still offers Keep mine or Take theirs).
- Phone: after the computer chooses Allow for a new phone, the phone's lock screen opens by itself. It waits up to three minutes, saying so on the button, and stops if you change the password field.
- Help: the Guide's phone answer says an iPhone's browser needs Local Network on and a VPN or ad-blocking app (AdGuard's local VPN) paused when the phone cannot connect.
- Memory: the search model is let go after an hour with no search or filing and loads again on the next one, freeing about 115 MB; Settings, Background tasks, Let the search model go after an idle hour keeps it loaded.
- Internals: the whiteboard and file routes now hand their work to two services (`whiteboard/service.py`, `files/service.py`); nothing a person sees changes.
- Background work: a model download, a re-index, a pass you started and an autonomous pass now pick up again after the app is closed part way, and Settings, Running now updates as jobs change instead of on a timer.
- Help text: nineteen long explanations across the app are now one or two short lines, and the long hints beside Settings menus fold behind their '?' like the others.
- Settings kept in this browser: every saved choice is now written through one place that never throws, so a private window or a full browser storage no longer breaks the control that saved it; the quick note outbox and the notification list still say when a save was refused.
- Mind map: a topic added under one on a left-hand branch now starts to its left, under its last sibling, instead of back on the trunk side (it stayed there on a Free map). Launcher banners in `start.sh` and `start.bat` read Tessellate.
- The tagline under the Tessellate name in the launchers, the Windows splash and the Linux desktop entry reads "your notes, pieced together".

- Mind map: a topic added under one you had dragged (on any layout, Timeline included) is placed beside it instead of in the layout's own column far across the map. A topic added under one on a left-hand branch now starts to its left, under its last sibling, instead of back on the trunk side (it stayed there on a Free map). Launcher banners in `start.sh` and `start.bat` read Tessellate.

- Launcher: `doctor`, `reinstall` and `tools` are one double-click each, as `.sh` and `.bat`: the machine check, a rebuild of the Python environment that asks first and leaves notes alone, and a menu of every launcher action.
- Notes: a note with fewer than three tags shows a quiet "+ Tag" after its tags. It opens up to three suggested tags as one-press chips above a field for your own, and its menu has "Don't suggest tags for this note" (Undo in the notice, and "Suggest tags for this note again" in the same menu).
- Settings: sizes are the device's own. Zoom, Text size, Density, the companion's size and place, the chat box's height and the whiteboard's panel places are no longer copied to your notebook or applied from it, so changing the zoom or the companion's size on a computer leaves a phone as it was (colours, themes and fonts still follow you). They are marked On this device in Settings, Appearance, and a saved look no longer carries them.
- Whiteboard: one colour menu for every board colour. A shape's Fill and Border sit side by side, labelled, on its bar and in the Format panel; the menu names which one you are setting, with Same as fill (or Same as border) and Swap as one Undo each. Recent holds your last eight picks on this device above the palette, and Pick from the board is an eyedropper: the next click takes a colour from a shape (its fill, or its border with Alt or Take a shape's border), a line, a text box or any colour button, without opening that button's menu. Setting a border to its fill is two clicks.
- Whiteboard: the Format panel with several items selected shows only what they all share, a value they differ on reads Mixed (a striped colour, an empty number, a list reading Mixed, a half-ticked box), and one change sets it on all of them as one Undo.
- Whiteboard: nine more shapes in the Shapes flyout, drawn by dragging: rounded rectangle, ellipse, hexagon, parallelogram, star, cylinder, cloud, speech bubble and block arrow. Each is filled and takes text like the others, and the command palette finds them by name.
- Whiteboard: more line ends. Open triangle and filled circle join the lists (seventeen ends, crow's foot named), a plain line shows Start and End before it has an end, the Format panel takes them for a drawn line, and the Line and Arrow tools choose the mark as well as which ends.
- Whiteboard: an undone delete of a shape kept off every layer restores it exactly, with no empty layer field added.
- Library, Files: the "Text extracted from this file" box grows with its text up to about a page (the smaller of 28rem and 55% of the window height) instead of showing a line and a half.
- Composer: more of the owner's typing is read as meant ("ot to" as "it to", "ther" before a date as "the", "ehte", "ist", "tis own", "restert", "typeos", "linal", "cor workspace", "abutton", "it liks" as "it likes").
- The "Connect a model in Settings" button in the no-model notice keeps a visible border, so it reads as a button.
- Shortcuts: the m menu has "OCR workspace" under Go to, key o, opening the reader the way the Library does.
- Code editor: the assistant sidebar's Quick fix, Format, Run tests and Find usages buttons are an even two-by-two grid of equal width instead of wrapping three and one.
- Notes: "Show more" and "Show less" under a long note now sit flush with the text and are as wide as their label, so the focus ring hugs them instead of spanning the card.
- Themes: nine more accents (coral, gold, forest, navy, cyan, berry, olive, copper, lavender), and every accent's button text now reads at 4.5:1 or better in both modes (7 of 30 were under it in dark). A custom accent is toned per mode, and a pick that would read under 4.5:1 is refused with the nearest shade that passes, one press to use it.
- Themes: Parchment and Ember in dark read a little brighter in muted text and a little softer in accent tints, so a selected row's grey words and an accent label pass 4.5:1. Every look now measures 0 low-contrast surfaces in light and dark (was 151 across eight looks).
- Themes: two new looks, Midnight and Rosewood; the muted text and inner surfaces of Ember, Parchment, Mono, Plum, Sage, Ocean and Lagoon are retoned for contrast.
- Background art: four lighter styles (dusk, ripples, fireflies, rain), and the style list is now a row of cards, lightest first, each with a preview and its measured cost (Light, Medium or Heavy, and the milliseconds a frame). Constellation draws fewer stars so no style passes 2ms a frame.
- Themes: Classic and Quiet utilitarian are pinned by a test (their palettes, cards and presets), so the theme work cannot change them.
- Other devices: each network is one row in the trusted and untrusted lists, named by its Wi-Fi name with its address range under it. The same router read with and without its address range (Windows' quick fallback) was two trusted networks; it is one, Stop trusting and Forget take both records, and Trust still moves only records known to be the same router. A row's Stop trusting, Trust and Forget stay on screen rather than appearing on hover, and its name starts with a capital.
- Other devices: a wifi icon in the status bar says whether a phone on this network can open the app (open, closed on this network, or off) and changes as soon as the wifi drops or you join a network you have not trusted. Pressing it, or Alt+L, opens the switch, the address, Trust this network and two lists: trusted networks with Stop trusting and Forget, and untrusted ones with Trust and Forget (a sheet on a phone-sized window). Settings lists untrusted networks too, and a notice says when it switched itself off after 14 days unused.
- Security: other devices on this network turn on and off while the app runs, with no restart; off closes the port, drops every open connection and signs every other device out. The certificate is made again when this computer's address changes (joining a phone's hotspot), losing Wi-Fi and mobile data closes the port within seconds, a network you stop trusting stays closed, a phone connecting is a row on the privacy receipt, a phone can no longer loosen the network options or allow the network it is on, LAN access switches itself off after 14 days unused, and a phone's note never starts the search-by-meaning install on the computer (it waits until someone at the computer uses the app).
- Security: a phone is never the desktop app: it downloads exports to itself (it used to write them onto the computer and open Explorer there), and Settings dims what only the computer can do with one line saying so. It can no longer download or remove models, switch the search model, write files into the exports folder, open the recovery key dialog, turn other devices on, make a new certificate, stop asking for the password on open, or turn on web search, updates, SearXNG or auto-install, or change where the computer looks for SearXNG or saves exports; it can still turn each off. A notebook with no password answers no other device, the network port sends HSTS, and on a phone the model cards' Download and Remove are dimmed and a backup's Restore is left out.
- Settings, Recent changes: every row can be undone. A setting that was never set is put back to its default (the notebook now accepts `unset` on a settings save), and a value too big for the browser to store is held for as long as the page stays open.
- Making a space no longer reloads the page: the menu updates in place and the step goes on the Undo bar (Undo moves anything put in it to the default space and removes it; Redo makes it again), with an "Open it" action on the notice.
- Undo after accepting a link type or a name merge from the suggestions inbox now also takes away what the accept taught the notebook, and Redo teaches it again.
- Fixed: Ctrl+Z on the Notes tab (or any tab but the board) walked the last board's history instead of the app's steps, and Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z, Ctrl+Z on a Mermaid import or any several-shape step left a shape behind, because items brought back reuse the ids just deleted.
- Undo and Redo have no gaps left: deleting a picture or a file, a past question, what the notebook learned, a board library, the cut-off tail of an edited chat question, a dismissed tidy merge or tension, a renamed [[name]] rewrite, a graph pin, a topic rename, a map's theme, layout and numbering, branch cuts and reversals, imports and new boards, a space rename, a recording and a stand-alone capture or clip each carry an Undo with a working Redo. The server keeps what a delete took in an undo bin for two weeks. A ratchet fails any step without a Redo.
- Undo and Redo reach every write: a note made from a chat answer, a web page, the map or a wiki link, a draft published, an image or a link reason removed, links made on the map or from a suggestion, bulk tags, bookmarks (add, edit, regroup, mark read), restoring and unarchiving from the Library, Library bulk deletes, document and file renames, reminders made from a selection, a margin card or a chat answer, memories, learned claims, kinds of link, note types and categories each put a step on the Undo bar, with a working Redo. Ctrl+Z outside a text box runs the same stack. A new test (`tests/test_undo_coverage.py`) reads every write the app sends and fails on one that offers no Undo and is not on its shrinking list of reasons.
- Atlas has three ways or more to hold its lower body, hair and nebula stream for every pose, and a pose it takes again never repeats the way it took last time (Brief 88).
- The companion has two more ways onto the screen: it drops in from above onto its perch with a squash and a bounce (Atlas drifts down, swaying), or tumbles in from the nearer side in a roll. Every place but a hang under a bar now has three ways in or more, never the last one twice (Brief 88).
- Atlas juggles three of its stars, reads its star map and floats cross-legged to meditate now and then: three acts drawn for it long ago that nothing ever played (a switch for them in Appearance, What it does on its own).
- Companion: its large view has a row of things to ask of it (wave, cheer, hop, stretch, shrug, wiggle, and Atlas's own three), each played at once, waking it first if it sleeps.
- Atlas: what it holds or wears reads against its body: each prop (a bell, the moon on its ear, its lenses, a book's pages, juggled stars, the broken link) has a dark keyline, 4 to 1 or more, the moon is drawn larger, and resting the pointer on the companion names what it has on and why.
- Companion: no snap as a move starts or stops: a walk's legs, body and head ease into their stride and out of it, a move cut short in a landing or a float's lean eases out of it, and an act's start no longer drops the body's lean in one frame.
- Companion: every act has three manners (brisk, easy with its weight on one foot, full with a give at the knees) and every walk or float three strides, never the same as the last time.
- The companion's large view opens on its own resting limbs: Atlas hanging from a panel no longer shows both arms up in the large view while they swing down.
- Atlas: an arm raised out (a wave when you click it, a lifted arm) bends its forearm up towards its head instead of letting it hang down from the elbow; a wave holds the forearm about upright.
- Companion: thrown, it flies. It carries on at the speed it was let go (the pointer's last 80ms, by mouse or touch), falls under gravity, bounces off the window's edges and the floor, leans into the throw, squashes as it lands and stays where it comes down. It used to slide on for a quarter of a second and take a perch the tab chose, which could be back on the side it came from. Reduce motion crossfades to the same landing.
- Documents: the Python runtime loads once per session. The Python runner page is one hidden frame kept across documents and warmed when a Python document opens, so a second document runs in about 0.2 s instead of 5 to 7 s and the first run is quick once you have read the file. Another document's console never sees the last one's variables.
- First run: optional packages picked in Setup install on the first launch as one Background task (progress, each package, Stop); a list the app could not start yet (another install running) is kept for the next launch instead of being deleted.
- First run: an empty or partly downloaded model folder is no longer treated as installed. Settings, Search and index and Packages show "Files missing" with Reinstall, and when the search model's files are incomplete the app repairs them itself as a visible Background task ("Fixing search by meaning", with Stop, at most twice a launch) instead of failing with a broken-cache error.
- First run: the filing warm-up only loads a model that is installed, and a fresh install first chooses its chat model from the installed ones (one rule shared with the launch step), so a default nobody chose no longer reports "llama3.2 failed".
- Stop on a skill run now refuses a write the model asked for while Stop was landing, instead of only stopping between steps.
- Undo the run on an agent run now takes its writes off the Ctrl+Z stack and removes the rows' own Undo, so a later Ctrl+Z no longer re-runs an inverse already applied.
- Exports of private notes and of more than one space are tested for all four formats (a space's export carries only that space, All spaces carries every one, a locked vault exports neither words nor ciphertext).
- A reminder's Done and Snooze buttons on a notification still on screen survive an app restart: the signing key is kept in the data folder (reminder_token.key) and replaced only when the notebook is locked.
- The timeline no longer stays at 100 rows when the range changes while the rest of the first page is loading.
- The reminder edit form has an Alert menu: change the early alert or clear it (it could only be set by words), and Undo puts the old one back.
- A monthly or yearly repeat remembers its day: ticking off a reminder from the 31st lands on 28 February, then 31 March, 30 April (it used to stay on the 28th for good).
- Importing a folder export restarts the bin clock: a note binned long ago was purged by the next startup sweep before it could be looked at (Brief 101b).
- New Tessellate logo: three cells, the last one settling into place.
- Ask and Chat with no model: "how many days until the dentist" counts to the day your dentist note names ("Ten days from today, on 21 October, going by your note: ...") and "how long until mum's birthday" to the next 3 December; "what is still open on the harbor launch" lists only the unticked checklist items ("Two of three items are still open on Harbor launch"); "list my work notes" lists the notes in Work (or tagged work), newest first, each one a link; a comparison opens with its counts and goes straight to the two sides. A note's "booked for 21 October" and "on the 14th of November" are read as the days they name, not last year's or this month's 14th.
- Chat with no model: every one of the agent's 70 tools reports what it did in sentences, with a list or a table and its counts, a link to each note, document or board it names and a next-step link (Open it, Show all notes); a tool that fails says so plainly and where to go next ("I could not find note 42." then a link to Notes), never its raw result. Asking for a list in your own words, typos and all, reaches it: "shwo me evry tag i hav plz", "which docs do i have", "any reminders", "how big is my notebook" (30 of 30 phrasings, from 12). The newest-notes answer links each note by its name and says "from today" rather than "on today".
- Ask, Chat and the Guide, with no model: "I think so", "good plan" and "nice idea" are answered as agreement rather than searched for; "what do I know about rust" no longer quotes a note that says "rest" (a dictionary word is never put right to a note's word); "what are my notes about sourdough" is about sourdough, in the answer and its next-question chip; the Guide says how it read a misspelt question and answers it as it answers the spelled one ("hwo do i set a remnder" gets the three steps). Reminders: a monthly reminder set on the 31st comes back on the 31st after February, not the 28th from then on.
- Ask and Chat: call Atlas anything, a nickname or a word you just made up ("hey lil bro, what's on today", "what's due this week, broski", "brotatockiibidyrizzler what did I say about the dentist"): the name comes off before the question is read, so it is never searched or corrected, while "what did I say about Bro the dog" still asks about Bro. A message that is only a name ("yo brotato") is a call, answered with a short reply and three things to ask as chips. 38 of 38 gold messages read, 14 of 14 controls left whole.
- Ask and Chat, with no model: replies vary. Every family of small talk has eight phrasings or more in both voices, in more than one shape, and a reply never repeats or opens like any of the last three: over 50 replies a family, distinct openers 0.82 to 1.00, shape changes 0.60 to 1.00, repeats 250 to 0. Nothing found is said eight ways or more a voice and an answer's opener is never one of the last three answers': over 50 unanswerable questions in one chat, distinct openers 0.25 to 1.00. "I'm happy" is no longer met with "I'm sorry to hear that", and "i'm tired" and "you're useless" are no longer read as "ok".
- Ask and Chat: "where is the bin", "I can't find dark mode", "how do I get to backups" say where it is and give a Show me link that opens the place and rings the control, for every row of Tools and features, every Settings section and every tab (143 places); two near readings are offered as a choice, one link each. 40 gold questions with typos, 40 opened.
- Search, Ask and Chat: British and American spellings find each other both ways (colour and color, organise and organize, centre and center, travelled and traveled; 2,240 pairs), read at query time in search and in the composer, and an answer keeps the note's own spelling. Typos are read in context: a slip that is still a word ("insanely god", "its use" for "it's use", "intractable results") and a long misspelt word ("knowledgable", "speach", "infoa dn") are mended before the question is answered. Dates and units in an answer ("today" in a note, a lift's "90 kg", a count's figure) are read by the app's one date and unit reader rather than three more of their own.
- Ask, with no model: a dated note in shorthand is told as what you did that day, not under its date ("On 8 September, you squatted 80 kg for 5 and benched 60 kg for 5, going on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays"; "On 30 August, you planned the Lisbon trip for May"); "three weeks on" is followed by "by 2 October", never a second "on".
- Ask and Chat: questions about the app's own records are answered from them, with times on your clock: "what did I search yesterday" lists that day's questions (a question asked again is said once, with how many times) and offers History; "what ran overnight" lists each job from 18:00 to 09:00 with how it went; "when did I last back up" gives the time, how long ago and how many backups are kept, and a failed try after it. Notebook stats puts each labelled line on its own line.
- Ask, with no model: every note in an overview is told in its own sentence rather than under its heading ("In your first psych lecture, on 22 July, you learned that memory is reconstructive rather than a recording, and you set yourself chapters 1 to 3 of the Myers textbook to read before 27 July"; "At the Data Structures lab on 4 August you got linked lists working, though you were still shaky on big O"); "before next week" is said as the day it meant, "a week later" names its day, an open plan is said once in its own line (the row under the answer only asks Is that open plan right?), and an offer whose day has gone by drops it ("Remind you to ask the tutor about big O?"). The first question after a launch no longer waits for the search model: 27.28 s before, 0.34 s now, reading words while the model loads and saying so in Why.
- Ask and Chat, with no model: sums in words ("12 times 7", "2 to the power of 8"), roots, a list's average, median, total, largest or smallest, a time in one city read in another ("9am London in Tokyo"), "days until christmas", the days in a month and an age are worked out, each with a Read as line; the time somewhere reads "It's 18:31 in Perth, Western Australia (AWST, UTC+8)"; "notebook stats" opens with the count and span, then the most filed category and busiest month, and offers Statistics as a link. 60 phrasings, 60 answered.
- Ask, with no model: a note with a dated event ("Uni starts back next week") is told as what happened, its time said from today ("you're back at uni next week" that week; "you went back to uni the week of 20 July" months on), with the note's other facts in the same sentence ("and you mentioned you're doing Intro to Psychology and Data Structures this semester, with classes on Tuesdays and Thursdays"), cited once for all of them.
- Ask and Chat: a numbered mark's preview asks Is this line right? Not right leaves those sentences of the note out of every answer from the next one on (and any pattern quoting them); Confirm pins them as true, said as your word with the day. Both go on the undo stack and list in Settings, What it learned, as Marked wrong or Pinned as true; a model reads the notes with the same verdicts.
- Ask: Why this answer, under every answer, opens the lines that made it with the seconds each landed at: what the question was read as, what was searched and how many notes matched, who wrote it (Atlas from your notes, or the model by name and whether it was handed the app's own answer), its shape, how many notes it cites and how long it took.
- Ask and Chat with a model running: "can you search the web?" and "Summarise this" are answered by the model, with the app's own line or the open note handed to it as context; the app answers them itself only with no model, or when Ask is set to From your notes. Nothing searches the web for the question either way.
- Ask: the ... beside Copy keeps an answer as a note, a document titled with the question, or a mind map of the notes it cites; each goes on the undo stack.
- Settings, Personas: What Atlas adds of its own is Nothing, One line (the default) or Everything it finds. With no model, an answer about a topic can end with a pattern measured in your notes (a plan no later note picks up, a subject that keeps coming up, a change of mind), never one the answer already said; Ask now shows Confirm and Not right under it, as Chat does, and each Not right raises the bar for the next.
- Ask and Chat with no model: answers now join their facts rather than list them. An overview opens with where you have got to ("and you're leaning towards the Logitech", "with one thing still open"); lines say how they follow on ("a week later, you tried the Viper", "though you're still shaky on big O") and what no single note says (the $30 between two prices, a trip seven months away, $84 against your $100 aim); and a closing line says how the notes sit in time (stale, one burst, or a steady habit). Wordings vary from question to question; every clause comes from the notes or their dates.
- Ask and Chat: "Summarise this" sums up what is open, the note you are editing or last opened, point by point, or the category the sidebar is filtered to; with nothing open it says so rather than listing your newest notes. "summarise Travel" and "what's in Travel?" read every note in that category, not only the few a keyword search finds.
- Ask and Chat with no model: when one word means two unrelated things in your notes (python in Coding and python in Pets, split evenly and sharing no other word), the answer takes the newer reading, says where the other one is, and offers one chip to ask about it. With no tie there is no chip.
- Ask and Chat with no model: a follow-up that is a question of its own ("what about running?", "and Oppenheimer?") is answered in the same shape as the first; "no, the data structures one" stays chosen for the next "shorter"; "tell me more" once everything is said says so ("That's all your notes say on psych so far: one note") instead of "Nothing in the notes found answers that"; and "what did I think of Dune?" no longer repeats the rating inside the title.
- Ask and Chat: your own abbreviations are learned from your notes. When a note says "Human Computer Interaction (HCI)", or names Cloud Computing beside CC, asking about CC also finds the notes that spell it out, and "what does CC stand for?" is answered from the note that told it, with no model and no dictionary.
- Ask with no model: "what have I saved about pottery?" now counts every note on the topic rather than the first five found; a long answer shows five lines and a Show more for the rest, each cited; #tags and "today" in a note no longer reach the answer ("trimmed your first bowl" under its day); and the words read in a picture are quoted only when you ask what it says or it has no caption.
- Ask and Chat with no model: an answer's shape now follows its question. A count leads with its figure drawn large, "who is Sam?" is a card, "Logitech or Razer?" is a table of price, what you found and your notes, and "what do I need to buy?" is a checklist you can save as a note.
- Settings, Personas: How Atlas sounds with no model is now Warm and concise (the default), Neutral, Playful or Plain, with a live sample; the facts are the same in each, and a chat no longer opens five answers the same way.
- Ask and Chat with no model: an answer now ends with what the facts mean ("It's the only week you've written down", "Nothing on bench since September") and one offer for its kind you press to do (a reminder, a weekly reminder, a list or a table as a note), with Undo; "this week" in an old note is said as the week it meant.
- Chat with web search on: a search that found pages always answers, a line a page; the pages sit in a Web results fold under the answer, each with its site and one line, and a title opens the page to read right there.
- Ask and Chat: "can you search the web?", "can you do maths?" or "what can you do?" is answered about the app, whether and how, and whether its switch is on, never searched for, with or without a model.
- Ask and Chat with no model: an answer about your notes now reads like a person wrote it, the count and the days first, the facts under bold labels in your terms, what the notes do not cover, and one offer you can press (a reminder, a checklist); no bracketed dates, quote bars, Grounded in chips or count under it.
- New Tessellate logo: three cells, the last one settling into place.
- Security: an action refused from another device now reads "Not available on this device. Do it on the computer MemoryMap runs on."
- Renamed to Tessellate; formerly MemoryMap AI. Every title, window, shortcut, help page, document and the website say Tessellate; your notes, settings and data folder stay where they were, and the repository moved to github.com/Braydenh563/Tessellate (the old address redirects).
- Security: an action refused from another device now reads "Not available on this device. Do it on the computer Tessellate runs on."
- Security: a phone or another computer on the network can no longer make this computer act. Opening a folder, restarting or quitting the app, installing or running software (extras, updates, SearXNG), importing a folder of this computer's files, changing the model server and restoring a whole backup now answer "Only this computer can do that" to any other device.
- Other devices: on a network you have not allowed (a cafe, a hotel, or one this computer cannot identify), other devices stay out until you choose Allow on this network; turning the switch on remembers the network you are on, Windows' public networks are never opened without asking, and Allow on any network (off, password-gated) restores the old behaviour. Only addresses on your own network can reach the port at all.
- Other devices: a phone signing in for the first time waits for this computer to say yes: a notice with Allow and Deny appears here and in the bell, and Settings, Other devices lists the allowed devices and networks with Remove. Ask before a new device signs in is on by default.
- Other devices: the address a phone types is shown on its own line, large, with Copy, and the rest under Other addresses (virtual adapters left out), in Settings and the privacy receipt alike; the lock screen on a phone offers Install the certificate with the iPhone steps.
- Dashboard: without a model the welcome line is composed: seven times of day (small hours to late evening) with seven or eight lines each, weekday lines (a new week, Friday, the weekend), and lines from your notebook (a writing streak, a busy day, back after some days, the subject on your mind lately). It changes each hour and holds steady within one.
- Phone: Settings and every dialog fit the visible screen in Safari, with its toolbars showing, so the top, the close button and the bottom can be reached; a dialog taller than the screen scrolls instead of being centred off both edges.
- Logs: errors from scripts that are not the app's (Safari's own helpers and browser extensions, shown as "user-script" or a bare "Script error.") are no longer logged as the app's errors.
- Files tab on a phone: opening a file's extracted text no longer scrolls the library sideways (Copy text and Open reading wrap under each other instead of running 37px past the screen; the view was 414px wide in 364), and in the OCR workspace the reading's source chip stays on one line with an ellipsis instead of spilling out of its box.
- Whiteboard on a phone: pinching to zoom no longer moves a note. A second finger puts any drag back where it started and hands over to the zoom (a pinch that began on a note now zooms; before, the note moved up to 373px and a pinch from the note itself did not zoom at all), and a finger must travel 8px before it carries a note, text box or shape; a mouse is unchanged.
- Phone: the chat composer stays above the keyboard. The keyboard strip is read again as a field takes focus (iOS sometimes sends no resize), a pinch zoom no longer counts as a keyboard, and the no-model line steps aside while the keyboard is up; on a phone that line is tidier too (its action lines up with the words, 93px tall instead of 109). The viewport also asks for resizes-content, which Chrome on Android honours.
- Other devices: a second notebook on the same computer (another person's account) takes the next free port for phones (8444 and up) instead of staying on that computer only; Settings shows the address it took.
- Notifications: the circle and cross on each row sit at its right edge, centred on the row, and stay drawn, instead of at the bottom beside the time.
- Graph: tapping the settings button on a phone no longer opens the Layout dropdown by itself. A sheet that opens under a finger lands focus on the sheet, not on its first select.
- Graph: on a phone the note panel's actions are one row (Open, Link and a ⋯ whose rows are named in words) instead of three rows of unlabelled icons, and the New note button no longer floats over the panel.
- Companion: it steps off a dock's open "more" menu (Notes' Reload, Manage tags and the rest), and any open menu or list, instead of standing over it.
- Other devices: a phone's page no longer stalls. Safari opens connections ahead of need and sends nothing on them, and each held one of eight waiting threads for ten seconds, so the page's real requests queued behind them; one watcher now waits on every new connection. A computer on a global IPv6 address keeps the phone's trust when that address changes within its network, and the phone help says nothing installs on the phone.
- Settings, Help: the search box and its count sit under Welcome and tours, above the topics they filter.
- Chat: every message shows when it was written, muted at the end of its line (the time today, "Yesterday 14:05", the weekday within a week, the date after that, the full date and time on hover), in your locale; the server stamps each message as it is saved, and a chat saved before this shows none. The chat list reads its time from the last message.
- Restart: Settings' Restart works however the app was started (the Windows app, start.bat or start.sh), not only the desktop app; the new copy waits for the old one to close before it opens, so it no longer hands off to the closing copy and stops, and the page reloads by itself when the app is back. Other devices shows a Restart now button when a change needs one.
- Other devices: a phone can now trust the notebook for good. The certificate is a small authority made on this computer, limited to your own network, signing the server certificate (an address change no longer asks the phone again); Trust this certificate on your phone downloads it without a sign-in error; and an address typed without https is sent on to https instead of failing.
- Graph: the map opens where you left it and fades in, rather than spreading out from the centre; while the first map is on its way the card breathes a soft glow instead of standing empty.
- Graph: hovering a note eases the highlight, the dimming and the labels in and out; Reduce motion and Performance mode switch them at once.
- Graph: adding, hiding or filtering notes moves the map from where it is, new notes grow in beside their neighbours, and notes that leave fade out with their links.
- Graph: notes have a faint shade and a crisp rim in their own colour, the glow is unchanged, and the note whose card is open wears a ring.
- Graph: Fit and the first view centre the map on the canvas (the minimap and zoom buttons no longer push it to the right), and fit, zoom, pan and Locate glide; with less motion asked for they cut.
- Graph: a note you drag and drop stays where you put it while the map settles round it.
- Dashboard: the notebook constellation keeps its room while it loads and fades in, so nothing below it jumps.
- Ask and the Guide: a misspelt word anywhere in a question is read as the word it is near ("redeisgn", "noficiations", "westen australia"), split words are joined ("thes ebuttons", "a nd"), a missing apostrophe is read ("doesn follow"), and a stray semicolon inside a word or two words run together are put right ("natura;l", "thenthe"); the Guide, the clock and the other utilities read the repaired question.
- Graph: a small pull on a note moves its neighbours a little and settles at once, instead of reheating the whole map.
- Quick sketch: the tool bar is a single row of 32px tools with no group labels (names are in tooltips), the ink is one chip that opens its colours, and the bar is a third of its height on a phone.
- Back and forward list: Clear this list is a quiet text action in a footer beside the older-steps count, not a bordered button with a trash icon.
- Back and forward list: each row's remove cross sits inside the row's highlight rather than past it.
- Dashboard: changing theme no longer collapses the notebook constellation for a frame or restarts its drift, so it keeps its shape while it fades.
- Agent: with no model its button says it runs the app's own tools only, and the first time you choose it a line under the box says the same.
- Timeline: the years are one menu beside the month picker rather than a chip row of their own.
- Chat: the settings button in the bottom dock has the same rounded-square corner as the other icon buttons.
- Start-up: the bell's panel and the meeting recorder's buttons load the first time they are used, and 89 Library-only style rules load with the Library; the app starts with about 3.2 KB less script and 1.5 KB less style (gzipped).
- Notes: pressing Save before the settings have loaded no longer fails silently.
- Mind maps, drafts, web clips, voice notes, transcripts, OCR text, new linked notes and chat answers saved as notes are filed in the background, like Capture's: a mind map's new topic took the filing model's whole answer (4.7 s measured against a 4 s model) and now appears in 0.3 s.
- First run: "Connect a model" on the welcome opens Settings and the recovery-key offer waits until Settings is closed, instead of drawing over it.
- Start-up: opening the app with no notes waiting no longer lists a "Filing a note" job in Activity and the bell, a new row on every launch.
- Start-up: the quick-add reader warms up after sign-in instead of on the lock screen, so a launch with a password no longer logs two 401 errors.
- Ask and the Guide: a misspelt word anywhere in a question is read as the word it is near ("redeisgn", "noficiations", "westen australia"), split words are joined ("thes ebuttons", "a nd"), and a missing apostrophe is read ("doesn follow"); the Guide, the clock and the other utilities read the repaired question.
- Ask: an answer to a question that needed a spelling repair opens by saying how it was read ("I took that to mean ..."), in wording that changes from one answer to the next.
- Settings: Import & export has Clear and forget (recent searches in every box, saved previews, the Guide's conversation, dismissed suggestions), each saying how much it removes and each undoable for ten seconds.
- Settings: every change and clear is undoable from its toast and listed with its Undo in Recent changes (the last twenty).
- Search: every search box suggests as you type (recent searches, then note titles, tags and categories) with the best match in grey; Tab or Right takes it. A recent search has its own x and a Clear recent searches, and Settings, General, Search turns suggestions off.
- Notes: unsaved edits kept on this device are no longer dropped when the app restarts and starts up while still locked; the offer to open them comes back after you sign in.
- OCR workspace: finding in what was read marks every match in the text, the current one stronger and scrolled into view, counts occurrences ("3 of 15"), and steps with Enter, Shift+Enter or two buttons.
- Settings: Filing style is the same row heading as Categories and Tags (one element, one type); a lint holds every row head to it.
- Hover grounds: a link-like row's hover ground keeps its rounded corners (a lint and a sweep, `hoverradius.js`, hold it).
- Notifications: a notice's actions sit on their own row under its message, left-aligned with it, so the close button is alone in its corner.
- Notes, Select mode: the tick sits in the card's left gutter on the first line instead of stacking a row above the title (cards and rows keep their height).
- Library: flicking quickly through the sub-tabs no longer flashes the other kind's tiles or jumps the layout (Images and Files redraw from what is loaded, an overtaken load never draws, placeholders are tile-sized).
- Search by meaning: Settings, the command palette, Help, the manual and the Guide find a thing by another word for it or a slip in its name ("trash" is the bin, "the little guy in the corner" the companion, "chnage pasword" the password); with an embedding model on, Settings and the palette add a Close in meaning list.
- Settings: on a phone, a long matching setting no longer widens the results list past the screen.
- Autocorrect in notes, chat, Ask and titles: a clear typo is fixed as you finish the word, underlined for five seconds (click it to put the word back), Backspace or Ctrl+Z straight after undoes it and the toast carries Undo; never in code, links, tags or search; one switch in Settings, General, Writing.
- Tidy: a review opens under a quiet back link with its name as the heading; an empty review is one line with no selection bar; Recent runs is a quiet disclosure row instead of a bordered box.
- Focus timer: a ring with the time large, 5, 15, 25 and 50 minute lengths plus a stepper, one Start and Pause button, a chime and a notification at the end, optional breaks, and today's focused minutes.
- Voice notes: Enhance on save (on by default, in the Microphone fold and Settings) cuts low rumble and evens the loudness of the kept audio on this computer; the original is kept until the transcript is saved.
- Voice notes: the level line is the microphone's real signal, and with reduced motion it is a still level bar.
- Voice notes: with the captions helper, the words appear in the recorder as you speak; the full transcript replaces them after.
- Live captions: a Captions button in Library, Recordings and a Live captions button in the voice note, and the Guide answers "how do I get live captions".
- Voice notes: the recorder is one large Record and Stop control with the clock beside it and the microphone as a chip; after saving it shows the transcript's first lines with Open.
- Microphone: choose the input, and switch noise suppression, echo cancellation and automatic gain, with a live level and a three-second test, in the recorder and in Settings, General; dictation, recordings and live captions all use them.
- Recordings: each recording is a card with a playhead, the time ("1:12 / 4:30") and drag to seek; M or the pin marks a moment with a comment, listed under the player and linked to the transcript.
- Voice notes: closing the recorder keeps recording in a small bar with the clock, Pause, Stop and Open; transcription runs in the background with its progress on the card, a Stop, and a notification when it is done or fails.
- Ask, with no model: a dated note in shorthand is told as what you did that day, not under its date ("On 8 September, you squatted 80 kg for 5 and benched 60 kg for 5, going on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays"; "On 30 August, you planned the Lisbon trip for May"); "three weeks on" is followed by "by 2 October", never a second "on".
