- Ask and Chat with no model: a follow-up that is a question of its own ("what about running?", "and Oppenheimer?") is answered in the same shape as the first; "no, the data structures one" stays chosen for the next "shorter"; "tell me more" once everything is said says so ("That's all your notes say on psych so far: one note") instead of "Nothing in the notes found answers that"; and "what did I think of Dune?" no longer repeats the rating inside the title.
- Ask and Chat: your own abbreviations are learned from your notes. When a note says "Human Computer Interaction (HCI)", or names Cloud Computing beside CC, asking about CC also finds the notes that spell it out, and "what does CC stand for?" is answered from the note that told it, with no model and no dictionary.
- Ask with no model: "what have I saved about pottery?" now counts every note on the topic rather than the first five found; a long answer shows five lines and a Show more for the rest, each cited; #tags and "today" in a note no longer reach the answer ("trimmed your first bowl" under its day); and the words read in a picture are quoted only when you ask what it says or it has no caption.
- Ask and Chat with no model: an answer's shape now follows its question. A count leads with its figure drawn large, "who is Sam?" is a card, "Logitech or Razer?" is a table of price, what you found and your notes, and "what do I need to buy?" is a checklist you can save as a note.
- Settings, Personas: How Atlas sounds with no model is now Warm and concise (the default), Neutral, Playful or Plain, with a live sample; the facts are the same in each, and a chat no longer opens five answers the same way.
- Ask and Chat with no model: an answer now ends with what the facts mean ("It's the only week you've written down", "Nothing on bench since September") and one offer for its kind you press to do (a reminder, a weekly reminder, a list or a table as a note), with Undo; "this week" in an old note is said as the week it meant.
- Chat with web search on: a search that found pages always answers, a line a page; the pages sit in a Web results fold under the answer, each with its site and one line, and a title opens the page to read right there.
- Ask and Chat: "can you search the web?", "can you do maths?" or "what can you do?" is answered about the app, whether and how, and whether its switch is on, never searched for, with or without a model.
- Ask and Chat with no model: an answer about your notes now reads like a person wrote it, the count and the days first, the facts under bold labels in your terms, what the notes do not cover, and one offer you can press (a reminder, a checklist); no bracketed dates, quote bars, Grounded in chips or count under it.
- Voice: recordings transcribe again on installs where the audio library refused an option the speech model passed it.
- Attach: a picture's selection circle sits inside its corner.
- Running jobs and Activity: every answer, agent turn and background job is listed with a plain title, who started it and how long it took; each opens to its own timed lines, live while it runs.
- Status bar: one indicator says how many things are running and names the newest; it opens Activity.
- Notifications: a job's "Started" notice becomes its ending (finished, failed or stopped) in the same row.
- Backups: each backup says when in words, marks the newest Latest, and says what made it (the daily backup, Back up now, before an update or a restore), its size and whether it was checked; Restore and Delete are always shown.
- Where your data went: one row per place, saying what it was for (the file downloaded, the search words, the page clipped) and which feature reached it; the exact addresses are under Addresses.

- Ask: a question about notes in one category stays inside that category rather than widening into another.
- Board: a selected connector's bar has a Label button, so a connector's label no longer depends on knowing to press Enter.
- Board: a page in the Pages sidebar renames in place (double-click or F2, Enter keeps, Esc cancels, one Undo step) and its row has a menu with Rename, Fit to contents, Present from here and Delete.
- Board: double-click a frame's edge handle to fit that edge to what it holds with a 32-unit margin (a corner fits two, "Fit to contents" in its menu fits all four, one Undo step).
- Board: the Layers tab says how many items are selected on the board (with Clear), and a frame lists the items it holds under its own row, folded with an arrow.
- Board: a tool's kind popover (Line or Arrow, and the other shape pickers) opens above its options bar instead of under it.
- Mind maps: a line's label stays on the line while a topic is dragged and sits on its midpoint.
- Mind maps: while a topic's text is edited the format bar stays on the selection through a pan or zoom and never covers the text, and the topic's + and link buttons, fold toggle and resize grip step aside.
- Mind maps: a selected topic's + and link buttons now stand beside the topic and scale with it (28px at full size, 20px zoomed out), and only the + stays below half zoom.
- Mind maps: a topic's Shape, Text and Branch line menus open beside, above or below the topic instead of over it, so a change shows while the topic is still selected; the chosen option in them has one look and every reset one quiet icon.
- Backups: every start holds the backups folder to the number you keep, so a safety copy before an update no longer leaves one too many.
- Settings: the bar that marks a changed setting sits in the margin beside the row rather than on the text.
- Chat: with no model, Agent answers with the app's own tools first: the time in a named place ("what's the time in western australia"), a bare sum ("5 + 5"), your notebook's counts in any case, the notes on a topic, and "can you search the web?" (whether web search is on, and how to turn it on). The thinking line says "Working it out without a model…", never "Waking the model…".
- Chat: a stray backslash or a run of spaces is cleaned from the question and from every tool's one-line arguments; a search sent with no words searches the question's topic.
- Chat: with the Needle extra, a tool's result is said as the answer (the time, the sum, the counts, the notes found with a line each), never "its result is in the step above"; Needle is never offered a question to ask you.
- Agent: a question with only one choice is never shown and never retried; the agent answers or acts instead.
- Notes: the Select button in the top bar is a square icon button, like its neighbours, where its word is hidden.
- Links that hold an icon (the Questions group links, Read this in the Library, text links with an icon) underline their words and never the icon.
- OCR workspace: an image's saved description shows as soon as it opens, before and while it is read; a document page's comes with its stored reading, asked for beside the read.
- Dashboard: the Notebook constellation sits on an off-white well in light mode, and cross-fades when the theme changes (instant with animations off or reduced motion).
- Capture: with Line numbers on, the note box keeps the numbers' column from the first paint, so the text no longer moves on the first click.
- Documents: the code snippets panel's search field and Save button are one height, the button reads Save (its tooltip says what it saves), and the label no longer wraps.
- Ask: a badge with no text (the model and the search mode, before an answer arrives) is not drawn as an empty tinted box.
- Companion: Atlas's check for words underneath it counts only text that is drawn, so it no longer sits over the Ask answer's "You asked:" line in a notebook with a long history.
- Skills: every change a skill or the agent makes to a document, a board, a map or a saved skill is read back before it is reported as done, as notes, tags and reminders already were.
- Skills: a skill can cap its own tool calls and steps; a run that passes a cap stops, says which, and keeps its changes for Undo.
- Skills: with small model mode on, a skill measured as unreliable on small models is shown as needing a larger model, with the reason.
- Settings: your look follows you. Contrast, border style, shadow, avatar and Atlas looks, dashboard mark and the other appearance settings that were kept only in one browser are now kept in your notebook, so a second browser (or a desktop window that lost its storage) opens in the same look, and a theme or density changed in one shows in the other after a reload. Only performance mode stays with the machine, still marked This browser.
- Timeline: a third view, the calendar. A month (reminders and meetings with their titles and times, a day's page at the top of its day, a dot for each note), a week with hour rows, or a day; drag a reminder to another day or hour to move it, or press Alt and an arrow on it (Undo puts it back). The arrows walk the days, Page Up and Page Down the months, T is today, Enter opens the day in the feed and N starts a reminder on it. Below a tablet's width it is the month as a list.
- Reminders: Calendar opens the Timeline's calendar with only reminders (the tab's own month grid went), and More, Import a calendar (.ics) reads a calendar file as reminders, naming any event it skipped; Undo removes what it added.
- Timeline: a custom range now holds the notes that sit in it (a meeting on its date, a note on the day it mentions), not only the ones written in it.
- A note's name is plain words everywhere it is shown (a board's Layers row, the palette's sources, the graph panel, menus, toasts, link lists), not its first line with the Markdown marks still on it; the Dashboard's quoted lines too.
- Reminders: a high or low priority reads as a word beside the repeat, not only as a red edge; the List and Calendar view, the Open, All and Done filters and Select say they are on to a screen reader.
- Mind map: the progress count ("3/7") on a solid topic reads in the topic's own ink instead of grey on blue (1:1 before).
- Chat: the chosen Ask or Agent mode keeps a visible keyboard focus ring in the Utilitarian, Paper and Mono looks; a scrolling page and widget body leave room for the ring at their bottom edge; Settings, Background tasks, Run now keeps its ring inside its row on a phone.
- Dashboard: the day digest and the recent activity list read as lists to a screen reader; a task box on a note card says why it cannot be ticked there.
- Menus with settings in them (the Library's More, the Timeline's options) no longer have a wider gap at their top and bottom than at their sides.
- Pop-up notices: Undo and the other actions are quiet words in the accent colour rather than grey boxes, and a notice with its Undo stays on one line on a desktop.
- Help, Welcome and tours: each part of the app is a row with its name over what it covers, under one Start the tour button, instead of fourteen boxed buttons.
- Settings, Shortcuts: press a shortcut's keys to change it; the column of Change buttons is gone. Actions repeated on every row (Run now, Restore, a learned fact's Edit) are quiet text buttons, a Delete stays grey until you point at it, and a row of three or more keeps its first and puts the rest under ⋯.
- The notifications panel: each notice is one block, its time with read and remove beside it and its Undo at the end of the same line; a lapsed Undo says Undo expired; the unread dot is named for screen readers.
- The code editor: the assistant's question box, its send and its suggestion chips are one height, and the Python console's focus ring no longer touches the line above it. When the grammar checker cannot start, its message names the file that failed and why.
- Bars: the Ask box's and the chat strip's model pickers take the bar's quiet fill, the Library's Filter collapses to its icon on a phone as Notes' does, its view switch reads Rows then Cards, and the graph's filter headings say what a struck-through or outlined chip means.
- Buttons inside a card (the dashboard's widgets, the code editor's toolbar and its assistant's tools) are quiet: no box or edge until you point at or Tab to them; the code editor's Run is its one filled button; the night pass's "36 claims" lines are rows; the graph's link and property filters are chips, a hidden kind struck through.
- Every hover now shows the same way when you reach the control with Tab, and colour changes on hover run at the quick speed.
- Reminder notifications: Done and Snooze now work with a token scoped to that one reminder and those two actions (24 hours, signed by the server), instead of your whole session token sitting in the browser's notification store.
- The Guide's whiteboard keys, board library, board format and mind map features topics are each two shorter topics, so a question lands on the half it is about.
- Renaming a topic from the Library's Contents list or a note's panel in the graph has Save and Cancel beside the field (Enter saves, Escape cancels).
- Chat: a reminder (or new note, or pin) made from a chat message says what it did once, not twice; the card keeps Undo.
- Library: a map template's picture draws each branch in its own colour (the map's branch palette) instead of one grey.
- Whiteboard: an item on a hidden or locked layer has an eye or lock that says the layer decides (and a press says so); a link's hollow end (diamond, circle or square) stops the line at the shape's edge instead of drawing it through.
- Graph: a Tree, Radial or Arc map is named in the toolbar with a chip that opens the Layout choice, and notes leaving the picture fade out instead of vanishing.
- Connections: the Link button on an unlinked mention is a quiet row action (no edge, a tint on hover), the same in a document's panel.
- The dashboard's search bar answers hover with the same quiet box as every other button, not a coloured edge.
- The loading placeholder's shimmer follows the system's reduced-motion setting, unless Progress indicators is set to Always move on purpose.
- Dashboard: a new notebook starts in three steps (your name, typed in place; a first note; a first answer from your notes, which needs no AI model), each ticked when done and kept past the first note; saving the first note offers Ask about it. Try a sample notebook adds eight example notes once per notebook, and Remove the sample notes moves them to the bin.
- Help: the manual, every topic Atlas answers from on one page with contents, a search that keeps the topics holding every word, and print (Settings, Help, Open the manual, or the Guide's ... menu). Made from the Guide's own topics, so it cannot drift from the help.
- Settings: a setting changed from its default shows a bar at its edge and a reset at the end of its row, and a section with changes offers Reset N changes in its title bar; appearance settings kept only in this browser say This browser. Import & export, Your settings: export every setting as one .json file and import one back, each setting checked on its own, with what was skipped named and Undo.
- Whiteboard: a draw.io file with several pages comes in whole, each page in a frame named after it, side by side; the Pages tab lists them and Present walks them.
- Whiteboard: Edit data, as in draw.io: the Format panel's new Data tab keeps named values on a shape, connector, text box, picture, frame or table.
- Whiteboard: tables, as in draw.io: Insert, Table places a grid of text cells; double-click a cell to type, Tab to move on, and right-click to add or delete rows and columns or make the first row a header.
- Whiteboard: a hand-drawn look, as in Excalidraw: the View menu's Hand-drawn look draws every shape and connector with rough strokes, the same each time; one shape can differ from its Format panel.
- Whiteboard: a current layer, as in draw.io: press a named layer's name in Layers and everything new goes on it, drawn, typed, pasted or placed from the library.
- Mind maps: stamps and votes on a topic, as on a Miro board: its menu, Stamps, adds a vote, a heart, a star, an agree, a question or a hot, each with its count; press a stamp on the topic to add one more.
- Mind maps export as XMind (.xmind) from the export dialog, keeping notes, links, labels, callouts, priorities, tasks and each branch's structure; an XMind file imported now brings the same back.
- Mind maps: labels under a topic, as in XMind: its menu, Topic, Add labels… writes up to eight short tags, drawn as a row of chips under its words; the exports keep them.
- Mind maps: a topic can carry a callout, a few words in a bubble over it (its menu, Topic, Add a callout…); double-click the bubble to change it. The map makes room for it and the exports keep it.
- Mind maps: a branch can have its own structure, as in XMind: a topic's menu, Structure, lays the branch under it out as a logic chart, an org chart, a tree table, a timeline, a fishbone, both sides, a tree or radial while the rest of the map keeps its layout.
- Graph: changing the layout, a return to the tab or a saved view moves the notes from where they were, with the camera easing to the new frame (no more vanishing and reappearing); a tree, radial or arc fits the free space, notes new to the picture fade in, and topic outlines are drawn on the force layout only.
- Graph: the head's '?', settings and ⋯ menus close each other when one opens, so they no longer stack on top of each other (INBOX 796).
- Graph: a fresh open shows the layout settling again (the notes move into a frame already set on where they end, about a second, the same on a return to the tab), Fit fills the space the dock, legend, minimap, zoom strip and any open panel leave, a fitted map refits when a panel opens or closes, and a small map spreads so its dots have room (INBOX 775, 792).
- Each interaction has a time budget: boot to first paint, first interaction, list paint, search, opening a board of 500 objects and a document of 50,000 words, with the measured figure and the cap (1.5 times it) in the README's Performance table. CI fails when the server or the browser exceeds a cap, and `GET /models/bench/budgets?live=true` times the server's share against your own notebook.
- Reminders reach you with the app's window closed: the desktop app shows each due reminder once as your system's own notification (Windows, macOS, Linux), with Done and Snooze 10 minutes on Windows and on Linux where the notification service offers buttons; a click opens Reminders. Nothing is shown while the notebook is locked.
- In a browser or the installed app, a due reminder's notification now comes through the app's service worker: it shows in a background tab, stays after the tab closes, and has Done and Snooze 10 minutes on it.
- Meetings: Summarise finds the decisions and action items with no model, from lines saying decided, agreed, Action or TODO, or a name taking a task, each with its owner and day, and says so in one line; with a model on it rewords the same list.
- Library, Recordings: a transcribed recording lists its lines with their times under Transcript; press one to play from that moment. The menu downloads the transcript as SRT or VTT subtitles.
- Recordings: with the local AI on, a transcript's turns are labelled with who spoke, read from what was said (Name the speakers in the recording's menu does it again); with no model nothing is labelled.
- Documents: a code file has an Assistant (beside Run, replacing AI edit there) in the code panel: Explain, Fix the problem at the caret, Write tests, Refactor or a question, over the selected lines or the file; a change shows as a diff to Apply (one Ctrl+Z takes it out) or Reject. With no model, Fix uses the quick fix, Quick fix, Format, Run tests and Find usages work as they are, a question goes to the needle extra when installed, and the panel says what needs a model (INBOX 788).
- Documents: a code file has a Snippets button (beside Run) that opens a code panel beside the editor, a sheet on a phone: a built-in library and your own snippets by language and tag, a search, a row inserts at the caret (one Ctrl+Z takes it out), and Save selection keeps the selected code with #words in its name as tags; saving, renaming and deleting each undo; the Guide's new Code panel topic covers it (INBOX 788).
- Documents: a code file's editor uses the pane's width (1,090px at 1440, was 724px centred), capped only on ultrawide windows; prose keeps its measure (INBOX 788).
- Documents: New from a template has a Code group: a Python script with a test, a command line tool, a FastAPI endpoint, JavaScript with tests, an HTML page, a SQL schema, a README, a notebook of cells and the p5.js sketch, each opening in the code view as its own file type (INBOX 788).
- Graph: changing the layout, a return to the tab or a saved view moves the notes from where they were, with the camera easing to the new frame (no more vanishing and reappearing); a tree, radial or arc fits the free space, notes new to the picture fade in, and topic outlines are drawn on the force layout only.
- Graph: the head's '?', settings and ⋯ menus close each other when one opens, so they no longer stack on top of each other (INBOX 796).
- Graph: a fresh open shows the layout settling again (the notes move into a frame already set on where they end, about a second, the same on a return to the tab), Fit fills the space the dock, legend, minimap, zoom strip and any open panel leave, a fitted map refits when a panel opens or closes, and a small map spreads so its dots have room (INBOX 775, 792).
- Settings, Import & export: Export notebook folder downloads the whole notebook as a zip of markdown files, one per note with its attachments beside it and a .json file of every field, plus documents, boards and an index; From a MemoryMap folder reads it back with dates, pins, links, reminders and boards as they were.
- Every import keeps a report: what it read, wrote, skipped and found already here, each skipped file named with why; See the report when it ends, or Report in the Activity panel.
- A long import shows in the Activity panel with its progress and Stop; the notes it made before Stop stay.
- Translate this, in the command palette: a selected passage of a note, a document or a reading turned from English into Spanish on this computer with no model, then copied or put in place of the selection (Ctrl+Z undoes it). It needs "Translate offline", a 27 MB download in Settings, Packages (new bundle Languages); until it is installed the row says so and opens that page.
- Tag suggestions with no model are better and the same on every path (the note card, Tag and file with Atlas, Capture while typing): your own tags found under short or other forms ("stats", "running"), the title and first line first, linked notes' tags, nothing from quotations or a scan's footer, one spelling each, and a tag turned down on three notes offered less until Manage tags, Turned down, Offer again. On a 67-note set, the first suggestion right 0.687 to 0.791, suggestions shown right 0.769 to 0.861. Tag and file with Atlas now suggests tags with no model running.
- Whiteboard: a laser pointer while presenting (L, or the bar's button): the pointer leaves a short red trail that fades, and nothing is drawn on the board (INBOX 797).

- Whiteboard: find on a board now finds text boxes and shape and connector labels (text boxes were never found), and Ctrl+H (Edit, Find and replace) replaces across them in one undo step (INBOX 797).

- Whiteboard: named layers. The Layers tab's + puts the selection on a new layer; each layer's eye and lock hide or lock everything on it, and its menu moves the selection there, selects its items, renames or deletes it (INBOX 797).

- Whiteboard: the Library's Frames has swimlanes, a pool with three lanes in rows or in columns (INBOX 797).

- Whiteboard: Insert, Mermaid, draw.io or board SVG also brings in Mermaid state, class and sequence diagrams, and opens a .drawio file (its first page: shapes, labels, swimlanes as frames, connectors), naming anything it could not keep (INBOX 797).

- Whiteboard: the Library has five more shape sets from draw.io (basic shapes, flowchart, arrows, BPMN, network and cloud: 196 shapes), loaded when a set is opened or a search is typed, and a connector snaps to each shape's own connection points (INBOX 797).

- Chat: Agent mode is greyed, with Ask shown in use, whenever no model can answer, not only when the model server is off: the server up with nothing installed, Ollama without the chosen chat model, and before the first status all count. Your saved choice is untouched and Agent returns when a model answers; Needle keeps it available (INBOX 778).

- Notes, Questions: each note's questions sit under its title as a link-styled heading with the note's icon (hover underline, kept under the sub-tab strip while its questions scroll) instead of a bordered button, and a question an older rule had cut at a quote mark (`" or "What's the most ...`) leaves the list the moment it opens rather than at the next night pass.
- The "[[" picker names a note by its opening line only and previews it with its first picture and a short excerpt that does not repeat the title (a sketch note read as its title four times and showed no drawing).
- The "/" menu's Table and Code block previews draw their bar on one line, with Copy and the ⋯ as two small icon buttons side by side instead of a grey blob over a wrapped caption.
- Faster start: the Tools and features list (about 195 rows of text) loads when the dashboard, the palette or that list first needs it, not with the first screen; boot scripts shrank by 5,879 bytes gzipped.
- Chat with no model: asking about a topic as a whole ("games notes", "what did I write about uni", "who is Jake", "what am I working on") says how many notes there are and when, the thread most of them share, then each note with its day and one line, grouped by that thread, and offers next questions taken from the notes.
- Chat with no model: a picture in a note is said as what it shows and its words, once, never "shows The image shows" or a cut-off reading; a note is found by what its pictures say; and the notice under the answer appears only when most of it is how the app read pictures.
- Guide with no model: an answer is written for the question (where it is, the steps, the sentence that answers), with From the help beside it for the topic word for word; "hey" gets a greeting and three questions to ask instead of the open tab's topic, and no sentence is shown twice.
- Code editor panel: one compact header row (tabs left, the run state as a chip, the actions as icon buttons with tooltips), a padded body that says what an empty tab will show, and the console as a single prompt line in the editor's font; the footer and the keys line stand on the editor's column, and a code file's keys line names code chords instead of bold and italics.
- Code editor: a diagnostic card shows a severity icon and colour, the message, then its fix as a button on its own row, with room around it and a gap from the line it is about.
- Documents sidebar: the Outline is one tree (each heading's chevron stands left of its own text, task counts end on one edge, the current section is filled whole), its headings carry their counts on the right, and the empty band under the tab strip is gone; References are one row each (icon and title) with insert-at-caret and remove icons that show on hover or focus, and always on touch; Attach a bookmark is a quiet row.
- Graph: a topic's card is a title row (colour dot, name, rename and close icons) with the note count as a muted line under it; renaming puts the name field in the same row with Save and Cancel, and the card no longer changes height or wraps "7 notes" while you edit.
- OCR workspace: the Read split button keeps one shared border over a reading, so its caret reads as part of the same control.
- Find anything: the star saves the search (its naming box opened behind the finder before) and turns into a filled star while the search is saved; an active favourite is a filled star everywhere.
- Sticky sub-tab strips are opaque, a body control tall and edged while a list scrolls under them.
- Mind map: a topic's add buttons are real buttons (28px, 44 on touch, one size at every zoom) with a link glyph for the reference, and the board is rasterised again after a zoom so link labels stay crisp.
- Mind map: the "This map" tab is number-over-label tiles, one group of action buttons and a help popover for the templates hint.
- Mind map: Outline rows read until a double click, F2, Enter or their pencil opens one; Enter saves, Escape cancels, Shift+Enter adds a topic.
- Whiteboard: line ends gain filled triangle, diamond, filled diamond and bar beside the open arrow; the Start and End lists group plain and entity-relationship ends and draw each end in its row.
- Whiteboard: sticky notes can hide their folded corner, per note (Format panel) or as the board's default (View, Folded sticky corners).
- Whiteboard and mind map: Fit to screen fits the canvas you can see (not under the top bar, tools dock, sidebar or Format panel) and refits when a panel opens or closes until you pan or zoom.
- Whiteboard: the View menu is one column in Panels, Canvas and Zoom, and the Board menu is plain icon rows under section heads with Clear and Delete last and red; every row is one height.
- Whiteboard Library: shape tiles are drawn in the pen's ink with the shape's own fill opacity, width and dash, as the shape is placed.
- Every button answers hover the same way: an icon button takes the quiet fill a labelled one does, with its glyph going to full ink, instead of tinting blue with no background; the header's status pill and the chips on a note's meta line follow. Measured over the header, seven tabs and Settings at 1440: 153 of 361 buttons answered with the glyph alone before, 1 after (INBOX 784, 788).
- Focus rings are no longer cut off on the Notes list's rows view (every row), the chips on its meta line, a category's ⋮ and a rows-view wiki link (INBOX 784).
- Confirm and Not right on a pattern are one compact pair on the sentence's own row (a check and a cross, quiet until hovered), in Chat and Tidy; the dashboard's pattern line keeps its ⋯ and now has a gap between the last word and it (INBOX 782, 786).
- Tidy: a cross on each suggestion dismisses it for good, remembered so it is not listed, counted or applied again; the toast's Undo brings it back (INBOX 783).
- Connections, in the sheet and in the Notes column, is a quiet list: a glyph, the title and a muted line for the kind or day, a count on each section, count chips at the top, and no bordered button per row; the sheet has Open in the sidebar to dock it as the column (INBOX 784).
- Settings, Appearance: Peek now lets go of the panel: the ground is 8% with no blur and the body of the panel fades to 22%, so the app behind reads clearly; the head stays in full so Peek and the close button are easy to find (INBOX 780).
- Settings, Appearance, Your themes: each saved look's delete bin is a small icon button inside the card (beside its name) instead of a badge on its corner, and the section reads top to bottom: the cards across the full width, then the name box and Save on one row, then the two reset buttons on a row of their own (INBOX 779).
- The top tab bar's focus ring is no longer cut off at the top and bottom (INBOX 776).
- Sub-tab strips (Notes, Library, the document sidebar): hovering a tab you are not on draws a grey line under it again; it had stopped after the first hover or press on a strip.
- Loading placeholders shimmer slowly and softly (about a quarter of the old speed) instead of fast and jittery.
- Translate this, in the command palette: a selected passage of a note, a document or a reading turned from English into Spanish on this computer with no model, then copied or put in place of the selection (Ctrl+Z undoes it). It needs "Translate offline", a 27 MB download in Settings, Packages (new bundle Languages); until it is installed the row says so and opens that page.

- Recording never refuses: with no Voice notes add-on a meeting or a voice note is still kept, as a recording with its length; the add-on transcribes it when installed.
- Recordings are saved every 10 seconds, so a closed or crashed tab keeps all but the last few seconds, and the next start says "Recording recovered".
- An Audio group in Tools and features, and palette rows for Voice note, Dictate a note and Recordings, each also a Quick access tile.
- Undo for starting a meeting, a reminder made from an action item, and saving a transcript into a meeting, as a meeting or as a document.
- Library, Recordings: play at 0.5 to 2x over the saved waveform, markers pressed while recording (M or Marker), Trim into a new recording that keeps the original, Rename, and Delete into the bin.
- Reminders: every weekday, every 2 weeks, every other Monday and the last Friday of the month repeat as said, and "1 day before" or "an hour before" adds an early alert; quick add shows both as chips, and ticking a repeating reminder moves it to its next time (Brief 85).
- Reminders fire on the minute they are due (they could be up to a minute late), and an early alert fires once, ahead of its reminder.
- Reminders: adding, completing and editing one undo with Ctrl+Z, like deleting and snoozing already did.
- Reminders and Settings say once when the browser blocks notifications, with how to allow them in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari and the desktop app.
- Timeline: a row under the day strip offers On this day (what you wrote on today's date in earlier years) and a chip per year that narrows the list to it.
- Timeline: the selection bar adds favourite and archive, and every act on it (move, tags, favourite, archive, delete) undoes; undoing a move no longer marks the notes as filed by hand.
- Dashboard: On this day counts in months, so last November's note is "11 months ago", not "1 year ago" in place of the one written on this date.
- Timeline and reminders: a closed dock menu no longer lays out under the page (the timeline's folded view switch at 390, the reminder presets over the Open, All and Done chips).
- Agent: with no model it still works. Every starter runs from your notes: what changed today, what is due, the loose ends, a summary of the open note or of the conversation, and Add to today's note, Tag my untagged notes and Link related notes as cards you confirm and can undo; typed acts ("tag every note about the harbor with harbor") run the same way.
- Agent on a phone: it opens as a sheet from More (Ask the agent), the command palette and the shortcut, rather than switching to Chat; the starters, the field and the use-the-open-note box come with it.
- Agent: a plan the model draws waits for Run the plan, listing each step and the writes it will make; each step ticks with what it wrote (an edit with its lines out and in) and an Undo per write; Stop between two steps keeps the next step from writing, and the writes made so far stay on the undo bar.
- Agent and Chat: Ctrl+Z after a run takes back its last write (and Ctrl+Shift+Z does it again); each write of a run goes on the undo bar as it is made, and the run's Undo the run still takes back the whole.
- Live captions: the command palette's Live captions row starts a bar over any screen that writes what the microphone hears as you speak, three finished lines above the one still being written, with Copy and Stop (Stop saves everything as a note tagged captions). It talks to a local whisper.cpp server named by MEMORYMAP_CAPTIONS_URL (Settings, Packages, Live captions says it is not packaged for one-click install yet); the status reports `captions: {available, model}`, and audio never leaves this computer.
- Documents: every act on a document is one undo step: rename, archive, restoring a version, a writing fix, adding a word to the dictionary, attaching or removing a link, detaching a note and making a new document all undo with Ctrl+Z or the toast's Undo (Brief 76). On an open document Ctrl+Z takes back whichever came last, the typing or the act.
- Documents: version history names versions (Name this version, a Named filter, a row's menu to rename one), shows Changes side by side on a wide window, and a restore happens at once and undoes byte for byte.
- Documents: Replace in every document (the editor's Ctrl+K list) replaces across all documents, plain or a regular expression, with or without case, and one Ctrl+Z takes the whole replace back.
- Documents: with no model connected, AI edit and Extract notes say why when pressed and offer Set up a model, instead of sitting disabled.
- Documents: on a phone the document menu no longer lies over the breadcrumbs or past the screen's edge while closed, and a code document opens in about half the time (the outline and checks draw a frame after the text).
- Chat: Ctrl+Z undoes a chat's rename, pin, archive, fork, a deleted message and a chat saved as a document, as it already undid a deleted chat; a deleted message comes back in its place (Brief 88).
- Chat: a note source opens its note with the quoted passage marked, from a source card, a citation's preview or the evidence list.
- Chat: message actions, grounding chips and citation marks take a full-size press; the head's hidden Export and Delete stand-ins are gone (the menu's rows do it).
- The Guide: an answer's open button lands on the control it is about, ringed, not the top of a tab or a Settings section; Ctrl+K "guide" finds Ask the Guide.
- Documents (code): the panel under the editor has tabs, Output, Problems, Tests and Console, each keeping its own height; Ctrl+J shows or hides it, Ctrl+Shift+M opens Problems and Ctrl+Shift+Y the Console, as in VS Code (Brief 71). Every code file has the panel, not only the kinds that run.
- Documents (code): two consoles. A line of JavaScript evaluates in what the last run left (its `let` and `const` included), a line of Python in the run's namespace; Up and Down recall earlier lines, Ctrl+L clears.
- Documents (code): Problems lists every underline the checks make, each a link to its line, the count in its tab; HTML has a check of its own now (a stray closing tag, an element left open).
- Documents (code): Ctrl+Shift+P (or F1) runs any editor command by name with a fuzzy match, Ctrl+\ splits the editor into two views of one file, and Ctrl+K Ctrl+S opens a searchable sheet of every editor command and its key.
- Statistics: one page for your notebook (notes, words, tags, categories, links, notes with no link, growth per month), your reminders (made, done, open, late) and what you use, opened from the Dashboard's Activity heatmap or the palette's Statistics (Brief 89).
- This week: notes made, words written and reminders done against last week, on the Statistics page and as a Dashboard card.
- Chat's counted answers ("how many notes do I have") no longer end with a false "Heads up: I could not find 96 in your notes".
- The command palette has a timer ("timer 10 minutes") and a stopwatch that run on the status bar and stop when you press them, Count words for any selection, and "insert template" to put a template where the cursor is.
- Ctrl+K finds every feature in Tools and features, every act Chat does and the matching settings, not only its own list: "statistics", "timer", "word count", "calculator" and "find anything" each find their row.
- Ctrl+K learns: the command you ran for some words comes first the next time you type them, and hovering a row says why it is where it is; "todo", "whiteboard" and "hotkeys" find what they mean.
- Nothing matched now says why: Ctrl+K offers the nearest command for a word a letter out, and Find anything offers one way on (every kind, a spelling, or the nearest feature).
- Find anything's search field is the whole height of its bar, and 44px tall on a touch screen.
- Chat with no model runs the notebook's read tools itself: "list my tags", "what reminders do I have", "give me an overview of my notebook" and the like answer in one line and draw the answer in its shape: a bar chart of counts, a table, a card or a list (CHAT_PLAN decision 59, Brief 84).
- Chat with no model follows the conversation: "and delete it", "same for Tuesday", "pin the other one" and "the gym note too" act on what the last five turns were about (200 of 200 spoken follow-ups, from 20).
- Chat's answers open in more ways: twenty turns of one question now open at least eight ways in each voice (was three).
- The Guide answers first: its reply leads with the one line that answers the question, the same line Chat gives, and says it is the app's own help text after it; "how do I pin a note" or "rename a note" is answered from Chat's acts.
- CI: the chat's "propose a change" tool now draws its Confirm card and stops the turn (its handover was missing, so the card never showed); Stop all in Activity says when a stop is refused; "how do I open the app on my phone" answers from the phone topic first; the Settings word groups load when the search is first used, not at start; a board's snapshot list takes a limit and reports its total.
- OCR workspace: saving an edit, deleting a reading, cleaning up repeated lines, a region read and a fresh read all undo (Ctrl+Z, the toast's Undo) and redo; a deleted reading goes to the bin and is restored from the Library's Bin (0 of 5 to 5 of 5 in `scratchpad/ui-sweeps/ocr79.js`).
- OCR workspace: a pinch zooms about the pointer, from a trackpad (Ctrl and the wheel, continuous now) or two fingers on a touch screen (at 390 px: Fit to 176% and back to 63%; before, a touch pinch did nothing).
- OCR workspace: at 390 and 320 px the reader menu spans the window and Read loses its icon before it would leave the screen (controls past the right edge 3 to 0 at 390, 4 to 0 at 320).
- OCR workspace: with no engine and no model the reader menu offers RapidOCR first (60 MB, nothing else to install) then Tesseract, each with Install, and Read and the region's Read and Describe say why they cannot act yet.
- OCR workspace: Live Text in place. Where Tesseract or RapidOCR read a page, its words lie over the picture; drag across them and Ctrl+C copies them in reading order.
- OCR workspace: opens faster at phone width (the tool row is fitted in about three measures, once per size, where it took up to six, twice): 390 px open 398, 246, 683 ms to 353, 127, 387 ms on a loaded machine.
- Mind map: New, Mind map makes "Untitled map N" and opens its central topic for typing (what you type names the map); "mind map" is the one word for it everywhere; four new layouts, logic chart, timeline, fishbone and tree table; every map command is in the top bar's More sheet on a phone; a selected topic's buttons no longer overlap; adding a topic renders once; a topic's shadow, glow and icon reach the PNG and SVG; the board help names every top bar control and the palette has a row for each.
- Whiteboard: every command has a phone path (a More kebab at the top bar's end below 820 px; 40 of 81 commands reachable at 390 px before, 81 of 81 now, no top-bar target under 44 px); New makes an Untitled board and asks for its name in place of the picker, so a canvas is there before a dialog; a change made by the agent or by another tab is one Undo step; named snapshots with a picture under Board, and a restore is one Undo step (Brief 77).
- Documents (code): a debugger (Brief 70). Debug (F5, or the run panel's new Debug tab) runs a JavaScript, TypeScript or Python document to its first breakpoint: click beside a line number or press F9 for one, right-click it for a condition. At a stop the line is lit and the Debug tab shows Variables, Watch (expressions evaluated at each stop), the Call stack and Breakpoints; F10 steps over, F11 into a call, Shift+F11 out, F5 continues, Shift+F5 stops, and the same five are buttons. An error nothing catches stops on the line that raised it with its traceback. Python steps through its own `bdb`; JavaScript through JS-Interpreter (vendored, 27 KB gzipped, loaded on the first Debug), with `let`, `const`, arrow functions and template strings rewritten for it and anything it cannot step (a class, destructuring, async) named with its line. The first stop comes 50 to 200 ms after Debug once the runtime is loaded.
- Documents (code): Python's `input()` asks in the Output panel mid-run once the Input box's lines are used up (it raised EOFError before); the app is now cross-origin isolated (two response headers), which this and the Python debugger need. F11 is Step into while a debug session is on and Focus mode otherwise.

- Documents (code): Run speaks one protocol for every language (Brief 69). TypeScript runs with its types removed and not checked (sucrase, vendored, 47 KB gzipped, loaded on the first run); SQL runs against an empty in-memory SQLite per run, each statement's result a table on its line (sql.js, vendored, 339 KB gzipped, loaded on the first run); CSS previews over a sample page, SVG renders as an image (a new `.svg` document type that edits as XML), and a p5.js sketch draws beside its code with the vendored p5 (a new p5.js sketch template). Live in the Output panel refreshes a preview 400 ms after the typing stops, and a save refreshes it.
- Documents (code): tests are a kind of run. A file of tests runs its tests (describe, it and expect in JavaScript and TypeScript; unittest and plain `test_` functions in Python), each listed with its state and time, a failure's diff under it and an underline on its line; Run tests in the panel and the palette.
- Documents (code): Python's `input()` reads its lines from the Output panel's Input box (it got the end of the input before); Run the selected lines and Run the cell between `# %%` markers are in the palette, with every line number the document's.
- Documents (code): a `.py` document before Python is installed shows Run greyed with "Install Python in Settings, Packages" beside it; a run still going after two seconds is listed in Activity, whose Stop ends it.
- Documents (code): the Output panel on a phone: its buttons fold to icons and the head no longer runs 49 px past the panel; the grip and each Line N link take a 44 px tap (6.4 and 16.8 px before), the grip's hairline where it was; a '?' says what Run does.
- Atlas's arms at rest: calm, its most common mood, had all three arm variants hanging straight down; it now rests an arm a little out, puts a hand on its hip, or brings its hands together in front, and the companion eases between them.
- Reduce motion stops Atlas's loops and keeps its pose, under the system's hint as under the app's own setting (the hint slowed them to 9 seconds).
- Atlas costs less at rest in the corner: its tail holds a drawn shape and sways on the compositor between behaviours (it redrew its path 15 times a second), calm behaviours hold 9 to 18 seconds, and the chest's breath steps 2.5 times a second there.
- Atlas's moods read at small sizes: the chat heads and inline marks (28 and 20 px) show bold brows and one sign beside the head for the mood (a note, sparkles, a heart, Zs, a question mark, a tear, a flame, a star), so all fifteen moods are fifteen faces there (2 and 1 before, measured by pixel diff in the light theme).
- Companion: rub it (the pointer back and forth over it, not pressing) and it leans into your hand with a fond face, and a sulk ends; asleep it nuzzles and sleeps on. Shake it up and down while you carry it and it turns upside down, then lands a little dizzy. Both have a switch under Appearance, What it does on its own (INBOX 743).
- Atlas changes face more (INBOX 742): a calm Atlas passes through a nearby mood every 35 to 75 seconds and eases back, never one of its last two; a ticked-off reminder makes it proud, a search glad or puzzled. A settled Atlas also changes how it holds its arms now and then, rather than hanging them the whole time it stays.
- Atlas moves differently at different distances: a hop or a float for a step, a swooping leap across a change of level, and a glide, a walk or a poof when far; it used to float or glide and nothing else.
- Companion cost: the perch check runs after input, a resize or a toast and otherwise once in 10 seconds (it walked the page's controls every 1.5 seconds); at rest in the corner Atlas's tail is drawn 15 times a second from a timer, not from a 60 Hz frame loop; the hold's hidden hands are no longer stepped; and under the lock screen nothing of the companion or Atlas runs.
- Library, boards and mind maps: every failure toast speaks in one register through the voice table (`realise.VOICE`, `voiceLine`): "Couldn't open that document.", never "Could not" beside it (67 toasts moved; 7 said "Could not" before); no toast in the app says "Oops" or ends in "!" (Brief 68, decision 55).
- Agent: four tools hand the model the app's own working: Calculate (sums, percentages, conversions, days), Read text (the recogniser), Check answer (the validators) and Propose act (the act registry: a card that waits for your Confirm); "15% of 240" is now worked out (36) rather than answered from a note; a number against its unit ("120kg", "10k") is checked against the sources, 12 of 12 unsourced numbers caught on the fixture (Brief 68).
- Help: the Guide answers "phone", "can I use it on two computers", "is my data encrypted", "how do I delete my data" and "how do I share a note" with topics of their own (the engine probe's table, 8 of 8; 3 had no topic and 2 the wrong one); the agent palette's "Do" group adds every act Chat does from one sentence, from the act registry, each with its help line (Brief 68).
- Import from another app: a note's day comes from the export (a daily note's name, a `date:` or "Created:" line, an Obsidian `created:`), so it lands on its own day on the Timeline (5 of 5 on the fixture, 1 of 5 before: every dated note landed on the import day), and its "tomorrow" is read on that day; the summary names the people and places read (Brief 68).
- Graph and Library: the search box reads filters: "connected to Harbor", "untouched since June", "tagged work", "pinned", "with pictures", "edited last week", "filed under Cooking" (`ai/filters.py`, `GET /read/filter`, 40 of 40 on the fixture). Settings: the search finds a setting by what it does, with words that mean the same ("night mode", "darker", "bigger text", "back up my notes", "hotkeys"; 10 of 10 first results right) (Brief 68).
- Boards: in the command palette over a board, "arrange as a grid of 3", "put them in a row", "stack them", "align left", "space them evenly" and "same width" are acts with Undo (`acts.board_parse`, 40 of 40 on the fixture); a sticky that names a day shows it as a chip, a press away from a reminder (Brief 68).
- Documents: counts and reading time come from one module shared with the note composer and the server (`ai/utilities.py` `counts`, `textCounts`), equal to `wc` on the fixture (583 characters, 113 words; an emoji was two characters before); the outline reads `~~~` fences; the Library's Contents index uses the same outline; Search documents reads a window ("harbor last week") as the notes search does (Brief 68).
- Dashboard: the Digest opens with your day, composed with no AI: what is due, the open questions, what changed since yesterday and the topics gone quiet, each line a count or words quoted from one note or reminder, each opening where it came from; Atlas's week stays below on request (CHAT_PLAN section 2, Brief 68; `GET /insights/day`).
- Note editor: while you write (Capture or a note's Edit form), a day in the text is offered as a reminder, a sum with a wrong answer shows the right one, a name another note opens with is offered as a [[link]], and the filing suggestion shows its reason; never on quoted words, at most five, drawn 162 to 179 ms after the pause at 1440 and 390 (CHAT_PLAN section 2, Brief 68; `POST /read/offers`).
- Whiteboard: on a phone or a narrow window, More (the dots at the top bar's end) lists every board command the bar has no room for, in the menus' groups; at 390 every one of the 81 board commands now has a path (was 40).
- Whiteboard: New, Whiteboard makes "Untitled board N" and opens it at once, its name ready to type over in the top bar (Enter saves, Escape keeps it); Rename this board edits the name in the same place, and the templates are New, From a template.
- Whiteboard: a change Atlas or another tab makes to the open board is one step on its Undo stack ("Atlas changed 3 items"), so Ctrl+Z takes it back rather than stepping past it.
- Whiteboard: Board, Snapshots… saves a named version of the board (Snapshot and the time by default), shows each with its picture, and Restore puts the board back as one Undo step.
- Backups: the notebook file gets a quick check each time the app starts (30 ms on a 5,000-note notebook), before anything writes to it; when it fails, a notice that stays until closed points to the newest backup in Settings, Import & export, where the Backups section says the same. A file too damaged to open at all stops the start with words naming the newest backup and the files to move aside (WORLD_CLASS 25e, Brief 51).
- Notes: History's Put this back no longer asks first; it is one Undo (the toast, the status bar, Ctrl+Z) that returns the text and tags the note had (rule 1.8).
- Undo: an import and a Writing desk AI pass are now entries on the undo stack too, so the toast's or the pane's Undo, the status bar and Ctrl+Z are the same act and each can be redone; categories and chats share one `offerUndo` with them (rule 1.8, `tests/test_undo_contract.py`).
- Tests: a backup restored on a new machine is compared kind by kind (`tests/test_restore_roundtrip.py`), and typed drafts in Capture, Quick note and the edit form are found again after the server is killed (`tests-e2e/specs/draft-recovery.spec.js`).
- Developer ratchets (no change to the app): silent swallows (21), routes no test names (49), unregistered background threads and tasks (26), functions over complexity 15 (260), import cycles (none at load) and per-file frame loops, intervals and observers are held at today's counts; `print` in `src` outside the command line fails ruff (`T201`); the measured census is WORLD_CLASS_PLAN 26.4 and 26.5.
- PWA: the service worker now caches the stamped scripts and stylesheets, the vendored libraries, the icons and the manifest (a reload asks the server for none of them), and a page load with MemoryMap not running shows "MemoryMap is not running on this computer" with a Retry button instead of the browser's error page; the app itself is never cached, so it never paints without its server.
- Settings, About: Install as an app (when the browser offers it; on iPhone it says Share, then Add to Home Screen), with its help and a Guide topic.
- Search: Find anything finds saved chats and Ask questions as well (a Chat chip, `kind:chat`), wears a kind chip on every row, pages with Show more results, lists every operator (`tag:`, `in:`, `kind:`, `before:`, `after:`, `has:`, `is:`, quotes, minus) behind its '?', and its star saves a search as a row under Saved searches in the Notes sidebar; a notes filter that matches nothing offers Search everything. The box loads after boot rather than with it (Brief 47, decision 46).
- Search: `tag:` alone finds every note with the tag; it was read over the newest 200 rows only, so at 5,000 notes `tag:tag3` found 5 of about 110.
- `GET /search` takes `page` beside `limit` and answers `page`, `limit` and `more`; the index gains the `chat` kind, filled once at the next start for a notebook indexed before it.
- Documents (code): the Output panel's grip takes a press 24px tall (7px before) with its hairline where it was, and is there on a phone too (it was hidden below 600px with the sidebars' handles).
- Documents: Ctrl+Shift+8, Ctrl+Shift+7 and Ctrl+Shift+9 make a bulleted, numbered and task list (Google Docs' keys), and every document command now carries its key or a recorded "none" (a code document's palette: 52 rows, 26 with keys, 0 undecided).
- Documents (code): Format (Shift+Alt+F) on a whole JavaScript, CSS or HTML file lays it out with js-beautify (vendored, 25 KB gzipped, loaded on the first Format, nothing at boot): 504 lines in 328 ms the first time, 268 ms after; a selection and the other types keep the re-indent that moves no token.
- Documents (code): four more file types, Diff (`.diff`, `.patch`, added lines green and removed red), Dockerfile, Visual Basic (`.vb`) and VBScript (`.vbs`), each highlighted by a mode the editor already carried (0 bytes more).
- Documents: Download as Word writes pictures as Word pictures (not their alt text), suggested changes as Word's tracked changes, nested lists as list levels and numbered lists as Word numbering; a .docx imported in the Library keeps its nested lists, code blocks and pictures (stored in the media folder).
- Packages: the "Export to Word (python-docx)" extra is gone (11 extras to 10), with `GET /documents/{id}/export.docx` and the server's Word writer; Download as Word has been written in the browser since the docx library landed, and a Setup that still names `docx` installs the rest.
- Quick add: the Reminders box, Quick note, a new meeting's title, the Timeline's search and the command palette show what was read (a day, a time, a repeat, a person, a #tag, a window) as chips under the box as you type; Enter saves what the chips say, a chip pressed off stays words, and a reminder with no day or time asks for one rather than guessing (CHAT_PLAN decision 50, Brief 66). Lazy: the boot scripts are 140 bytes smaller gzipped.
- Reminders: Magic add saves "water the plants every tuesday" as a weekly repeat named "Water the plants", reads "every morning at 7" as 07:00 daily, "dentist 21st 9am" as the 21st, "remind me in 20 minutes to check the oven" as "Check the oven", and "in 1.5 hours", "in 6 months" and "in a year" (CHAT_PLAN F1, Brief 65).
- Search and chat: "notes from march", "on friday" (the one before, in a question) and "two weeks ago" filter by date, read by the one recogniser (`ai/recognise.py`); "how many notes did I write today" counts the day rather than the whole notebook; chart questions read the same windows (Brief 65).
- `GET /read` (and `/api/v1/read`): the typed reading of what was typed, its spans, confidence band and the one question an unsure reading asks, for the quick-add chips (Brief 65, decision 47).
- Chat: a broad question ("what do my notes say about running") opens with the topic and how many notes it quotes, a count or a date is said once rather than again by the closing pattern line, and twenty turns of one question open at least three ways in both voices and in help (Brief 67, INBOX 729).
- Chat: a model's answer is checked like Atlas's own: a number or name that none of its notes or the question holds is said under it (Brief 67, decision 53).
- Chat: every act runs through one registry with its undo; Ctrl+Z after an act takes it back, Ask names the act it read, and the Guide has "Things Chat does for you" (Brief 67).
- Chat: a reminder is said back as "Remind you on Friday at 9: call the dentist", attached to the note it comes from, and "on Friday at 9 remind me to ..." is read too (INBOX 734).
- Insights: every pattern line (Chat, Tidy, the dashboard) has Confirm, which keeps it as your own word from then on, and Not right, which never shows it or a variant of it again (decision 60).
- Chat: the time, a coin toss and a dice roll say how the question was read ("Read as ...").
- Density (UI Phase 12): the top bar is 44px (was 64), its tabs 32 in a 36px strip; every dock's controls are one 28px height (40 to 44 under touch) and the Notes and Library sub-tab strips are 28px (was 36). Three control heights are tokens now (`--control-h-dense` 28, `--control-h-lg` 32, `--control-h-touch` 40) and literal heights are a ratchet.
- Hover (UI Phase 12): an icon button answers the pointer and keyboard focus by turning its glyph the accent colour, with no box behind it (334 of 334 icon buttons drew one, now 0, light and dark); an open menu's button keeps a soft accent box; a sub-tab takes a grey underline on hover rather than a tint.
- Date and time fields (UI Phase 12): Reminders' due date and time, the Timeline's custom range and Ask's as-of day open a month grid (arrows, Page Up and Down) or the day's times in your clock, read a typed day such as "next friday" or "3pm" (`POST /reminders/when`, no model), and have Today or Now and Clear; the date and time fields also draw a focus ring now, which they never did.
- Note cards: the category is its colour dot and its word, as on the Timeline's rows, rather than a filled pill.

- Filing: a health, money, relationships, legal or identity note is held for the person on every filing path, the embedder's nearest notes and the chat model's answer included, until Settings lets it file (decision 6, INBOX 770); the capture E2E spec checks both states.
- Documents: Download as Word is written in the browser (docx, vendored, loaded on the first press) rather than by an optional server extra that answered 501 on most installs, and a .docx added in the Library is read by Mammoth with its headings, lists, emphasis, links and tables kept rather than as bare text (Brief 42, INBOX 765).
- Documents (code): the Output panel has a grip on its top edge (drag, arrow keys, double-click to reset; the height kept per document), and Stop greys out once a script has finished and has no timer left, rather than staying lit after "Finished." (INBOX 736).
- Documents (code): the active line number is bold and the line bordered as in VS Code; Minimap in Editor and layout (off at first); Fold every block, Unfold every block, List every problem (Ctrl+Shift+M) and Compare with a saved version (an inline merge view with Reject per hunk) in the palette; the code-file class no longer drops when the editor takes focus. CodeMirror bundle +18,706 bytes gzipped for the merge view, the minimap and Visual Basic (Brief 42).
- Chat dock skills panel: on a phone the Auto | Manual pace pill sat 4px inside its track and now sits 1px inside, the same as the Ask | Agent pill, at 390 and 1440 (INBOX 694).
- First-run tour: the Library step "A card's menu" now reveals the card's hover-only menu button while it is highlighted, instead of framing an empty square (INBOX 745).
- Documents: a new document names itself "Untitled document N" (the next free number), as boards and maps do, so Create never needs a name and the list can tell new pages apart (INBOX 739).
- Filing with no model: a note files only into a category you have, by your other notes' words and a built-in list of 512 topics ("squats" finds Gym before any Gym note said it), and says why ("It mentions squat and deadlift (Fitness), like the 10 notes in Gym."); unsure, it offers one-tap choices that say why and, when none of yours fits, "New: Art", made only if pressed. On the 120-note fixture, top-1 0.175 to 0.417 (WORLD_CLASS_PLAN 23).
- Filing: notes about health, money, family, the law or identity wait for you to choose unless Settings, Background tasks, "File health, money and family notes by their words too" is on; Tidy lists them unticked and never moves them by itself.
- Fixed: "Study" and "university" no longer suggested on notes that say nothing about either (the owner, 2026-10-10): a suggested tag needs a word in the note, at most three, and its tooltip says which word.
- Tidy: two new reviews, Categories that overlap ("Merge Misc and Fitness into Gym?") and Category names ("Rename Misc to Fitness?"); both ask first and undo in one press, and a merge or a move you make teaches where those topics go next time.

Literal error toasts 36 to 28, 4 with an action of their own and 24 on the default, a ratchet in `tests/test_error_toasts.py`.

Measured against a slow fake Ollama: an answer listed and stopped in 347 ms at 390 and 360 ms at 1440, the model out of memory after Stop the model, 0 overlaps and 0 overflow in the panel at both widths (`tests/test_activity.py`, with a lint that every thread site registers).

- Setup on Linux and macOS can share the packages already installed on the computer (MEMORYMAP_SYSTEM_SITE_PACKAGES=1), and refuses with a reason when the installed torch is outside the supported range.

### Changed
- Plans: six features deepened under the trust contract (Brief 72a, decision 71): the documents editor (DOCUMENTS_PLAN 24), the code editor (25), the whiteboard, the mind map (MINDMAP 15), the OCR workspace (WORLD_CLASS 28.4) and the audio set (28.5), each measured by `scratchpad/ui-sweeps/deepen72a.js` with undo coverage, clicks from the dashboard, overflow at 1440 and 390 and open times; Briefs 76 to 83; the audio go taken (INBOX 759).

- Answers from your notes: a short question that names three or more notes ends by asking which you mean, numbered ("Which do you mean: 1. Boiler service; 2. Boiler manual; 3. Boiler quote?"); "why?" after "longer" still asks about the subject; "any patterns in my running notes" answers with the weeks in a row.
- With web search on and no model, a Chat question your notes do not answer is answered from the web pages the search finds, every sentence quoted from its page and cited by address ("[page **Tides explained**]"), the pages listed under the answer; with web search off nothing is fetched.
- The answer from your notes is Atlas's: "who are you" and "what can you do" answer as Atlas, the answer's chip reads From your notes (the model's name when a model answers), "how do I change the theme" is answered from the app's Help with no model, and a model that stops before its first word leaves Atlas's answer from your notes rather than only an error.
- Chat acts with no model: "remind me to call Sam on Friday", "make a note that...", "pin the dentist note" are done at once with Undo; "delete the boiler note", "rename...", "move... to Work", "tag...", "link the gym note to the running note" show the exact change and wait for Confirm; "open settings" goes there; a note it cannot tell apart is asked about, never guessed. With a model in Agent mode the agent does them as before.
- Patterns: a broad answer about a subject closes with what your notes measure ("You have written about golf 4 times since 5 September, three of them after work; that may be a hobby forming."), only when the rule is met (3 notes across 3 weeks); "any patterns in my golf notes" leads with it; the dashboard's line and Tidy show the notebook's patterns (a subject that recurs, a plan gone quiet, a change of mind, a busy week).
- Answers from your notes read a picture's caption as part of its note (the picture's, said as such), say what kind each source is ("[board **Harbor board**]") and open a cited board, map, document or file in its own place.
- Answers from your notes follow the conversation: "and last week?", "what about running?", "and Sam?", "why?", "shorter" and "no, the gym one" are read against the question before, "tell me more" never repeats a sentence, a 20-turn chat opens 15 different ways where it opened 13, and Try again rewords the answer while keeping its first sentence.
- Answers from your notes say your own sentences back to you ("you went to the gym" for "I went to the gym", "you planned to" once the day has passed), never inside someone else's quoted words, and draw every sentence taken from a note in a quote style; hovering a reworded one shows your note's own words.
- Ask and Chat work some questions out instead of searching, with or without a model: sums, unit and currency conversions (the rates' date is said), the time and date, days until or since a date, a die or a coin; "what did I do last week" lists every note of that week, newest first; "notes tagged X" keeps to that tag; "how do I change the theme" and "what's new" are answered as questions about the app; the weather is said to be unknown rather than guessed.
- Answers from your notes cite each note as [**Title**]; hovering the name previews the passage it came from and pressing it opens the note (Ask and Chat).
- Filing with no model: a fixed keyword map now votes only for a category you already have (top-1 on a 40-note test notebook 0.05 to 0.15, no more wrong filings), and tag suggestions are only ever tags you already use.
- The Guide is offered to the agent when a question is about the app ("how do I", "where is", a setting), not on every turn.

### Fixed

- Filing: a sensitive note is held on every path (words, embedder, model) until the Settings switch is on, and only a category named as the sensitive topic itself holds a note; "Dad Jokes" was held as Relationships.
- Draft tag suggestions with a model running no longer fail on an unbound name; the "I meant ..." correction follow-on no longer fails on its second form.
- The code editor's output grip states its height to assistive technology and remembers it through the preferences door; the Word writer's load failure offers Try again.
- Graph and Library: pinning a dragged group of notes and renaming a topic now say so when the save fails, instead of failing silently.
- Ask: the match reason ("70% similar") now folds to its icon last on a crowded details line, after the tags and the other word facts, so every matching record shows its number or none does (INBOX 728).
- Notes: a card's time now sits at the card's foot, the same 7px above its edge on every card (INBOX 760); a note with links showed it 48 to 113px up (80 to 146px at 390 against 7px with none), and "ago · edited" has its space back.
- Accessibility sweep: `a11yname.js` no longer reports "Show more" as unnamed (it read `innerText`, empty under `content-visibility: auto`); 2 false findings to 0. The plan and briefs name `axe.js`, the sweep that exists, where they named a `wcag22.js` that does not.
- Accessibility: the x buttons on suggested tags and inline images, and a note's tag chips folded to icons, carry an aria-label as well as a title (54 in the Notes list at 1440 and 21 at 390 were named by title alone).
- Accessibility: the "+N" chip that folds a note's extra tags keeps a 24 px target on phones (it measured 23.6 by 24).
- Accessibility: the dashboard activity heatmap, which scrolls sideways, is a keyboard stop with a focus ring, so the arrow keys reach older weeks.
- Accessibility: the task checkboxes in note cards are named by their task ("Done: ..." or "To do: ..."), where axe found 20 with no label.
- Graph: switching to Radial, Tree or Arc while the force layout was still settling left the camera on the old view, the new layout off in a corner; a layout switch now ends on the new layout's fitted view, and the radial is centred.
- Graph: the map no longer opens zoomed in and then pulls back (INBOX 738); its first visible frame is at the fitted zoom.
- Graph: a fitted view has even margins: the fit is measured on what was drawn (dots, names and topic names) and centred, on the first open, after a layout switch and from the Fit button.
- Graph: Shape is dimmed with its reason under Tree, Radial and Arc; it is the Force layout's own.
- Graph: collapsing and opening the local map beside a note no longer loses its notes off the edge; a folded map keeps its size and framing.
- Notes: a property value on a note card finds every note with it (the filter writes prop:key=value, quoted when the value has a space), and a note's panel on the graph shows its properties, a value lighting those notes on the map, with a Properties button to add or change them.
- Graph: topics can be renamed where their name is (double-click the name on the map, the pencil on the topic's card or a note's panel, or F2 or right-click on a topic's heading in Library, Contents, By topic), dragged by their name to move all their notes together, and a note's card and panel show its topic, which opens the graph on that topic.
- Dropdown buttons are named with the value they show (Audit 2026-10-10): "Sort notes: Newest first" rather than "Sort notes", so voice control that says what is written on the button reaches it. The lock screen no longer asks the server for the Tidy count before you have signed in.
- An update that changes the notebook's structure now copies the notebook to Backups first (Audit 2026-10-10): the migration used to run on the only copy, and the nightly backup could be a day old. Ordinary launches copy nothing.
- The Notes dock's Tidy count no longer takes 23 seconds on a 5,000-note notebook (Audit 2026-10-10): it counted loose notes by matching every one against the rest, and rescanned for duplicates on every list redraw. It now takes about 1.4 seconds the first time and answers from memory until a note changes.
- A full backup now carries your settings (Audit 2026-10-10): a restore onto a new computer brought back every note but none of the settings. The model API key and the sign-in switch are left out on purpose.
- Answers from your notes quote your words exactly again (no added quotation marks, no rewritten "I" to "you"), and "How long is the train from Lisbon to Porto?" or "Who are we looking to hire?" are no longer read as requests to translate.
- Small talk with only the tools extra installed and no model is answered by the app rather than handed to the tool runner.
- Answers from your notes: "who is Sam" no longer quotes "Same breakfast", a sentence written once is never said to repeat, "what is 12 * 7" is worked out on Ask, "how many notes are about Harbor" counts Harbor notes, time words ("last week") are never the subject, a subject no note holds is named, "what did I write most about" is counted, small talk and "what can you do" get a reply with From your notes on, and the first answer no longer takes a second to load.

### Removed

- 15 MB of vendored libraries the app never imported (networkx, whoosh, langdetect, dateutil, pint and a Windows .exe, among others); what remains is credited in docs/THIRD_PARTY.md. Sums ("what is 12 * 4") are worked out by a small evaluator of our own.
### Added

- Whiteboard and mind maps: a comment can be edited (in place, Enter keeps it, the row says edited), replied to (drawn one step in under it), resolved (folded into "N resolved", the corner mark counts what is open and shows a tick when nothing is) and deleted with its replies. The box has Attach (a bookmark, note, document or board) and the "/" and "[[" menus; a link alone on a line is drawn as a link card, a [[note]] as its chip.
- Whiteboard and mind maps: "/" in a text box or a topic being typed in opens the editor's menu (a text box: lists, a to-do, headings, links, an emoji; a topic: links, an emoji, the date), and "[[" links a note.
- Mind maps: Enter while typing a topic's name breaks the line; Tab adds a child, Ctrl+Enter a sibling below and Shift+Enter one above, each keeping the name; Esc keeps it.
- Whiteboard and mind maps: the emoji and icon library is a smiley on the tool dock (Add on a board, Map on a map), not only Insert, Emoji and icons….
- Boards & maps: a new board or mind map needs no name: Create with the name empty makes "Untitled board N" or "Untitled map N", the next free number, shown in the name field first (INBOX 739). An empty Boards & maps tab offers New board and New mind map; the board picker no longer offers an empty Default board.
- Mind maps: Effect, a topic's soft shadow or a glow in its branch colour, in the topic's Shape group and per level in How this map looks (No effect keeps one topic plain on a level that has one); kept in OPML and FreeMind exports.
- Mind maps: Spacing, in How this map looks: Compact, Normal or Roomy, the gaps between topics and between a topic and its children (16 and 46, 26 and 76, 42 and 122 pixels), laid out again at once.
- Whiteboard: a sticky note is paper (its colour, a lift and a folded corner) and a text box is words on the board (no fill, a faint dashed edge); a sticky's bar starts with seven paper colours.
- Whiteboard: dragging out a frame, sticky or text box draws a ghost of what the release makes; clone arrows follow a drag, resize and turn on all four sides; top, middle or bottom alignment for a text box's and a shape's words; the sidebar's note rows are a name over one quiet line.

- Mind maps: Rounded draws a rounded rectangle on every topic, a core one and the centre included (a core topic drew an ellipse whichever Rounded was chosen), never square under a sharp look; the picture and SVG export draw each topic's own shape.
- Mind maps: a topic put between two others keeps every branch its colour and takes its child's side and place among the branches; on a both-sides map a branch stays on its side when one grows (one added topic used to send two branches across the trunk).
- Whiteboard: the selection rectangle is no longer cut off part way across when the board grows during the drag; clone-and-connect joins fixed ports so the far end stays put.

### Fixed

- First run: the welcome, the tour, the recovery-key offer and the update question take turns, so none opens over another and the tour is no longer cut to one card; the tour card stays hidden until it is placed, a control that only shows on hover is shown for its step, and the tour's dim is lighter so the neighbours stay readable.
- With no model, a Skills or Plan button built after the last status check is greyed at once; Ask about this turns Agent on when Agent can run.
- The Guide shows the Thinking fold above its phase line, with a gap on both sides.
- No saved chats sits under the Chats heading, not at the foot of the sidebar.
- In the chat's / menu, A note, A document and the other rows that open a panel open it even when the press is held; the press no longer closes what it opened.
- A board or a mind map found by Ask or Chat is labelled Board or Mind map and opens as itself, not as a note; Sources count it as a board.
- Ask shows its searching line and "Searching your notes…" as soon as you ask, not only once the first result arrives.
- Ask's matching records show a similarity percentage on every card or on none; the reason chip keeps its words when a card is narrow, and the date ends each card's facts line at the right.
- A chat reply's head says who wrote it: Atlas, from your notes, or Atlas and the model's name; a composed answer's paragraphs rise in turn instead of appearing at once.
- Web: web pages lead the Sources list; a failed web search offers Try again; the reader's bookmark button shows when the page is kept; "give it a minute" is said only before SearXNG's first run.
- A chat question that points back at the page the last answer read (this page, more details, what else) carries that page's text, so the follow-up is answered from it.
- With no model running, Capture's tag suggestions come from your notebook's own tags instead of nothing, and the server log no longer fills with a traceback per pause.

The list is grouped by note and shows the questions without markdown, and a note that asks any says so on its card ("2 open questions"), opening only its questions.
